sentences.zh: 《記》曰：「人生而靜，天之性也；

translations.literal: The Record says: "Man is born in stillness—that is Heaven's nature;
translations.idiomatic: The Record says: "At birth people are still—that is Heaven's nature;

sentences.zh: 感物而動，性之欲也。

translations.literal: stirred by things he is moved, and that is the nature of desire.
translations.idiomatic: moved by things, desire stirs in the nature.

sentences.zh: 」欲無限極，禍亂生焉。

translations.literal: " When desire knows no bound, calamity and disorder arise.
translations.idiomatic: Unbounded desire breeds trouble and chaos.

sentences.zh: 聖人懼其邪放，於是作樂以和其性，制禮以檢其情，俾俯仰有容，周旋中矩。

translations.literal: The sages, fearing its perverse excess, thereupon composed music to harmonize the nature and fashioned ritual to restrain the feelings, so that in bowing and rising there was seemliness and in coming and going one kept to the square.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing excess, sages made music to tune the heart and ritual to check feeling, so deportment had form and conduct kept measure.

sentences.zh: 故肆覲之禮立，則朝廷尊；

translations.literal: Thus when the rite of the grand audience was established, the court was honored;
translations.idiomatic: When the grand-audience rite stood, the court gained dignity;

sentences.zh: 郊廟之禮立，則人情肅；

translations.literal: when the suburban and temple rites were established, human feeling was solemn;
translations.idiomatic: suburban and temple rites made custom solemn;

sentences.zh: 冠婚之禮立，則長幼序；

translations.literal: when the capping and wedding rites were established, elder and younger were ordered;
translations.idiomatic: capping and wedding rites fixed seniority;

sentences.zh: 喪祭之禮立，則孝慈著；

translations.literal: when the mourning and sacrifice rites were established, filial piety and kindness were displayed;
translations.idiomatic: mourning and sacrifice rites displayed filial kindness;

sentences.zh: 搜狩之禮立，則軍旅振；

translations.literal: when the hunt rites were established, the army was rallied;
translations.idiomatic: hunt rites rallied the hosts;

sentences.zh: 享宴之禮立，則君臣篤。

translations.literal: when the feast rites were established, ruler and minister were sincere.
translations.idiomatic: feast rites bound lord and minister.

sentences.zh: 是知禮者，品匯之璿衡，人倫之繩墨，失之者辱，得之者榮，造物已還，不可須臾離也。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that ritual is the jeweled balance of all categories and the measuring cord of human relations—who loses it is shamed, who gains it is honored; creation itself returns to it and one may not for an instant depart from it.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual is the scale of all kinds and the rule of human bonds; to lose it is shame, to hold it honor—not a moment may pass without it.

sentences.zh: 五帝之時，斯為治本。

translations.literal: In the time of the Five Emperors, this was the root of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Five Emperors it was the root of rule.

sentences.zh: 類帝禋宗，吉禮也；

translations.literal: Worshiping the Emperor and offering to the Ancestor were auspicious ritual;
translations.idiomatic: Worship of the Lord and Ancestor were auspicious rites;

sentences.zh: 遏音陶瓦，凶禮也；

translations.literal: suppressing music and using earthenware were inauspicious ritual;
translations.idiomatic: silencing music and pottery vessels were baleful rites;

sentences.zh: 班瑞肆覲，賓禮也；

translations.literal: presenting jade tablets at the grand audience was guest ritual;
translations.idiomatic: jade at the grand audience was guest ritual;

sentences.zh: 誅苗殛鯀，軍禮也；

translations.literal: punishing the Miao and executing Gun were military ritual;
translations.idiomatic: punishing the Miao and executing Gun were military rites;

sentences.zh: 厘降嬪虞，嘉禮也。

translations.literal: conferring rank and bestowing marriage were felicitous ritual.
translations.idiomatic: enfeoffment and marriage were celebratory rites.

sentences.zh: 故曰，修五禮五玉，堯、舜之事也。

translations.literal: Hence it is said that to perfect the five rituals and five jades was the affair of Yao and Shun.
translations.idiomatic: So perfecting the five rituals and five jades was Yao and Shun's work.

sentences.zh: 時代猶淳，節文尚簡。

translations.literal: The age was still pure and the forms and text were yet simple.
translations.idiomatic: The age was plain and ceremonies still spare.

sentences.zh: 及周公相成王，制五禮六樂，各有典司，其儀大備。

translations.literal: When the Duke of Zhou assisted King Cheng, he fashioned the five rituals and six kinds of music, each with its proper officer, and the ceremonies became fully complete.
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke of Zhou served Cheng, five rituals and six musics each had officers—the ceremonial fully formed.

sentences.zh: 暨幽、厲失道，平王東遷，周室浸微，諸侯侮法。

translations.literal: When You and Li lost the Way, King Ping moved east, the Zhou house gradually declined, and the feudal lords held the law in contempt.
translations.idiomatic: From You and Li's failure through Ping's eastern move, Zhou waned and lords scorned the law.

sentences.zh: 男女失冠婚之節，《野麕》之刺興焉；

translations.literal: Men and women lost the norms of capping and marriage; the satire of "The Wild Deer" arose;
translations.idiomatic: Loss of capping and wedding brought "The Wild Deer";

sentences.zh: 君臣廢朝會之期，踐土之譏著矣。

translations.literal: ruler and minister abandoned the schedule of audiences; the reproach of Jimu was recorded.
translations.idiomatic: broken audiences brought the shame of Jimu.

sentences.zh: 葬則奢儉無算，軍則狙詐不仁。

translations.literal: Burials knew no limit between extravagance and thrift; armies practiced deceit without humanity.
translations.idiomatic: Burials swung between waste and stinginess; armies grew crafty and cruel.

sentences.zh: 數百年間，禮儀大壞。

translations.literal: Within several hundred years the rituals were greatly ruined.
translations.idiomatic: In centuries the rites collapsed.

sentences.zh: 雖仲尼自衛返魯，而有定禮之言，蓋舉周公之舊章，無救魯邦之亂政。

translations.literal: Though when Confucius returned from Wei to Lu there was talk of fixing ritual, he merely raised the Duke of Zhou's old statutes and could not rescue Lu's chaotic government.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius's return from Wei brought talk of fixing ritual, but raising Zhou's old forms could not save chaotic Lu.

sentences.zh: 仲尼之世，體教已亡。

translations.literal: In Confucius's age the substance of teaching was already lost.
translations.idiomatic: By Confucius's time the body of teaching was gone.

sentences.zh: 遭秦燔煬，遺文殆盡。

translations.literal: Qin's burning left the transmitted texts nearly all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's fires nearly wiped the classics out.

sentences.zh: 漢興，叔孫通草定，止習朝儀。

translations.literal: When Han arose, Shusun Tong drafted on the fly, studying only court ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Han's Shusun Tong sketched rites, learning only court ceremony.

sentences.zh: 至於郊天祀地之文，配祖禋宗之制，拊石鳴球之備物，介丘璧水之盛猷，語則有之，未遑措思。

translations.literal: As for the texts of sacrificing to Heaven on the outskirts and Earth, the regulations pairing ancestors with the Ancestor, the full provision of stone clappers and sounding spheres, and the great designs of the Hillock of Jie and the Jade Water—such things were spoken of but there was no leisure to set one's mind to them.
translations.idiomatic: Suburban sacrifice to Heaven and Earth, ancestral pairing, stone chimes and sounding spheres, fengshan at Jieqiu and Jade Water—men spoke of them but had no time to plan.

sentences.zh: 及世宗禮重儒術，屢訪賢良，河間博洽古文，大搜經籍，有周舊典，始得《周官》五篇，《士禮》十七篇。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu honored Confucian learning, repeatedly sought out worthy men, the Prince of Hejian's mastery of ancient texts led to a great search of the classics, and with Zhou's old statutes he first obtained the five chapters of the Offices of Zhou and seventeen chapters of the Rites of the Scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Wu honored Ru learning and sought worthies; Hejian's mastery unearthed the Offices of Zhou (five chapters) and the Scholar's Rites (seventeen).

sentences.zh: 王又鳩集諸子之說，為禮書一百四十篇。

translations.literal: The prince also gathered the sayings of the various masters into a ritual book of one hundred forty chapters.
translations.idiomatic: The prince also assembled masters' sayings into one hundred forty chapters of ritual.

sentences.zh: 後倉二戴，因而刪擇，得四十九篇，此《曲台集禮》，今之《禮記》是也。

translations.literal: Later Cang and the two Dais selected from them and got forty-nine chapters—this was the Quetai Collected Rituals, today's Book of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Later Cang and the two Dais cut it to forty-nine—the Quetai Collected Rituals, now the Book of Rites.

sentences.zh: 然數百載不見舊儀，諸子所書，止論其意。

translations.literal: Yet for several hundred years the old ceremonies were not seen; what the masters wrote only discussed the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: For centuries old performance vanished; masters wrote meaning only.

sentences.zh: 百家縱胸臆之說，五禮無著定之文。

translations.literal: A hundred schools vented private theories; the five rituals had no fixed written form.
translations.idiomatic: Schools indulged private opinion; the five rituals lacked fixed text.

sentences.zh: 故西漢一朝，曲台無制。

translations.literal: Therefore throughout the Western Han at Quetai there was no system.
translations.idiomatic: Western Han had Quetai text but no enforced system.

sentences.zh: 郊上帝於甘泉，祀後土于汾陰。

translations.literal: The suburban Lord was sacrificed to at Sweet Springs; the Queen of Earth at Fenyin.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven at Sweet Springs, Earth at Fenyin.

sentences.zh: 宗廟無定主，樂懸缺金石。

translations.literal: The ancestral temple had no fixed focus; music lacked metal and stone.
translations.idiomatic: The temple had no fixed lord; music lacked bells and stones.

sentences.zh: 巡狩非勳、華之典，封禪異陶匏之音。

translations.literal: Tours of inspection were not the canon of Kun and Hua; fengshan differed from pottery and gourd sound.
translations.idiomatic: Inspection tours were not Kun-Hua canon; fengshan diverged from rustic simplicity.

sentences.zh: 光武受命，始詔儒官草定儀注，經邦大典，至是粗備。

translations.literal: When Guangwu received the mandate, he first ordered ritual officials to draft ceremony and statute; the great statutes of the state were then roughly complete.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu ordered scholars to draft rites—the state's great canon was roughly set.

sentences.zh: 漢末喪亂，又淪沒焉。

translations.literal: At the end of Han turmoil fell upon them again.
translations.idiomatic: Han's end plunged them back into ruin.

sentences.zh: 而衛宏、應仲遠、王仲宣等掇拾遺散，裁志條目而已。

translations.literal: Wei Hong, Ying Zhongyuan, Wang Zhongxuan, and others picked up what survived and trimmed it to headings only.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Hong, Ying Zhongyuan, and Wang Zhongxuan salvaged fragments into bare outlines.

sentences.zh: 東京舊典，世莫得聞。

translations.literal: The old statutes of the Eastern Capital—no one in the world could hear of them.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Capital's old rites were unheard in the world.

sentences.zh: 自晉至梁，繼令條纘。

translations.literal: From Jin through Liang orders and statutes followed one another.
translations.idiomatic: Jin through Liang issued continuing regulations.

sentences.zh: 鴻生钜儒，銳思綿蕝，江左學者，仿佛可觀。

translations.literal: Erudite scholars thought deep and far; scholars of the Jiang left could dimly behold them.
translations.idiomatic: Great scholars wove long formulations; Jiangzuo students could glimpse them.

sentences.zh: 隋氏平陳，寰區一統，文帝命太常卿牛弘集南北儀注，定《五禮》一百三十篇。

translations.literal: When the Sui pacified Chen and unified the realm, Wen Di ordered the Director of Ritual Niu Hong to collect northern and southern ceremony into the Five Rituals in one hundred thirty chapters.
translations.idiomatic: Sui's unification had Wen Di order Niu Hong to compile north-south ritual into one hundred thirty chapters.

sentences.zh: 煬帝在廣陵，亦聚學徒，修《江都集禮》。

translations.literal: Yang Di at Guangling also gathered students and compiled the Jiangdu Collected Rituals.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Di at Guangling gathered students for the Jiangdu Collected Rituals.

sentences.zh: 由是周、漢之制，僅有遺風。

translations.literal: Thus the systems of Zhou and Han survived only as a remnant breeze.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou and Han institutions survived only as a faint tradition.

sentences.zh: 神堯受禪，未遑製作，郊廟宴享，悉用隋代舊儀。

translations.literal: When Shenyao received the abdication, he had no leisure to create; suburban altars and feasts all used Sui's old ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Shenyao's succession used Sui rites for suburbs and banquets—no new work yet.

sentences.zh: 太宗皇帝踐祚之初，悉興文教，乃詔中書令房玄齡、秘書監魏征等禮官學士，修改舊禮，定著《吉禮》六十一篇，《賓禮》四篇，《《軍禮》二十篇，《嘉禮》四十二篇，《凶禮》六篇，《國恤》五篇，總一百三十八篇，分為一百卷。

translations.literal: When Taizong first took the throne he greatly revived culture and letters and ordered Chancellor Fang Xuanling, Secretariat Director Wei Zheng, and other ritual officials and academicians to revise the old rituals and fix the Auspicious Rituals in sixty-one chapters, Guest Ritual in four, Military Ritual in twenty, Felicitous Ritual in forty-two, Baleful Ritual in six, and National Mourning in five—a total of one hundred thirty-eight chapters in one hundred scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong revived letters and had Fang Xuanling, Wei Zheng, and ritual scholars revise rites: Auspicious sixty-one, Guest four, Military twenty, Felicitous forty-two, Baleful six, National Mourning five—one hundred thirty-eight chapters in one hundred juan.

sentences.zh: 玄齡等始與禮官述議，以為《月令》䄍祭，唯祭天宗，謂日月而下。

translations.literal: Xuanling and others first deliberated with ritual officers, holding that in the Monthly Ordinances the seasonal sacrifice is only to the Heavenly Clan, meaning sun and moon and below.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanling argued the Monthly Ordinances' seasonal sacrifice reaches only the Heavenly Clan—sun, moon, and below.

sentences.zh: 近代䄍五天帝、五人帝、五地祇，皆非古典，今並除之。

translations.literal: In recent times sacrificing to the Five Heavenly Emperors, Five Human Emperors, and Five Earth Spirits on the seasonal day were none of them classical antiquity; they are all now abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Recent worship of Five Heavens, Five Humans, and Five Earths on the jiao day—all abolished as unclassical.

sentences.zh: 又依禮，有益於人則祀之。

translations.literal: Again by ritual what benefits the people is sacrificed to.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual says: benefit the people, then sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 神州者國之所托，餘八州則義不相及。

translations.literal: The Spirit Land is what the state rests upon; the other eight provinces are not connected in meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit Land supports the realm; the eight regions are not analogous.

sentences.zh: 近代通祭九州，今除八州等八座，唯祭皇地祇及神州，以正祀典。

translations.literal: In recent times all nine provinces were commonly sacrificed to; now the eight altar-seats of the eight provinces are removed, and only the Imperial Earth Spirit and Spirit Land are sacrificed to, to rectify the sacrificial canon.
translations.idiomatic: Nine-province worship was cut to Earth Spirit and Spirit Land only.

sentences.zh: 又漢建武中封禪，用元封時故事，封泰山於圓臺上，四面皆立石闕，並高五丈。

translations.literal: Again in Jianwu of Han at fengshan they used Yuanfeng precedents, sealing Mount Tai on a round terrace with stone gate towers on all four sides, each five zhang high.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu fengshan followed Yuanfeng: round terrace on Tai with four stone gates five zhang high.

sentences.zh: 有方石再累，藏玉牒書。

translations.literal: There was a square stone piled in layers, concealing a jade text.
translations.idiomatic: Layered square stones hid a jade document.

sentences.zh: 石檢十枚，於四邊檢之，東西各三，南北各二。

translations.literal: Ten stone caskets at the four sides—three east and west, two north and south.
translations.idiomatic: Ten stone checks: three east and west, two north and south.

sentences.zh: 外設石封，高九尺，上加石蓋。

translations.literal: Outside were stone seals nine chi high with stone caps on top.
translations.idiomatic: Outer stone seals nine chi high, capped in stone.

sentences.zh: 周設石距十八，如碑之狀，去壇二步，其下石跗入地數尺。

translations.literal: Eighteen stone distances were set around like steles, two bu from the altar, their stone bases sunk several chi into the earth.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteen stone distances like steles two bu from the mound, bases sunk deep.

sentences.zh: 今案封禪者，本以成功告於上帝。

translations.literal: Now investigating fengshan: it was fundamentally to report success to the Lord on High.
translations.idiomatic: Fengshan was to report success to the Lord on High.

sentences.zh: 天道貴質，故藉用槁秸，樽以瓦甒。

translations.literal: The Way of Heaven esteems substance; hence straw mats and pottery vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's Way favors simplicity—straw and pottery.

sentences.zh: 此法不在經誥，又乖醇素之道，定議除之。

translations.literal: This method is not in the classics and also violates the path of pure simplicity; it was decided to abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: Not in canon, against simplicity—abolished.

sentences.zh: 近又案梁甫是梁陰，代設壇於山上，乃乖處陰之義。

translations.literal: Recently it was considered that Liangfu is the yin of Liang; generations set the altar on the mountain top, contrary to dwelling in yin.
translations.idiomatic: Liangfu is Liang's yin; mountain-top altars violated yin.

sentences.zh: 今定禪禮改壇位於山北。

translations.literal: Now the shan rite's altar position is fixed north of the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Shan altar placed north of the mountain.

sentences.zh: 又皇太子入學及太常行山陵、天子大射、合朔、陳五兵於太社、農隙講武、納皇后行六禮、四孟月讀時令、天子上陵、朝廟、養老於辟雍之禮，皆周、隋所闕，凡增多二十九條。

translations.literal: Also the crown prince entering study, the Director of Ritual going for imperial tombs, the Son of Heaven's great archery, heji, displaying the five weapons at the Grand Shrine, lecturing military matters in agricultural intervals, receiving the empress through the six rites, reading the seasons in the four meng months, the Son of Heaven's tomb visits, temple audiences, and nourishing the aged in the Piyong—rites omitted by Zhou and Sui; in all twenty-nine articles were added.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-nine rites Zhou and Sui lacked were added: heir's schooling, tomb rites, archery, heji, five arms at Grand Shrine, war lectures, empress's six rites, seasonal readings, tomb visits, audiences, aged at Piyong.

sentences.zh: 余並准依古禮，旁求異代，擇其善者而從之。

translations.literal: The rest according to ancient ritual, seeking out other ages beside, choosing the good and following it.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise follow ancient rites, borrow best from other ages.

sentences.zh: 太宗稱善，頒於內外行焉。

translations.literal: Taizong praised it and issued it for implementation inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong approved and promulgated it.

sentences.zh: 高宗初，議者以《貞觀禮》節文未盡，又詔太尉長孫無忌、中書令杜正倫李義府、中書侍郎李友益、黃門侍郎劉祥道許圉師、太子賓客許敬宗、太常少卿韋琨、太學博士史道玄、符璽郎孔志約、太常博士蕭，楚才孫自覺賀紀等重加緝定，勒成一百三十卷。

translations.literal: Early in Gaozong's reign critics said the Zhenguan Ritual's forms were not exhaustive; again ordered Grand Mentor Zhangsun Wuji, Chancellor Du Zhenglun, Li Yifu, Secretariat Vice Director Li Youyi, Yellow Gate Vice Liu Xiangdao, Xu Tushi, Chief Banquet Officer Xu Jingzong, Director of Ritual Wei Kun, Erudite Shi Daoxuan, Seal Director Kong Zhiyue, Ritual Erudite Xiao Chucai, Sun Zijue, He Ji, and others to compile anew into one hundred thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong had Wuji, Li Yifu, Xu Jingzong, and others revise into one hundred thirty juan.

sentences.zh: 至顯慶三年奏上之，增損舊禮，並與令式參會改定，高宗自為之序。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianqing it was submitted; augmenting and reducing old ritual and aligning with statutes and forms, Gaozong himself wrote the preface.
translations.idiomatic: Xianqing 3 it was presented with Gaozong's preface.

sentences.zh: 時許敬宗、李義府用事，其所損益，多涉希旨，行用已後，學者紛議，以為不及貞觀。

translations.literal: Xu Jingzong and Li Yifu then held power; their augmentations mostly pandered to will; after implementation scholars disputed that it did not equal Zhenguan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu and Li's changes often flattered the throne; scholars judged it below Zhenguan.

sentences.zh: 上元三年三月，下詔令依貞觀年禮為定。

translations.literal: Third month, third year of Shangyuan, an edict ordered the Zhenguan-era ritual taken as fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Shangyuan 3.3 returned to Zhenguan ritual.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳二年，又詔顯慶新修禮多有事不師古，其五禮並依周禮行事。

translations.literal: Second year of Yifeng, again an edict that Xianqing's new ritual often failed to follow antiquity and the five rituals were all to follow the Rites of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yifeng 2 ordered five rituals to follow Zhou ritual—Xianqing faulted for ignoring antiquity.

sentences.zh: 自是禮司益無憑准，每有大事，皆參會古今禮文，臨時撰定。

translations.literal: From this the ritual office increasingly lacked a fixed standard; for each great affair they compared ancient and modern ritual texts and drafted provisionally.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers had no fixed standard—major events improvised from old and new.

sentences.zh: 然貞觀、顯慶二《禮》，皆行用不廢。

translations.literal: Yet both Zhenguan and Xianqing Rituals continued in use without abolition.
translations.idiomatic: Both Zhenguan and Xianqing rituals stayed in use.

sentences.zh: 時有太常卿裴明禮、太常少卿韋萬石相次參掌其事，又前後博士賀敱、賀紀、韋叔夏、裴守真等多所議定。

translations.literal: At the time Director of Ritual Pei Mingli and Vice Director Wei Wanshi in succession managed affairs; erudites He Ai, He Ji, Wei Shuxia, Pei Shouzhen, and others decided much.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Mingli, Wei Wanshi, and erudites He Ai, He Ji, Wei Shuxia, and Pei Shouzhen decided much.

sentences.zh: 則天時，以禮官不甚詳明，特詔國子博士祝欽明及叔夏，每有儀注，皆令參定。

translations.literal: In Wu Zetian's time, ritual officers being insufficiently clear, she specially ordered Erudite Zhu Qinming and Shuxia—whenever there was ceremony they were to join in fixing it.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian ordered Zhu Qinming and Shuxia to fix every ceremony.

sentences.zh: 叔夏卒後，博士唐紹專知禮儀，博學詳練舊事，議者以為稱職。

translations.literal: After Shuxia's death Erudite Tang Shao specialized in ritual, learned and skilled in old affairs; critics deemed him fit for the post.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Shao took ritual after Shuxia—judged competent.

sentences.zh: 先天二年，紹為給事中，以講武失儀，得罪被誅。

translations.literal: Second year of Xiantian, Shao as Palace Attendant was executed for impropriety at martial exposition.
translations.idiomatic: Xiantian 2 Shao was executed for a drill lapse.

sentences.zh: 其後禮官張星、王琇又以元日儀注乖失，詔免官歸家學問。

translations.literal: Later ritual officers Zhang Xing and Wang Xiu erred on New Year's ceremony and were ordered dismissed to study at home.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xing and Wang Xiu lost New Year's rites and were sent home to study.

sentences.zh: ，詔國子司業韋絛為禮儀使，專掌五禮。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Guozi Vice Director Wei Chao as Ritual Commissioner exclusively in charge of the five rituals.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chao was made Ritual Commissioner for the five rituals.

sentences.zh: 十四年，通事舍人王嵒上疏，請改撰《禮記》，削去舊文，而以今事編之。

translations.literal: Fourteenth year, Reminder Wang Yan memorialized to revise the Book of Rites, cutting old text and compiling present affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan 14 Wang Yan asked to rewrite the Book of Rites from current practice.

sentences.zh: 詔付集賢院學士詳議。

translations.literal: The edict was sent to the Academicians for detailed discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Edict referred it to the Academy.

sentences.zh: 右丞相張說奏曰：「《禮記》漢朝所編，遂為歷代不刊之典。

translations.literal: Right Chancellor Zhang Yue memorialized: "The Book of Rites was compiled in Han and has become an unalterable canon for successive generations.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue said the Book of Rites is Han's unalterable canon.

sentences.zh: 今去聖久遠，恐難改易。

translations.literal: Now we are far from the sages and revision may be difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Saints are distant—hard to change.

sentences.zh: 今之五禮儀注，貞觀、顯慶兩度所修，前後頗有不同，其中或未折衷。

translations.literal: Today's five ritual statutes of Zhenguan and Xianqing differ in places and may not be reconciled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguan and Xianqing rites differ—may need reconciliation.

sentences.zh: 望與學士等更討論古今，刪改行用。

translations.literal: I hope together with scholars to discuss antiquity and the present again and revise what is in use."
translations.idiomatic: Hope to compare antiquity and present and revise what is used.

sentences.zh: 」制從之。

translations.literal: The Imperial decision granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict assented.

sentences.zh: 初令學士右散騎常侍徐堅及左拾遺李銳、太常博士施敬本等檢撰，歷年不就。

translations.literal: At first ordered Academician Right Regular Xu Jian, Reminder Li Rui, Ritual Erudite Shi Jingben, and others to compile; year after year without completion.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jian, Li Rui, and Shi Jingben drafted for years unfinished.

sentences.zh: 說卒後，蕭嵩代為集賢院學士，始奏起居舍人王仲丘撰成一百五十卷，名曰《大唐開元禮》。

translations.literal: After Yue's death Xiao Song replaced him as Academy Chancellor and had Recorder Wang Zhongqiu complete one hundred fifty scrolls titled Great Tang Kaiyuan Ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Song had Wang Zhongqiu finish one hundred fifty juan as Kaiyuan Ritual.

sentences.zh: 二十年九月，頒所司行用焉。

translations.literal: Ninth month, twentieth year, issued for the offices to implement.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan 20.9 promulgated for use.

sentences.zh: 昊天上帝、五方帝、皇地祇、神州及宗廟為大祀，社稷、日月星辰、先代帝王、嶽鎮海瀆、帝社、先蠶、釋奠為中祀，司中、司命、風伯、雨師、諸星、山林川澤之屬為小祀。

translations.literal: August Lord, Five Directional Emperors, Imperial Earth Spirit, Spirit Land, and ancestral temple are great sacrifice; altars of soil and grain, sun moon stars, former dynasties' emperors, peaks rivers seas, imperial soil altar, Silkworm Ancestor, libation for release are middle sacrifice; Director of Central, Director of Fate, Wind Earl, Rain Master, various stars, mountains forests rivers marshes are small sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Great sacrifice: August Lord, Five Emperors, Earth, Spirit Land, temple; middle: soil and grain, sun moon and stars, former kings, peaks and rivers, etc.; small: various spirits.

sentences.zh: 大祀，所司每年預定日奏下。

translations.literal: Great sacrifice—the office each year sets the day in advance and submits it.
translations.idiomatic: Great sacrifices get annual dated submission.

sentences.zh: 小祀，但移牒所由。

translations.literal: Small sacrifice—only a dispatch to the responsible office.
translations.idiomatic: Small sacrifices get a memorandum only.

sentences.zh: 若天子不親祭享，則三公行事；

translations.literal: If the Son of Heaven does not personally sacrifice, then the Three Excellencies perform the rite;
translations.idiomatic: If the emperor does not attend, Three Excellencies perform;

sentences.zh: 若官缺，則職事三品已上攝三公行事。

translations.literal: if the office is vacant, then active-duty officials of third rank and above act for the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Vacant posts: third-rank and above officers deputize.

sentences.zh: 大祀散齋四日，致齋三日。

translations.literal: Great sacrifice: dispersal fast four days, full fast three days.
translations.idiomatic: Great: four dispersal, three full fast.

sentences.zh: 中祀散齋三日，致齋二日。

translations.literal: Middle sacrifice: dispersal fast three days, full fast two days.
translations.idiomatic: Middle: three dispersal, two full.

sentences.zh: 小祀散齋二日，致齋一日。

translations.literal: Small sacrifice: dispersal fast two days, full fast one day.
translations.idiomatic: Small: two dispersal, one full.

sentences.zh: 散齋之日，晝理事如舊，夜宿於家正寢，不得弔喪問疾，不判署刑殺文書，不決罰罪人，不作樂，不預穢惡之事。

translations.literal: On dispersal-fast days one handles affairs by day as before, lodges at night in the home's main chamber, may not mourn or visit the sick, may not sign documents of punishment and execution, may not pass sentence on criminals, may not make music, may not attend unclean affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Dispersal fast: daytime business as usual, sleep in main chamber; no mourning, sick visits, capital sentences, music, or polluting work.

sentences.zh: 致齋惟為祀事得行，其餘悉斷。

translations.literal: On full-fast days only matters of sacrifice may proceed; all else is cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Full fast: only cult business; everything else stops.

sentences.zh: 若大祀，齋官皆於散齋之日，集於尚書省受誓戒，太尉讀誓文。

translations.literal: For great sacrifice, on dispersal-fast days all fast officers assemble at the Department of State Affairs to receive the oath; the Grand Mentor reads the oath text.
translations.idiomatic: Great sacrifice: fast officers gather at the Secretariat on dispersal day for the oath, read by the Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 致齋之日，三公於尚書省安置；

translations.literal: On full-fast days the Three Excellencies are lodged at the Department of State Affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Full fast: Three Excellencies stay at the Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 余官各于本司，若皇城內無本司，于太常郊社、太廟署安置。

translations.literal: other officers each at his own office; if there is no office within the Imperial City, at the Director of Ritual's suburban-altar or ancestral-temple sections.
translations.idiomatic: others at their bureaus, or at Ritual's suburban or temple offices inside the city.

sentences.zh: 皆日未出前至齋所。

translations.literal: All arrive at the fast lodge before the sun has risen.
translations.idiomatic: All reach the fast lodge before dawn.

sentences.zh: 至祀前一日，各從齋所晝漏上水五刻向祠所。

translations.literal: On the day before sacrifice each leaves the fast lodge at the fifth mark after the day clepsydra has been set and proceeds toward the shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Eve of sacrifice: leave fast lodge at day clepsydra mark five and go to the shrine.

sentences.zh: 接神之官，皆沐浴給明衣。

translations.literal: Officers receiving the spirit all bathe and are given bright garments.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit-receiving officers bathe and receive bright robes.

sentences.zh: 若天子親祠，則於正殿行致齋之禮。

translations.literal: If the Son of Heaven personally sacrifices, he performs the full-fast rite in the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: If the emperor sacrifices in person, full fast is in the main hall.

sentences.zh: 文武官服褲褶，陪位於殿庭。

translations.literal: Civil and military officers wear trousers and jackets and attend in the court yard.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officers wear military dress in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 車駕及齋官赴祠祭之所，州縣及金吾清所行之路，不得見諸凶穢及縗絰者，哭泣之聲聞於祭所者權斷，訖事依舊。

translations.literal: Where the imperial carriage and fast officers travel to the sacrifice, along prefectures and counties and where the Golden Crow clears the road, one must not see anything inauspicious or mourners in hemp; if sounds of weeping reach the sacrifice place they are provisionally stopped, and after the affair ends things return as before.
translations.idiomatic: Processional routes were cleared of mourning and pollution; weeping near the shrine was silenced until rites ended.

sentences.zh: 齋官至祠所，太官惟設食。

translations.literal: When fast officers reach the shrine, the Imperial Kitchen sets out food only.
translations.idiomatic: At the shrine the Imperial Kitchen served food only.

sentences.zh: 祭訖，依班序餕，訖，均胙，貴者不重，賤者不虛。

translations.literal: After sacrifice, according to rank order they partake of the offering; when finished, the sacrificial flesh is equally divided—the noble are not given double, the lowly are not left empty.
translations.idiomatic: After rites, ranked feasting; sacrificial meat shared—nobles not doubled, commoners not cheated.

sentences.zh: 中祀已下，惟不受誓戒，自餘皆同大祀之禮。

translations.literal: Middle sacrifice and below only do not receive the oath; otherwise all is the same as great sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Below middle sacrifice: no oath; otherwise as great sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 武德初，定令：

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude, the statute was fixed:
translations.idiomatic: Wude era statute:

sentences.zh: 每歲冬至，祀昊天上帝於圓丘，以景帝配。

translations.literal: Each year at the winter solstice sacrifice to August Lord at the Round Mound, with Emperor Jing as associate.
translations.idiomatic: Winter solstice: August Lord at Round Mound, Jing as associate.

sentences.zh: 其壇在京城明德門外道東二里。

translations.literal: The altar is two li east of the road outside Bright Virtue Gate in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Altar two li east of Bright Virtue Gate road.

sentences.zh: 壇制四成，各高八尺一寸，下成廣二十丈，再成廣十五丈，三成廣十丈，四成廣五丈。

translations.literal: The altar has four tiers, each eight chi one cun high; the lowest tier twenty zhang wide, the second fifteen, the third ten, the fourth five.
translations.idiomatic: Four tiers eight chi one cun each: bottom twenty zhang, then fifteen, ten, five.

sentences.zh: 每祀則天上帝及配帝設位於平座，藉用槁秸，器用陶匏。

translations.literal: At each sacrifice August Lord and the associate are set on the level terrace; straw mats are used, vessels pottery.
translations.idiomatic: Each rite: Lord and associate on level terrace, straw mats, pottery vessels.

sentences.zh: 五方上帝、日月、內官、中官、外官及眾星，並皆從祀。

translations.literal: Five Directional Emperors, sun and moon, inner officials, central officials, outer officials, and all stars are jointly sacrificed.
translations.idiomatic: Five Emperors, sun, moon, inner, central, outer officials, and stars all joined.

sentences.zh: 其五方帝及日月七座，在壇之第二等；

translations.literal: The Five Directional Emperors and the seven of sun and moon are on the altar's second tier;
translations.idiomatic: Five Emperors and seven sun-moon seats on tier two;

sentences.zh: 內五星已下官五十五座，在壇之第三等；

translations.literal: the fifty-five seats of inner five stars and below on the third tier;
translations.idiomatic: fifty-five inner star seats on tier three;

sentences.zh: 二十八宿已下中官一百三十五座，在壇之第四等；

translations.literal: the one hundred thirty-five seats of twenty-eight lodges and below central officials on the fourth tier;
translations.idiomatic: one hundred thirty-five central seats on tier four;

sentences.zh: 外官百十二座，在壇下外壝之內；

translations.literal: one hundred twelve outer-official seats inside the outer enclosure below the altar;
translations.idiomatic: one hundred twelve outer seats inside the outer mound;

sentences.zh: 眾星三百六十座，在外壝之外。

translations.literal: three hundred sixty seats of all stars outside the outer enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: three hundred sixty common stars outside the mound.

sentences.zh: 其牲，上帝及配帝用蒼犢二，五方帝及日月用方色犢各一，內官已下加羊豕各九。

translations.literal: Victims: for the Lord and associate two dark bullocks; for Five Emperors and sun and moon one bullock each in the direction's color; for inner officials and below add nine sheep and nine pigs each.
translations.idiomatic: Victims: Lord and associate two dark bulls; Five Emperors and sun-moon one colored bull each; inner and below plus nine sheep and nine pigs.

sentences.zh: 夏至，祭皇地祗于方丘，亦以景帝配。

translations.literal: At the summer solstice sacrifice to Imperial Earth Spirit at the Square Mound, also with Emperor Jing as associate.
translations.idiomatic: Summer solstice: Earth Spirit at Square Mound, Jing associate.

sentences.zh: 其壇在宮城之北十四里。

translations.literal: The altar is fourteen li north of the palace city.
translations.idiomatic: Altar fourteen li north of the palace.

sentences.zh: 壇制再成，下成方十丈，上成五丈。

translations.literal: The altar has two tiers; the lower square ten zhang, the upper five.
translations.idiomatic: Two tiers: lower ten zhang square, upper five.

sentences.zh: 每祀則地祇及配帝設位於壇上，神州及五嶽、四鎮、四瀆、四海、五方、山林、川澤、丘陵、墳衍、原隰，並皆從祀。

translations.literal: At each sacrifice Earth Spirit and associate on the altar; Spirit Land, Five Peaks, Four Guardians, Four Streams, Four Seas, Five Directions, mountains forests rivers marshes, hills mounds plains and lowlands—all jointly sacrificed.
translations.idiomatic: Earth and associate on mound; Spirit Land, peaks, guardians, streams, seas, directions, landforms—all joined.

sentences.zh: 神州在壇之第二等。

translations.literal: Spirit Land is on the altar's second tier.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit Land on tier two.

sentences.zh: 五嶽已下三十七座，在壇下外壝之內。

translations.literal: Thirty-seven seats from Five Peaks and below inside the outer enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-seven peak-and-below seats inside outer mound.

sentences.zh: 丘陵等三十座，在壝外。

translations.literal: Thirty seats of hills and mounds and the like outside the enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty landform seats outside the mound.

sentences.zh: 其牲，地祗及配帝用犢二，神州用黝犢一，嶽鎮已下加羊豕各五。

translations.literal: Victims: Earth Spirit and associate two bullocks; Spirit Land one dark bull; peaks and below add five sheep and five pigs each.
translations.idiomatic: Victims: Earth and associate two bulls; Spirit Land one dark bull; peaks and below five sheep and five pigs.

sentences.zh: 孟春辛日，祈穀，祀感帝於南郊，元帝配，牲用蒼犢二。

translations.literal: First month xin day: pray for grain, sacrifice to the Impulse Emperor at the southern suburb, Emperor Yuan as associate, victims two dark bullocks.
translations.idiomatic: First month xin: grain prayer at southern suburb to Impulse Emperor, Yuan associate, two dark bulls.

sentences.zh: 孟夏之月，雩祀昊天上帝於圓丘，景帝配，牲用蒼犢二。

translations.literal: Fourth month: rain sacrifice to August Lord at Round Mound, Jing associate, victims two dark bullocks.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth month: rain rite at Round Mound, Jing associate, two dark bulls.

sentences.zh: 五方上帝、五人帝、五官並從祀，用方色犢十。

translations.literal: Five Directional Emperors, Five Human Emperors, and Five Officials all jointly sacrificed; ten bullocks in direction colors.
translations.idiomatic: Five Emperors, Five Humans, Five Officials joined; ten colored bulls.

sentences.zh: 季秋，祀五方上帝於明堂，元帝配，牲用蒼犢二。

translations.literal: Last month of autumn: sacrifice to Five Directional Emperors at Bright Hall, Yuan associate, victims two dark bullocks.
translations.idiomatic: Late autumn: Five Emperors at Bright Hall, Yuan associate, two dark bulls.

sentences.zh: 五人帝、五官並從祀，用方色犢十。

translations.literal: Five Human Emperors and Five Officials jointly sacrificed; ten bullocks in direction colors.
translations.idiomatic: Five Humans and Five Officials joined; ten colored bulls.

sentences.zh: 孟冬，祭神州於北郊，景帝配，牲用黝犢二。

translations.literal: First month of winter: sacrifice to Spirit Land at northern suburb, Jing associate, victims two dark bullocks.
translations.idiomatic: Early winter: Spirit Land at northern suburb, Jing associate, two dark bulls.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，詔奉高祖配圓丘及明堂北郊之祀，元帝專配感帝，自余悉依武德。

translations.literal: Early Zhenguan, an edict made Gaozu associate at Round Mound and Bright Hall northern suburb; Emperor Yuan alone associated at Impulse Emperor; the rest all followed Wude.
translations.idiomatic: Early Zhenguan: Gaozu paired at Round Mound and Bright Hall north suburb; Yuan alone at Impulse Emperor; rest per Wude.

sentences.zh: 永徽二年，又奉太宗配祀於明堂，有司遂以高祖配五天帝，太宗配五人帝。

translations.literal: Second year of Yonghui, again Taizong was made associate at Bright Hall sacrifice; the office then made Gaozu associate with the Five Heavenly Emperors and Taizong with the Five Human Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Yonghui 2: Taizong paired at Bright Hall; office made Gaozu pair Five Heavens and Taizong Five Humans.

sentences.zh: 顯慶元年，太尉長孫無忌與禮官等奏議曰：

translations.literal: First year of Xianqing, Grand Mentor Zhangsun Wuji and ritual officers memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: Xianqing 1: Wuji and ritual officers memorialized:

sentences.zh: 臣等謹尋方冊，曆考前規，宗祀明堂，必配天帝，而伏羲五代，本配五郊，預入有堂，自緣從祀。

translations.literal: We have carefully traced the registers and examined former regulations: ancestral sacrifice at Bright Hall must pair the Heavenly Emperor; Fuxi and the five generations originally paired at the five suburbs and entered the hall only as joint sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Registers show Bright Hall must pair the Heavenly Emperor; Fuxi's five generations paired at five suburbs and entered the hall only as attendants.

sentences.zh: 今乙太宗作配，理有示安。

translations.literal: Now to make Taizong the associate has reason in showing repose.
translations.idiomatic: Making Taizong the associate shows proper repose.

sentences.zh: 伏見永徽二年七月，詔建明堂，伏惟陛下天縱聖德，追奉太宗，已遵嚴配。

translations.literal: We observe that in the seventh month of Yonghui 2 an edict built Bright Hall; Your Majesty's sage virtue pursues Taizong and already follows strict pairing.
translations.idiomatic: Yonghui 2.7 built Bright Hall; Your Majesty already honors strict pairing for Taizong.

sentences.zh: 時高祖先在明堂，禮司致惑，竟未遷祀，率意定儀，遂便著令。

translations.literal: At the time Gaozu was already in Bright Hall; the ritual office was confused and never moved the sacrifice, following inclination to fix the ceremony and then putting it in statute.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was already in Bright Hall; ritual officers never moved him, improvised, and codified it.

sentences.zh: 乃乙太宗皇帝降配五人帝，雖復亦在明堂，不得對越天帝，深乖明詔之意，又與先典不同。

translations.literal: Thus Taizong was demoted to pair with the Five Human Emperors; though also in Bright Hall he could not face the Heavenly Emperor—deeply contrary to the edict's intent and also unlike former canon.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was demoted to Five Humans—still in Bright Hall but not facing Heaven, against edict and canon.

sentences.zh: 謹案《孝經》云：「孝莫大于嚴父，嚴父莫大于配天。

translations.literal: We examine the Classic of Filial Piety: "Of filial piety none is greater than honoring the father; of honoring the father none is greater than pairing with Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Filial Piety says: "No filial piety exceeds honoring the father; no honoring the father exceeds pairing with Heaven.

sentences.zh: 昔者周公宗祀文王於明堂，以配上帝。

translations.literal: In antiquity the Duke of Zhou ancestrally sacrificed to King Wen at Bright Hall to pair with the Lord on High.
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity: the Duke of Zhou sacrificed to Wen at Bright Hall to pair with the Lord on High.

sentences.zh: 伏惟詔意，義在於斯。

translations.literal: We observe the edict's meaning lies in this.
translations.idiomatic: The edict's meaning lies here.

sentences.zh: 今所司行令殊為失旨。

translations.literal: What the office now implements in statute is greatly contrary to the intent.
translations.idiomatic: Current statute greatly misses the intent.

sentences.zh: 又尋漢、魏、晉、宋歷代禮儀，並無父子同配明堂之義。

translations.literal: Again tracing Han, Wei, Jin, and Song ritual through the ages, none has father and son jointly paired at Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Han through Song show no father-son joint pairing at Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 唯《祭法》云：「周人禘嚳而郊稷，祖文王而宗武王。

translations.literal: Only the Canon of Sacrifices says: "The Zhou people di to Ku and jiao to Ji, zu to Wen and zong to Wu."
translations.idiomatic: Only the Canon of Sacrifices says: "Zhou di to Ku, jiao to Ji, zu to Wen, zong to Wu."

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄注云：「禘、郊、祖、宗，謂祭祀以配食也。

translations.literal: " Zheng Xuan's commentary says: "Di, jiao, zu, and zong mean sacrifice with paired offerings."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan comments: "Di, jiao, zu, and zong mean sacrifice with paired food."

sentences.zh: 禘謂祭昊天於圓丘，郊謂祭上帝于南郊，祖、宗謂祭五帝、五神於明堂也。

translations.literal: Di means sacrificing to August Lord at the Round Mound; jiao means sacrificing to the Lord at the southern suburb; zu and zong mean sacrificing to the Five Emperors and Five Spirits at Bright Hall."
translations.idiomatic: Di is August Lord at Round Mound; jiao is the Lord at southern suburb; zu and zong are Five Emperors and Five Spirits at Bright Hall."

sentences.zh: 」尋鄭此注，乃以祖、宗合為一祭，又以文、武共在明堂，連衽配祀，良為謬矣。

translations.literal: " Pursuing this commentary of Zheng, he takes zu and zong as one sacrifice and also Wen and Wu together at Bright Hall, joining mats in paired sacrifice—a clear error.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing Zheng's note, he merges zu and zong and pairs Wen and Wu at Bright Hall on shared mats—a clear error.

sentences.zh: 故王肅駁曰：「古者祖有功而宗有德，祖、宗自是不毀之名，非謂配食於明堂者也。

translations.literal: Thus Wang Su rebutted: "In antiquity zu honored merit and zong honored virtue—zu and zong are names that are not destroyed, not meaning paired food at Bright Hall."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su rebutted: "Antiquity's zu and zong were undying honorific titles, not Bright Hall paired food."

sentences.zh: 審如鄭義，則《孝經》當言祖祀文王於明堂，不得言宗祀也。

translations.literal: If Zheng's meaning holds, the Classic of Filial Piety should say zu sacrifice to Wen at Bright Hall and could not say zong sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: If Zheng were right, Filial Piety would say zu at Bright Hall, not zong.

sentences.zh: 凡宗者，尊也。

translations.literal: As for zong, it means honor.
translations.idiomatic: Zong means honor.

sentences.zh: 周人既祖其廟，又尊其祀，孰謂祖於明堂者乎？

translations.literal: The Zhou already zu their temple and again honored their sacrifice—who says zu at Bright Hall?
translations.idiomatic: Zhou already had temple zu and honored sacrifice—who says Bright Hall zu?

sentences.zh: 」鄭引《孝經》以解《祭法》，而不曉周公本意，殊非仲尼之義旨也。

translations.literal: " Zheng cited the Classic of Filial Piety to explain the Canon of Sacrifices but did not understand the Duke of Zhou's original intent—utterly not Confucius's meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng used Filial Piety to explain the Canon but missed the Duke of Zhou—far from Confucius.

sentences.zh: 又解「宗武王」云：「配勾芒之類，是謂五神，位在堂下。

translations.literal: Again explaining "zong Wu" he said: "Pairing with Gou Mang and the like—called the Five Spirits, rank below the hall."
translations.idiomatic: On "zong Wu" he said pairing Gou Mang and the like—Five Spirits below the hall.

sentences.zh: 」武王降位，失君敘矣。

translations.literal: " Wu demoted in rank violates lord-order.
translations.idiomatic: Demoting Wu breaks lord-order.

sentences.zh: 又案《六韜》曰：「武王伐紂，雪深丈余，五車二馬，行無轍跡，詣營求謁。

translations.literal: Again the Six Secret Teachings says: "When Wu Wang attacked Zhou, snow was more than a zhang deep; five chariots and two horses left no tracks as he went to camp to seek audience."
translations.idiomatic: The Six Secret Teachings says: "Wu Wang attacked Zhou; snow a zhang deep; five chariots and two horses left no tracks seeking audience at camp."

sentences.zh: 武王怪而問焉，太公對曰：'此必五方之神，來受事耳。

translations.literal: Wu Wang marveled and asked; Grand Duke Taigong replied: "These must be the spirits of the five directions come to receive orders."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Wang asked; Taigong said: "These are five-direction spirits come to receive orders."

sentences.zh: '遂以其名召入，各以其職命焉。

translations.literal: " He summoned them by name; each was charged with his office.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned each by name and charged each with office.

sentences.zh: 既而克殷，風調雨順。

translations.literal: Afterward he conquered Yin and wind and rain were harmonious."
translations.idiomatic: Then he conquered Yin and weather obeyed."

sentences.zh: 」豈有生來受職，歿同配之，降尊敵卑，理不然矣。

translations.literal: " How could spirits who received office in life after death be paired together—demoting the honored and equaling the base is not reasonable.
translations.idiomatic: Spirits who served in life cannot be paired in death—honor cannot equal the low.

sentences.zh: 故《春秋外傳》曰：「禘、郊、祖、宗、報五者，國之典祀也。

translations.literal: Thus the Outer Tradition of the Spring and Autumn says: "Di, jiao, zu, zong, and bao—the five are the state's canonical sacrifices."
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Outer Tradition says: "Di, jiao, zu, zong, and bao—five canonical state sacrifices."

sentences.zh: 」《傳》言五者，故知各是一事，非謂祖、宗合祀於明堂也。

translations.literal: " The Tradition speaks of five; thus one knows each is a separate affair, not that zu and zong are jointly sacrificed at Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Five means five separate rites—not joint zu-zong at Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 臣謹上考殷、周，下洎貞觀，並無一代兩帝同配於明堂。

translations.literal: We respectfully examine upward through Yin and Zhou and down to Zhenguan; none has two emperors of one generation jointly paired at Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: From Yin and Zhou through Zhenguan, no one generation paired two emperors at Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 南齊蕭氏以武、明昆季並於明堂配食，事乃不經，未足援據。

translations.literal: Southern Qi's Xiao clan paired Wu and Ming as brothers at Bright Hall—unorthodox and not to be cited.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Qi paired Wu and Ming as brothers at Bright Hall—too irregular to cite.

sentences.zh: 又檢武德時令，以元皇帝配于明堂，兼配感帝。

translations.literal: Again checking Wude statute, Emperor Yuan was paired at Bright Hall and also paired at Impulse Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Wude paired Yuan at Bright Hall and Impulse Emperor.

sentences.zh: 至貞觀初緣情革禮，奉祀高祖配于明堂，奉遷世祖專配感帝。

translations.literal: Early Zhenguan, following feeling and reforming ritual, sacrificed to Gaozu at Bright Hall and moved Shizu to pair only at Impulse Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Early Zhenguan paired Gaozu at Bright Hall and moved Shizu to Impulse Emperor alone.

sentences.zh: 此即聖朝故事已有遞遷之典，取法宗廟，古之制焉。

translations.literal: This is already the holy dynasty's precedent with succession in the canon, taking the ancestral temple as model—ancient regulation.
translations.idiomatic: That is already Tang precedent modeled on the temple—ancient rule.

sentences.zh: 伏惟太祖景皇帝構室有周，建絕代之丕業；

translations.literal: We observe that Grand Ancestor Emperor Jing founded the house in Zhou and built an unprecedented great enterprise;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Ancestor Jing founded the house in Zhou with unmatched achievement;

sentences.zh: 啟祚汾、晉，創曆聖之洪基。

translations.literal: he opened the mandate at Fen and Jin and founded the sage dynasty's vast foundation.
translations.idiomatic: he opened the mandate at Fen and Jin and laid the sage foundation.

sentences.zh: 德邁發生，道符立極。

translations.literal: Virtue surpassed birth; the Way matched establishing the pole.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue surpassed generation; the Way matched the cosmic pole.

sentences.zh: 又世祖元皇帝潛鱗韞慶，屈道事周，導浚發之靈源，肇光宅之垂裕。

translations.literal: Again Shizu Emperor Yuan concealed his scales and hoarded blessing, bent the Way to serve Zhou, guided the spirit source of dredging and issuing, and began the flowing blessing of glorious dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu Yuan concealed blessing, served Zhou, and opened the house's flowing fortune.

sentences.zh: 稱祖清廟，萬代不遷。

translations.literal: Called zu in the clear temple, ten thousand generations unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: As zu in the clear temple, unmoved for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 請停配祀，以符古義。

translations.literal: We ask to stop paired sacrifice to accord with ancient meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Stop paired sacrifice to match antiquity.

sentences.zh: 伏惟高祖太武皇帝躬受天命，奄有神州，創制改物，體元居正，為國始祖，抑有舊章。

translations.literal: We observe that Grand Ancestor Taizu received Heaven's mandate, embraced the Spirit Land, created institutions and changed things, embodied the origin and dwelt in correctness, was the state's founding ancestor, and indeed has old statute.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu received mandate, held the realm, founded institutions—founding ancestor with old statute.

sentences.zh: 昔者炎漢高帝，當塗太祖，皆以受命，例並配天。

translations.literal: Formerly Han Gaodi and Wei's founding ancestor, all upon receiving the mandate by precedent paired with Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gaodi and Wei's founder, on receiving mandate, paired with Heaven by precedent.

sentences.zh: 請遵故實，奉祀高祖于圓丘，以配昊天上帝。

translations.literal: We ask to follow the old fact and sacrifice to Gaozu at the Round Mound to pair with August Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Follow precedent: sacrifice to Gaozu at Round Mound pairing August Lord.

sentences.zh: 伏惟太宗文皇帝道格上元，功清下瀆，拯率土之塗炭，協大造於生靈，請准詔書，宗祀於明堂，以配上帝。

translations.literal: We observe Taizong Wen's Way reached the upper origin and merit cleared the lower streams, rescued the land's charcoal, and harmonized the great creation for the living; we ask to follow the edict and ancestrally sacrifice at Bright Hall to pair with the Lord on High.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's Way reached heaven and merit cleared earth; rescue the realm—ancestral sacrifice at Bright Hall pairing the Lord on High per edict.

sentences.zh: 又請依武德故事，兼配感帝作主。

translations.literal: Again we ask to follow Wude precedent and also pair at Impulse Emperor as chief.
translations.idiomatic: Also follow Wude: pair at Impulse Emperor as chief.

sentences.zh: 斯乃二祖德隆，永不遷廟；

translations.literal: Thus the two founders' virtue is lofty, never moved from temple;
translations.idiomatic: Two founders' virtue is lofty, never moved from temple;

sentences.zh: 兩聖功大，各得配天。

translations.literal: the two sages' merit is great, each pairing with Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: two sages' merit is great, each pairing with Heaven.

sentences.zh: 遠協《孝經》，近申詔意。

translations.literal: Far it agrees with the Classic of Filial Piety; near it declares the edict's intent.
translations.idiomatic: It agrees with Filial Piety and declares the edict.

sentences.zh: 二年七月，禮部尚書許敬宗與禮官等又奏議：

translations.literal: Seventh month, second year, Minister of Rites Xu Jingzong and ritual officers again memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: Year 2, month 7: Xu Jingzong and ritual officers memorialized again:

sentences.zh: 據祠令及新禮，並用鄭玄六天之議，圓丘祀昊天上帝，南郊祭太微感帝，明堂祭太微五帝。

translations.literal: According to the sacrifice statute and new ritual, all use Zheng Xuan's six-Heavens theory: Round Mound sacrifices August Lord; southern suburb sacrifices Supreme Palace Impulse Emperor; Bright Hall sacrifices Supreme Palace Five Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Statute and new ritual follow Zheng Xuan's six Heavens: Round Mound August Lord; southern suburb Supreme Palace Impulse Emperor; Bright Hall Supreme Palace Five Emperors.

sentences.zh: 謹按鄭玄此義，唯據緯書，所說六天，皆謂星象，而昊天上帝，不屬穹蒼。

translations.literal: We examine Zheng Xuan's meaning: it relies only on weft books; the six Heavens spoken of are all star images, while August Lord does not belong to the azure sky.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng relies on weft books; his six Heavens are stars—August Lord is not the sky.

sentences.zh: 故注《月令》及《周官》，皆謂圓丘所祭昊天下帝為北辰星曜魄寶。

translations.literal: Thus in commentary on the Monthly Ordinances and Offices of Zhou he all says the Lord on High sacrificed at Round Mound is North Star Brilliant Essence.
translations.idiomatic: He says Round Mound's Lord on High is North Star Brilliant Essence.

sentences.zh: 又說《孝經》「郊祀後稷以配天」及明堂嚴父配天，皆為太微五帝。

translations.literal: Again explaining the Classic of Filial Piety "jiao sacrifice to Hou Ji to pair with Heaven" and Bright Hall honoring the father to pair with Heaven, all as Supreme Palace Five Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: He makes Filial Piety's Hou Ji pairing Heaven and Bright Hall father pairing Heaven mean Supreme Palace Five Emperors.

sentences.zh: 考其所說，舛謬特深。

translations.literal: Examining what he says, the error is especially deep.
translations.idiomatic: His doctrine is deeply wrong.

sentences.zh: 按《周易》云：「日月麗於天，百穀草木麗於地。

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: "Sun and moon are attached to Heaven; the hundred grains and grasses are attached to Earth."
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says: "Sun and moon cling to Heaven; grain and grass cling to Earth."

sentences.zh: 」又云：「在天成象，在地成形。

translations.literal: " Again it says: "In Heaven forms are completed; on Earth forms take shape."
translations.idiomatic: Again: "In Heaven forms complete; on Earth forms take shape."

sentences.zh: 」足明辰象非天，草木非地。

translations.literal: " This suffices to show that star images are not Heaven and grasses are not Earth.
translations.idiomatic: That shows stars are not Heaven and plants are not Earth.

sentences.zh: 《毛詩傳》云：「元氣昊大，則稱昊天。

translations.literal: The Mao Odes Commentary says: "Primordial qi is vast and great—then it is called August Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Mao Commentary says: "Primordial qi vast and great is called August Heaven.

sentences.zh: 遠視蒼蒼，則稱蒼天。

translations.literal: Gazing far one sees the blue—then it is called Azure Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Gazing far at blue is called Azure Heaven."

sentences.zh: 」此則蒼昊為體，不入星辰之例。

translations.literal: 」This then treats the azure expanse as substance itself and does not fall under the category of asterisms.
translations.idiomatic: The azure vault is substance, not a star in the roster.

sentences.zh: 且天地各一，是曰兩儀。

translations.literal: Moreover Heaven and Earth are each one—this is called the Two Modes.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and Earth are each singular—the Two Modes.

sentences.zh: 天尚無二，焉得有六？

translations.literal: If Heaven still has no duplicate, how could there be six?
translations.idiomatic: Heaven admits no second; how six?

sentences.zh: 是以王肅群儒，鹹駁此義。

translations.literal: Therefore Wang Su and the mass of ru scholars all refuted this doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su and the ru scholars all rejected it.

sentences.zh: 又檢太史《圓丘圖》，昊天上帝座外，別有北辰座，與鄭義不同。

translations.literal: Again, examining the Grand Astrologer's Round Mound Diagram, beyond the seat of the Sovereign of Heaven there is a separate Pole Star seat—differing from Zheng Xuan's meaning.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Astrologer's Round Mound Diagram places Pole Star apart from the Sovereign of Heaven—unlike Zheng Xuan.

sentences.zh: 得太史令李淳風等狀，昊天上帝圖位自在壇上，北辰自在第二等，與北斗並列，為星官內座之首，不同鄭玄據緯書所說。

translations.literal: From memorials by Grand Astrologer Li Chunfeng and others: on the Sovereign of Heaven diagram the position is on the altar itself; Pole Star is on the second tier, arrayed with the Northern Dipper as head of inner official seats—unlike Zheng Xuan's reliance on apocryphal books.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chunfeng et al.: the Sovereign of Heaven sits on the altar; Pole Star ranks second with the Northern Dipper—not Zheng Xuan's apocryphal scheme.

sentences.zh: 此乃羲和所掌，觀象製圖，推步有征，相沿不謬。

translations.literal: This is what Xi and He controlled—observing images and drafting charts, calendrical steps with proof, handed down without error.
translations.idiomatic: Xi and He's observatory tradition: images, charts, and verified calendrics—transmitted correctly.

sentences.zh: 又按《史記天官書》等，太微宮有五帝者，自是五精之神，五星所奉。

translations.literal: Again, per the "Heavenly Offices" chapter of the Records and the like, the Five Emperors in the Supreme Ultimate Palace are the spirits of the five essences, attended by the five planets.
translations.idiomatic: The Records' Heavenly Offices: Supreme Ultimate's Five Emperors are five-essence spirits served by the five planets.

sentences.zh: 以其是人主之象，故況之曰帝。

translations.literal: Because they image the human ruler, they are styled emperors for comparison.
translations.idiomatic: As images of the earthly ruler, they are called emperors figuratively.

sentences.zh: 亦如房心為天王之象，豈是天乎！

translations.literal: It is also like Heart and Rooftop Beam as images of the Heavenly King—how could they be Heaven itself!
translations.idiomatic: Heart and Rooftop Beam image the Heavenly King—they are not Heaven.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》云：「兆五帝於四郊。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou says: "Establish the Five Emperors at the four suburbs."
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou: "Establish the Five Emperors at the four suburbs."

sentences.zh: 」又云：「祀五帝則掌百官之誓戒。

translations.literal: It also says: "When sacrificing to the Five Emperors, one administers the oath-admonitions of the hundred officials."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "Sacrificing to the Five Emperors, administer the hundred officials' oath-admonitions."

sentences.zh: 」惟稱五帝，皆不言天。

translations.literal: They only name the Five Emperors and never speak of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Five Emperors are named—never Heaven.

sentences.zh: 此自太微之神，本非穹昊之祭。

translations.literal: These are spirits of the Supreme Ultimate Palace in origin, not sacrifices to the vaulted azure.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme Ultimate spirits—not rites to the vaulted sky.

sentences.zh: 又《孝經》惟云「郊祀後稷」，無別祀圓丘之文。

translations.literal: The Classic of Filial Piety also only says "suburban sacrifice to Hou Ji," with no separate text on sacrificing at the Round Mound.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Filial Piety mentions only suburban sacrifice to Hou Ji—no Round Mound passage.

sentences.zh: 王肅等以為郊即圓丘，圓丘即郊，猶王城、京師，異名同實。

translations.literal: Wang Su and others held that suburb means Round Mound and Round Mound means suburb, like royal city and capital—different names, one reality.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su: suburb and Round Mound are one rite, as royal city and capital are one place.

sentences.zh: 符合經典，其義甚明。

translations.literal: It accords with the classics; the meaning is very clear.
translations.idiomatic: The classics support it clearly.

sentences.zh: 而今從鄭說，分為兩祭，圓丘之外，別有南郊，違棄正經，理深未允。

translations.literal: Yet now following Zheng's theory splits them into two sacrifices: beyond the Round Mound there is a separate Southern Suburban Altar—abandoning the orthodox canon, the principle deeply fails to convince.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's split—Round Mound plus a separate Southern Suburban Altar—abandons the canon.

sentences.zh: 且檢吏部式，惟有南郊陪位，更不別載圓丘。

translations.literal: Moreover, examining the Ministry of Personnel formulary, there is only Southern Suburban Altar attendant seating and no separate entry for the Round Mound.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry formulary lists only Southern Suburban attendants—not Round Mound.

sentences.zh: 式文既遵王肅，祠令仍行鄭義，令、式相乖，理宜改革。

translations.literal: The formulary follows Wang Su while the sacrifice ordinance still follows Zheng—ordinance and formulary at odds; reform is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Formulary follows Wang Su, ordinance follows Zheng—they should be reconciled.

sentences.zh: 又《孝經》雲「嚴父莫大于配天」，下文即云：「周公宗祀文王於明堂，以配上帝。

translations.literal: The Classic of Filial Piety also says "honoring the father, nothing is greater than matching Heaven," and the text below immediately says "the Duke of Zhou performed ancestral sacrifice to King Wen in the Bright Hall to match the Sovereign."
translations.idiomatic: Filial Piety: "honoring the father, nothing greater than matching Heaven"—then "the Duke of Zhou sacrificed to King Wen in the Bright Hall to match the Sovereign."

sentences.zh: 」則是明堂所祀，正在配天，而以為但祭星官，反違明義。

translations.literal: 」Then what the Bright Hall sacrifices is precisely matching Heaven; to hold that it only sacrifices star-officials reverses the clear meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Bright Hall sacrifice matches Heaven—not mere star-officials.

sentences.zh: 又按《月令》：「孟春之月，祈谷於上帝。

translations.literal: Again, per the Monthly Ordinances: "In the first month of spring, pray for grain to the Sovereign."
translations.idiomatic: Monthly Ordinances: "First month of spring—pray for grain to the Sovereign."

sentences.zh: 」《左傳》亦云：「凡祀，啟蟄而郊，郊而後耕。

translations.literal: The Zuo Commentary also says: "For all sacrifices, at Awakening of Hibernators perform suburb; after suburb then plow."
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Commentary: "Sacrifices begin at Awakening of Hibernators with suburb; after suburb, plowing."

sentences.zh: 故郊祀後稷，以祈農事。

translations.literal: Therefore suburban sacrifice to Hou Ji is to pray for agricultural affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Suburban sacrifice to Hou Ji prays for the harvest.

sentences.zh: 」然則啟蟄郊天，自以祈穀，謂為感帝之祭，事甚不經。

translations.literal: Thus suburb to Heaven at Awakening of Hibernators is in itself praying for grain; to call it sacrifice to the Feelings Emperor is very uncanonical.
translations.idiomatic: Awakening of Hibernators suburb prays for grain—it is not Feelings Emperor worship.

sentences.zh: 今請憲章姬、孔，考取王、鄭，四郊迎氣，存太微五帝之祀；

translations.literal: Now we ask to take the statutes of the Ji and Kong houses as model, examine Wang and Zheng, welcome seasonal qi at the four suburbs, and retain sacrifice to the Supreme Ultimate Five Emperors;
translations.idiomatic: We propose: follow Ji and Kong, weigh Wang and Zheng, keep four-suburb seasonal rites and Supreme Ultimate Five Emperors;

sentences.zh: 南郊明堂，廢緯書六天之義。

translations.literal: at the Southern Suburban Altar and Bright Hall, abolish the apocryphal doctrine of Six Heavens.
translations.idiomatic: and at Southern Suburban Altar and Bright Hall abolish the Six Heavens apocrypha.

sentences.zh: 其方丘祭地之外，別有神州，謂之北郊，

translations.literal: Beyond sacrifice at the Square Mound to Earth, there is a separate Divine Land, called Northern Suburban Altar;
translations.idiomatic: Besides Square Mound earth sacrifice, a separate Divine Land is called Northern Suburban Altar;

sentences.zh: 分地為二，既無典據，理又不通，亦請合為一祀，以符古義。

translations.literal: splitting Earth in two has no canonical warrant and is also unreasonable in principle—we also ask to unite them in one sacrifice to accord with ancient meaning.
translations.idiomatic: splitting earth in two lacks warrant—we ask one earth rite per ancient usage.

sentences.zh: 仍並條附式令，永垂後則。

translations.literal: Still attach the articles to ordinances and formulae as perpetual later standard.
translations.idiomatic: Attach these provisions to ordinances as permanent standard.

sentences.zh: 敬宗等又議籩、豆之數曰：「按今光祿式，祭天地、日月、嶽鎮、海瀆、先蠶等，籩、豆各四。

translations.literal: Jing Zong and others again debated the number of biǎn and dòu, saying: "Per the present Guanglu formulary, for sacrifice to Heaven and Earth, sun and moon, mountains and marshes, seas and rivers, and First Silkworm, biǎn and dòu are four each."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Zong et al. on biǎn and dòu: "Present Guanglu rules give four each for Heaven, Earth, sun, moon, mountains, seas, and First Silkworm."

sentences.zh: 祭宗廟，籩、豆各十二。

translations.literal: For ancestral temple sacrifice, biǎn and dòu are twelve each.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestral temple: twelve each.

sentences.zh: 祭社稷、先農等，籩、豆各九。

translations.literal: For Altars of Soil and Grain, First Agriculture, and the like, biǎn and dòu are nine each.
translations.idiomatic: Altars of Soil and Grain and First Agriculture: nine each.

sentences.zh: 祭風師、雨師，籩、豆各二。

translations.literal: For Wind Lord and Rain Lord, biǎn and dòu are two each.
translations.idiomatic: Wind Lord and Rain Lord: two each.

sentences.zh: 尋此式文，事深乖謬。

translations.literal: Searching this formulary text, the matter is deeply perverse.
translations.idiomatic: The formulary ranks are incoherent.

sentences.zh: 社稷多於天地，似不貴多。

translations.literal: Altars of Soil and Grain outrank Heaven and Earth—as if quantity were not honored.
translations.idiomatic: Soil and Grain outrank Heaven and Earth—as if more were not the rule.

sentences.zh: 風雨少於日月，又不貴少。

translations.literal: Wind and rain rank below sun and moon—yet neither is quantity honored less.
translations.idiomatic: Wind and rain below sun and moon—yet neither honors less.

sentences.zh: 且先農、先蠶，俱為中祭，或六或四，理不可通。

translations.literal: Moreover First Agriculture and First Silkworm are both middle sacrifices, yet one has six or four—unreasonable in principle.
translations.idiomatic: First Agriculture and First Silkworm are both middle rites—yet counts of six or four conflict.

sentences.zh: 又先農之神，尊於釋奠，籩、豆之數，先農乃少，理既差舛，難以因循。

translations.literal: Again, the spirit of First Agriculture outranks the libation-for-learning sacrifice, yet biǎn and dòu for First Agriculture are fewer—the principle already awry and hard to follow by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: First Agriculture outranks libation-for-learning—yet receives fewer biǎn and dòu; precedent cannot stand.

sentences.zh: 謹按《禮記郊特牲》云：'籩、豆之薦，水土之品，不敢用褻味而貴多品，所以交於神明之義也。

translations.literal: Respectfully per the "Suburban Victims" chapter of the Book of Rites: "The offering of biǎn and dòu are products of water and earth; one dare not use tainted flavors yet values many kinds—this is the meaning of communing with the spirits."
translations.idiomatic: Book of Rites, "Suburban Victims": biǎn and dòu present water-and-earth products; many kinds honor the spirits.

sentences.zh: '此即祭祀籩、豆，以多為貴。

translations.literal: 」That is, in sacrifice biǎn and dòu take multitude as honorable.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial biǎn and dòu honor abundance.

sentences.zh: 宗廟之數，不可逾郊。

translations.literal: The ancestral temple count must not exceed suburb.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestral counts must not exceed suburb.

sentences.zh: 今請大祀同為十二，中祀同為十，小祀同為八，釋奠准中祀。

translations.literal: Now we ask great sacrifice uniformly twelve, middle sacrifice ten, small sacrifice eight, libation-for-learning on middle-sacrifice standard.
translations.idiomatic: Proposed: great rites twelve, middle ten, small eight; libation-for-learning at middle standard.

sentences.zh: 自餘從座，並請依舊式。

translations.literal: For the rest of attendant seating, all please follow the old formulary.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant seating otherwise unchanged.

sentences.zh: 」詔並可之，遂附於禮令。

translations.literal: 」An edict approved all; they were then attached to the ritual ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: Approved and written into the ritual ordinance.

sentences.zh: 乾封初，高宗東封回，又詔依舊祀感帝及神州。

translations.literal: At the start of the Qianfeng era, after Gaozong returned from eastern feng and shan, he again ordered sacrifice to the Feelings Emperor and Divine Land per the old rites.
translations.idiomatic: Qianfeng: after Gaozong's eastern feng and shan, Feelings Emperor and Divine Land rites were restored.

sentences.zh: 司禮少常伯郝處俊等奏曰：

translations.literal: Director of Rituals Junior Regular Palace Attendant Hao Chujun and others memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: Director of Rituals Hao Chujun et al. memorialized:

sentences.zh: 顯慶新禮，廢感帝之祀，改為祈穀。

translations.literal: The Xianqing New Rites abolished sacrifice to the Feelings Emperor and changed it to praying for grain.
translations.idiomatic: Xianqing New Rites abolished Feelings Emperor worship for grain prayer.

sentences.zh: 昊天上帝，以高祖太武皇帝配。

translations.literal: The Sovereign of Heaven was matched with Grand Ancestor Taizu Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Sovereign of Heaven: Grand Ancestor Taizu as consort.

sentences.zh: 檢舊禮，感帝以世祖元皇帝配。

translations.literal: Examining old rites, the Feelings Emperor was matched with Shizu Yuan Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Old rite: Feelings Emperor with Shizu Yuan Emperor.

sentences.zh: 今既奉敕仍舊復祈穀為感帝，以高祖太武皇帝配神州，又高祖依新禮見配圓丘昊天上帝及方丘皇地祇，若更配感帝神州，便恐有乖古禮。

translations.literal: Now, obeying the edict to restore praying for grain as Feelings Emperor and match Grand Ancestor Taizu to Divine Land, while Grand Ancestor under the new rite already matches Round Mound Sovereign of Heaven and Square Mound Sovereign of Earth—if he also matches Feelings Emperor and Divine Land, one fears conflict with ancient rites.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu already matches Round Mound and Square Mound; adding Feelings Emperor and Divine Land may breach ancient pairing rules.

sentences.zh: 按《禮記·祭法》云：「有虞氏禘黃帝而郊嚳，夏後氏亦禘黃帝而郊鯀，殷人禘嚳而郊冥，周人禘嚳而郊稷。

translations.literal: Per the "Sacrifices" chapter of the Book of Rites: "Yu performed di to the Yellow Emperor and jiao to Kui; Xia also di to the Yellow Emperor and jiao to Gun; Yin di to Kui and jiao to Ming; Zhou di to Kui and jiao to Ji."
translations.idiomatic: Book of Rites, "Sacrifices": Yu di to Yellow Emperor, jiao to Kui; Xia likewise; Yin di to Kui, jiao to Ming; Zhou di to Kui, jiao to Ji.

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄注云：「禘謂祭昊天於圓丘也。

translations.literal: 」Zheng Xuan annotates: "Di means sacrificing to the Sovereign of Heaven at the Round Mound."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan: "Di is sacrifice to the Sovereign of Heaven at the Round Mound."

sentences.zh: 祭上帝於南郊曰郊」。

translations.literal: Sacrificing to the Sovereign at the Southern Suburban Altar is called jiao."
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice to the Sovereign at the Southern Suburban Altar is jiao."

sentences.zh: 又按《三禮義宗》雲，「夏正郊天者，王者各祭所出帝於南郊」，即《大傳》所謂「王者禘其祖之所自出，以其祖配之」是也。

translations.literal: Again per the Three Rites Meaning Summary it says, "Suburban Heaven in the first month of Xia—each king sacrifices the emperor from whom he arose at the Southern Suburban Altar"—this is what the Great Tradition means by "the king performs di to the ancestor from whom his house arose, with his ancestor as consort."
translations.idiomatic: Three Rites Meaning Summary: Xia first-month suburban Heaven—each king sacrifices his originating emperor at the Southern Suburban Altar—the Great Tradition's di with ancestor consort.

sentences.zh: 此則禘須遠祖，郊須始祖。

translations.literal: Thus di requires a remote ancestor; jiao requires the founding ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Di needs a remote ancestor; jiao needs the founding ancestor.

sentences.zh: 今若禘郊同用一祖，恐於典禮無所據。

translations.literal: If di and jiao now use one ancestor, one fears no warrant in canonical ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Using one ancestor for both di and jiao lacks canonical warrant.

sentences.zh: 其神州十月祭者，十月以陰用事，故以此時祭之，依檢更無故實。

translations.literal: Divine Land in the tenth month: the tenth month is when yin holds sway, hence sacrifice then—on examination there is no further ancient fact.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth-month Divine Land follows yin dominance—no ancient precedent found.

sentences.zh: 按《春秋》「啟蟄而郊」，鄭玄注「禮云：「三王之郊，一用夏正。

translations.literal: Per the Spring and Autumn Annals "suburb at Awakening of Hibernators," Zheng Xuan annotates "the Rites say: the three kings' suburb all used Xia first month."
translations.idiomatic: Spring and Autumn Annals: "suburb at Awakening of Hibernators"; Zheng Xuan: "three kings used Xia first month."

sentences.zh: 」又《三禮義宗》云：「祭神州法，正月祀於北郊。

translations.literal: 」Again the Three Rites Meaning Summary says: "The law for sacrificing Divine Land: sacrifice in the first month at the Northern Suburban Altar."
translations.idiomatic: Three Rites Meaning Summary: "Sacrifice Divine Land in first month at Northern Suburban Altar."

sentences.zh: 」請依典禮，以正月祭者。

translations.literal: 」We ask to sacrifice in the first month per the canon.
translations.idiomatic: We ask first-month sacrifice per canon.

sentences.zh: 請集奉常博士及司成博士等總議定奏聞。

translations.literal: Please assemble Director of Rituals erudites and Director of Studies erudites for joint deliberation and memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Assemble ritual and studies erudites for joint memorial.

sentences.zh: 其靈台、明堂，檢書禮用鄭玄義，仍祭五方帝，新禮用王肅義。

translations.literal: For the Spirit Terrace and Bright Hall, examining books and rites used Zheng Xuan's meaning and still sacrificed to the Five Directional Emperors; the new rites used Wang Su's meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit Terrace and Bright Hall: books followed Zheng Xuan (Five Directional Emperors); new rites followed Wang Su.

sentences.zh: 又下詔依鄭玄義祭五天帝，其雩及明堂，並准敕祭祀。

translations.literal: Again an edict followed Zheng Xuan's meaning to sacrifice to the Five Heavenly Emperors; rain prayer and Bright Hall all followed the edict for sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Zheng Xuan's Five Heavenly Emperors; rain prayer and Bright Hall followed.

sentences.zh: 於是奉常博士陸遵楷、張統師、權無二、許子儒等議稱：「北郊之月，古無明文。

translations.literal: Thereupon Director of Rituals erudites Lu Zunkai, Zhang Tongshi, Quan Wuer, Xu Ziru, and others debated, saying: "The month for Northern Suburban Altar—antiquity has no explicit text."
translations.idiomatic: Ritual erudites Lu Zunkai et al.: "Northern Suburban month lacks explicit antiquity."

sentences.zh: 漢光武正月辛未，始建北郊。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu on xinwei of the first month first established Northern Suburban Altar.
translations.idiomatic: Han Guangwu: first month xinwei, first Northern Suburban Altar.

sentences.zh: 鹹和中議，北郊同用正月，然皆無指據。

translations.literal: Xianhe-era deliberation also used first month for Northern Suburban Altar, yet all without pointed warrant.
translations.idiomatic: Xianhe used first month too—without explicit warrant.

sentences.zh: 武德來禮令即用十月，為是陰用事，故于時祭之。

translations.literal: Wude-era ritual ordinances immediately used the tenth month, because yin holds sway—hence sacrifice then.
translations.idiomatic: Wude ordinances used tenth month because yin dominates.

sentences.zh: 請依舊十月致祭。

translations.literal: We ask to sacrifice in the old tenth month.
translations.idiomatic: We ask to keep tenth-month sacrifice.

translations.literal: The memorial concluded."
translations.idiomatic: The memorial ended.

sentences.zh: 乾封二年十二月，詔曰：

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Qianfeng, an edict said:
translations.idiomatic: Qianfeng 2, twelfth month—edict:

sentences.zh: 夫受命承天，崇至敬於明祀；

translations.literal: Receiving the mandate and inheriting Heaven, one exalts utmost reverence in bright sacrifice;
translations.idiomatic: Mandate and Heaven demand utmost reverence in bright sacrifice;

sentences.zh: 膺圖纂籙，昭大孝于嚴配。

translations.literal: bearing the chart and seizing the register, one displays great filial piety in solemn matching.
translations.idiomatic: the chart and register call for great filial piety in solemn matching.

sentences.zh: 是以薦鰷鱨於清廟，集振鷺於西雍，宣《雅》、《頌》于太師，明肅恭於考室。

translations.literal: Thus one offers sturgeon and mudfish in the pure temple, gathers vibrating egrets at Western Yong, spreads the "Odes" and "Hymns" before the Grand Music Master, and makes reverent respect clear in the hall of the deceased father.
translations.idiomatic: Sturgeon in the pure temple, egrets at Western Yong, Odes before the Music Master, reverence in the father's hall.

sentences.zh: 用能紀配天之盛業，嗣積德之鴻休，永播英聲，長為稱首。

translations.literal: By this one can record the grand enterprise of matching Heaven, continue the vast blessing of accumulated virtue, forever broadcast illustrious fame, and long remain foremost in praise.
translations.idiomatic: Thus matching Heaven's enterprise and accumulated virtue endure in fame.

sentences.zh: 周京道喪，秦室政乖，禮樂淪亡，典經殘滅。

translations.literal: The Zhou capital's Way was lost; the Qin court's government went awry—rites and music perished, canonical scriptures were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou lost the Way; Qin warped government—rites perished, classics burned.

sentences.zh: 遂使漢朝博士，空說六宗之文；

translations.literal: Thus Han dynasty erudites vainly expounded the text of the Six Ancestors;
translations.idiomatic: Han erudites preached Six Ancestors in vain;

sentences.zh: 晉代鴻儒，爭陳七祀之議。

translations.literal: Jin-era great scholars vied to set forth the debate on seven sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Jin scholars debated seven sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 或同昊天於五帝，分感帝於五行。

translations.literal: Some equated the Sovereign of Heaven with the Five Emperors; some split the Feelings Emperor among the Five Phases.
translations.idiomatic: Some merged Sovereign of Heaven and Five Emperors; some split Feelings Emperor among Five Phases.

sentences.zh: 自茲以降，遞相祖述，異論紛紜，是非莫定。

translations.literal: From then downward each in turn took ancestors as model; diverse theories swarmed and right and wrong were never settled.
translations.idiomatic: Since then schools multiplied; right and wrong never settled.

sentences.zh: 朕以寡薄，嗣膺丕緒，肅承禋祀，明發載懷，虔奉宗祧，寤寐興感。

translations.literal: We, of meager capacity, have succeeded to the great succession, reverently undertake the suburban sacrifices, and at dawn our burden lies upon us; devoutly we tend the ancestral tablets—awake or asleep, feeling stirs.
translations.idiomatic: We succeed the throne, bear suburban rites at dawn, tend tablets waking and sleeping.

sentences.zh: 每惟宗廟之重，尊配之儀，思革舊章，以申誠敬。

translations.literal: Whenever we reflect on the weight of the ancestral temple and the rites of honored matching, we think to reform old statutes to declare sincere reverence.
translations.idiomatic: We would reform matching rites to declare sincere reverence.

sentences.zh: 高祖太武皇帝撫運膺期，創業垂統，拯庶類於塗炭，寘懷生於仁壽。

translations.literal: Grand Ancestor Taizu Emperor embraced the age's fortune, received the term, founded the enterprise and handed down the succession, rescued the multitude from flood and fire, and settled the living in benevolent longevity.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu received the mandate, founded the house, rescued the people, settled them in peace.

sentences.zh: 太宗文皇帝德光齊聖，道極幾神，執銳被堅，櫛風沐雨，勞形以安百姓，屈己而濟四方，澤被區中，恩覃海外。
