translations.literal: Taizong Wen Emperor's virtue shone equal to the sages, his Way reached the subtle divine; he grasped sharp weapons and donned hard armor, combed wind and bathed rain, labored in body to settle the hundred clans, bent himself to aid the four quarters—favor covered the realm, grace reached beyond the seas.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's virtue matched the sages; he bore hardship to settle the realm and aid the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 乾坤所以交泰，品物於是咸亨。

translations.literal: Heaven and Earth therefore achieved mutual peace; all things thereby flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and Earth at peace; all things flourished.

sentences.zh: 掩玄闕而開疆，指青丘而作鎮。

translations.literal: He closed the dark frontier and opened territory; he pointed to the Green Mound and made it a bastion.
translations.idiomatic: He opened borders and made the Green Mound a bastion.

sentences.zh: 巍巍蕩蕩，無得名焉。

translations.literal: Vast and boundless—no name can grasp it.
translations.idiomatic: Vast beyond naming.

sentences.zh: 《禮》曰：「化人之道，莫急於禮。

translations.literal: The Rites says: "In the Way of transforming people, nothing is more urgent than ritual."
translations.idiomatic: The Rites: "Transforming people—nothing urgent as ritual."

sentences.zh: 禮有五經，莫重於祭。

translations.literal: Ritual has five classics; nothing is weightier than sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual has five classics; sacrifice weighs heaviest.

sentences.zh: 祭者，非物自外至也，自內生於心也。

translations.literal: Sacrifice is not that things come from without to arrive; it is born from within the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice springs from the heart—not from without.

sentences.zh: 是以惟賢者乃能盡祭之義。

translations.literal: Therefore only the worthy can fully exhaust the meaning of sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Only the worthy fully grasp sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 」況祖功宗德，道冠百王；

translations.literal: 」How much more ancestral merit and clan virtue, the Way surpassing the hundred kings;
translations.idiomatic: How much more our ancestors, whose Way surpassed the hundred kings;

sentences.zh: 盡聖窮神，業高千古。

translations.literal: exhausting sagehood and probing spirit, achievement towering above a thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: sagehood exhausted, achievement towering a thousand ages.

sentences.zh: 自今以後，祭圓丘、五方、明堂、感帝、神州等祠，高祖太武皇帝、太宗文皇帝崇配，仍總祭昊天上帝及五帝於明堂。

translations.literal: From now on, for sacrifice at Round Mound, Five Directions, Bright Hall, Feelings Emperor, Divine Land, and the like, Grand Ancestor Taizu and Taizong Wen are honored as consorts; still collectively sacrifice the Sovereign of Heaven and Five Emperors at the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth Round Mound, Five Directions, Bright Hall, Feelings Emperor, and Divine Land: Taizu and Taizong as honored consorts; Sovereign of Heaven and Five Emperors at Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 庶因心致敬，獲展虔誠，宗祀配天，永光鴻烈。

translations.literal: May by heartfelt reverence we obtain the display of devotion; ancestral sacrifice matching Heaven forever glorify the grand achievement.
translations.idiomatic: May heartfelt devotion glorify matching Heaven forever.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳二年七月，太常少卿韋萬石奏曰：「明堂大享，准古禮鄭玄義，祀五天帝，王肅義，祀五行帝。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Yifeng, Junior Director of Rituals Wei Wanshi memorialized: "For the Bright Hall great offering, per ancient rites Zheng Xuan's meaning sacrifices to the Five Heavenly Emperors; Wang Su's meaning sacrifices to the Five Phases Emperors."
translations.idiomatic: Yifeng 2.7: Wei Wanshi—Bright Hall great offering: Zheng Xuan, Five Heavenly Emperors; Wang Su, Five Phases Emperors.

sentences.zh: 《貞觀禮》依鄭玄義祀五天帝，顯慶已來新修禮祀昊天上帝。

translations.literal: The Zhenguan Rites follow Zheng Xuan's Five Heavenly Emperors; since Xianqing the new rites sacrifice to the Sovereign of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguan followed Zheng; since Xianqing, the Sovereign of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 奉乾封二年敕祀五帝，又奉制兼祀昊天上帝。

translations.literal: Obeying the Qianfeng 2 edict to sacrifice to the Five Emperors, again per the imperial rescript jointly sacrifice the Sovereign of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Qianfeng 2 ordered Five Emperors; the rescript added Sovereign of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 伏奉上元三年三月敕，五禮並依貞觀年禮為定。

translations.literal: We respectfully submit: the third-month Shangyuan 3 edict fixed all five rites on the Zhenguan-era rites.
translations.idiomatic: Shangyuan 3.3: five rites fixed to Zhenguan standard.

sentences.zh: 又奉去年敕，並依周禮行事。

translations.literal: Again obeying last year's edict, all follow the Rites of Zhou in conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Last year's edict: follow the Rites of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 今用樂須定所祀之神，未審依古禮及《貞觀禮》，為復依見行之禮？

translations.literal: Now music must fix which spirits are sacrificed—unclear whether per ancient rites and the Zhenguan Rites, or per presently practiced rites?
translations.idiomatic: Which spirits the music serves—ancient and Zhenguan, or current practice?

sentences.zh: 」時高宗及宰臣並不能斷，依違久而不決。

translations.literal: 」At the time Gaozong and chief ministers alike could not decide; they wavered long without resolution.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong and ministers could not decide; the matter dragged on.

sentences.zh: 尋又詔尚書省及學者詳議，事仍不定。

translations.literal: Soon again an edict ordered the Department of State Affairs and scholars to debate in detail—still unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: State Affairs and scholars debated—still unsettled.

sentences.zh: 自此明堂大享，兼用貞觀、顯慶二《禮》。

translations.literal: From then Bright Hall great offerings used both the Zhenguan and Xianqing Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Bright Hall thereafter combined Zhenguan and Xianqing rites.

sentences.zh: 則天臨朝，垂拱元年七月，有司議圓丘、方丘及南郊、明堂嚴配之禮。

translations.literal: When Empress Zetian held court, in the seventh month of the first year of Chuigong, the relevant offices debated solemn matching at Round Mound, Square Mound, Southern Suburban Altar, and Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Chuigong 1.7: offices debated solemn matching for Round Mound, Square Mound, suburbs, and Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 成均助教孔玄義奏議曰：

translations.literal: Imperial University Assistant Instructor Kong Xuanyi memorialized in debate:
translations.idiomatic: Kong Xuanyi, Imperial University assistant, memorialized:

sentences.zh: 謹按《孝經》云：「孝莫大于嚴父，嚴父莫大于配天。

translations.literal: Respectfully per the Classic of Filial Piety: "Of filial piety nothing is greater than honoring the father; of honoring the father nothing is greater than matching Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Filial Piety: "Nothing greater than honoring the father; of that, nothing greater than matching Heaven."

sentences.zh: 」明配尊大，昊天是也。

translations.literal: 」The honored match most great is the Sovereign of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The greatest honored match is the Sovereign of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 物之大者，莫若於天，推父比天，與之相配，行孝之大，莫過於此，以明尊配之極也。

translations.literal: Of things the greatest is none like Heaven; comparing the father to Heaven and matching with it—the greatest filial conduct passes not this, to make clear the utmost of honored matching.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is greatest; matching the father to Heaven is filial piety's summit.

sentences.zh: 又《易》云：「先王以作樂崇德，殷薦之上帝，以配祖考。

translations.literal: The Changes also says: "The former kings made music to exalt virtue; in the Yin season they presented to the Sovereign, with ancestor and father as consorts."
translations.idiomatic: Changes: "Former kings made music; Yin season presented to the Sovereign with ancestors as consorts."

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄注：'上帝，天帝也。

translations.literal: 」Zheng Xuan annotates: "Sovereign means Heavenly Sovereign."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan: "Sovereign means Heavenly Sovereign."

sentences.zh: 」故知昊天之祭，合祖考並配。

translations.literal: 」Thus one knows sacrifice to the Sovereign of Heaven should jointly match ancestor and father.
translations.idiomatic: Sovereign of Heaven sacrifice should match ancestors and father.

sentences.zh: 請奉太宗文武聖皇帝、高宗天皇大帝配昊天上帝於圓丘，義符《孝經》、《周易》之文也。

translations.literal: We ask to match Taizong the Civil and Martial Sagely Emperor and Gaozong the Heavenly Sovereign Great Emperor with the Sovereign of Heaven at the Round Mound—accordant with the Classic of Filial Piety and the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Match Taizong and Gaozong to the Sovereign of Heaven at Round Mound—per Filial Piety and Changes.

sentences.zh: 神堯皇帝肇基王業，應天順人，請配感帝於南郊，義符《大傳》之文。

translations.literal: Spirit Yao Emperor first laid the royal foundation and responded to Heaven and followed the people—please match him to the Feelings Emperor at the Southern Suburban Altar, accordant with the Great Tradition.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit Yao founded the house—match him to Feelings Emperor at Southern Suburban Altar per Great Tradition.

sentences.zh: 又《祭法》云：「祖文王而宗武王。

translations.literal: Again the "Sacrifices" chapter says: "Take King Wen as zu and King Wu as zong."
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices: "King Wen as zu, King Wu as zong."

sentences.zh: 祖，始也；

translations.literal: Zu means "beginning";
translations.idiomatic: Zu denotes the founding ancestor.

sentences.zh: 宗，尊也。

translations.literal: zong means honoring.
translations.idiomatic: Zong means honoring.

sentences.zh: 所以名祭為尊始者，明一祭之中，有此二義。

translations.literal: Hence sacrifice is named for honoring the beginning—to make clear that within one sacrifice these two meanings exist.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice names honoring the beginning—two meanings in one rite.

sentences.zh: 又《孝經》云：「宗祀文王於明堂。

translations.literal: Again the Classic of Filial Piety says: "Perform zong sacrifice to King Wen in the Bright Hall."
translations.idiomatic: Filial Piety: "Perform zong sacrifice to King Wen in the Bright Hall."

sentences.zh: 」文王言祖，而雲宗者，亦是通武王之義。

translations.literal: 」King Wen is called zu yet the text says zong—this also extends King Wu's meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Wen is zu yet called zong—extending Wu's meaning.

sentences.zh: 故明堂之祭，配以祖考。

translations.literal: Therefore Bright Hall sacrifice matches with zu and kao.
translations.idiomatic: Bright Hall matches zu and kao.

sentences.zh: 請奉太宗文武聖皇帝、高宗天皇大帝配祭於明堂，義符《周易》及《祭法》之文也。

translations.literal: We ask to match Taizong the Civil and Martial Sagely Emperor and Gaozong the Heavenly Sovereign Great Emperor in Bright Hall sacrifice—accordant with the Changes and "Sacrifices."
translations.idiomatic: Match Taizong and Gaozong at Bright Hall—per Changes and Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 太子右諭德沈伯儀曰：

translations.literal: Right Tutor of the Heir Apparent Shen Boyi said:
translations.idiomatic: Heir Apparent Right Tutor Shen Boyi said:

sentences.zh: 謹按《禮》：「有虞氏禘黃帝而郊嚳，祖顓頊而宗堯。

translations.literal: Respectfully per the Rites: "Yu performed di to the Yellow Emperor and jiao to Kui; zu to Zhuanxu and zong to Yao."
translations.idiomatic: Rites: "Yu di to Yellow Emperor, jiao to Kui; zu Zhuanxu, zong Yao."

sentences.zh: 夏後氏禘黃帝而郊鯀，祖顓頊而宗禹。

translations.literal: Xia performed di to the Yellow Emperor and jiao to Gun; zu to Zhuanxu and zong to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Xia: di Yellow Emperor, jiao Gun; zu Zhuanxu, zong Yu.

sentences.zh: 殷人禘嚳而郊冥，祖契而宗湯。

translations.literal: Yin di to Kui and jiao to Ming; zu to Qi and zong to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Yin: di Kui, jiao Ming; zu Qi, zong Tang.

sentences.zh: 周人禘嚳而郊稷，祖文王而宗武王。

translations.literal: Zhou di to Kui and jiao to Ji; zu to King Wen and zong to King Wu."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou: di Kui, jiao Ji; zu King Wen, zong King Wu."

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄注云：「禘、郊、祖、宗，謂祭祀以配食也。

translations.literal: 」Zheng Xuan annotates: "Di, jiao, zu, and zong mean sacrifice with consort food."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan: "Di, jiao, zu, zong are sacrifice with consort food."

sentences.zh: 禘謂祭昊天於圓丘，祭上帝於南郊曰郊，祭五帝、五神於明堂曰祖、宗。

translations.literal: Di means sacrificing to the Sovereign of Heaven at the Round Mound; jiao means sacrificing to the Sovereign at the Southern Suburban Altar; zu and zong mean sacrificing to the Five Emperors and Five Spirits in the Bright Hall."
translations.idiomatic: Di at Round Mound; jiao at Southern Suburban Altar; zu and zong to Five Emperors and Five Spirits in Bright Hall."

sentences.zh: 」伏尋嚴配之文，於此最為詳備。

translations.literal: 」Searching the text of solemn matching, here it is most complete.
translations.idiomatic: Solemn matching is most fully stated here.

sentences.zh: 虞、夏則退顓頊而郊嚳，殷人則舍契而郊冥。

translations.literal: Yu and Xia set back Zhuanxu and jiao to Kui; Yin set aside Qi and jiao to Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Yu and Xia demoted Zhuanxu for Kui; Yin set aside Qi for Ming.

sentences.zh: 去取既多。

translations.literal: The taking and leaving are many.
translations.idiomatic: Too many shifts in precedence.

sentences.zh: 前後乖次。

translations.literal: Before and after violate order.
translations.idiomatic: Sequence is broken.

sentences.zh: 得禮之序，莫尚于周。

translations.literal: The sequence of rites—none surpasses Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's ritual order is supreme.

sentences.zh: 禘嚳郊稷，不間于二王；

translations.literal: Di to Kui, jiao to Ji, without gap between the two kings;
translations.idiomatic: Di Kui, jiao Ji—unbroken from the two prior dynasties;

sentences.zh: 明堂宗祀，始兼於兩配。

translations.literal: Bright Hall zong sacrifice first combined two consorts.
translations.idiomatic: Bright Hall zong first paired two consorts.

sentences.zh: 咸以文王、武王父子殊別，文王為父，上主五帝；

translations.literal: All took King Wen and King Wu, father and son distinct: Wen as father presided over the Five Emperors;
translations.idiomatic: Wen as father presided over Five Emperors; Wu as son—

sentences.zh: 武王對父，下配五神。

translations.literal: Wu facing the father, below matched the Five Spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Wu below matched Five Spirits.

sentences.zh: 《孝經》曰：「嚴父莫大于配天，則周公其人也。

translations.literal: The Classic of Filial Piety says: "Honoring the father, nothing greater than matching Heaven—the Duke of Zhou was such a man."
translations.idiomatic: Filial Piety: "Honoring the father, matching Heaven—the Duke of Zhou."

sentences.zh: 昔者周公宗祀文王於明堂，以配上帝。

translations.literal: In former days the Duke of Zhou performed zong sacrifice to King Wen in the Bright Hall to match the Sovereign."
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou zong-sacrificed to King Wen in Bright Hall to match the Sovereign."

sentences.zh: 」不言嚴武王以配天，則武王雖在明堂，理未齊於配祭；

translations.literal: It does not say honoring King Wu to match Heaven—thus though Wu was in the Bright Hall, in principle he did not equal consort sacrifice;
translations.idiomatic: It never honors Wu to match Heaven—Wu in Bright Hall was not Heaven's equal consort;

sentences.zh: 既稱宗祀，義獨主於尊嚴。

translations.literal: having called it zong sacrifice, the meaning rests solely in honoring.
translations.idiomatic: Zong sacrifice means honoring alone.

sentences.zh: 雖同兩祭，終為一主。

translations.literal: Though two sacrifices are the same, in the end there is one lord.
translations.idiomatic: Two rites, one lord.

sentences.zh: 故《孝經緯》曰「後稷為天地主，文王為五帝宗」也。

translations.literal: Thus the Filial Piety Apocrypha says "Hou Ji is lord of Heaven and Earth; King Wen is zong of the Five Emperors."
translations.idiomatic: Filial Piety Apocrypha: "Hou Ji lord of Heaven and Earth; King Wen zong of Five Emperors."

sentences.zh: 必若一神兩祭便，則五祭十祠，薦獻頻繁，禮虧於數。

translations.literal: If one spirit, two sacrifices were convenient, then five sacrifices and ten shrines—offerings frequent—the rites would fail in number.
translations.idiomatic: One spirit, two altars would multiply offerings beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 此則神無二主之道，禮崇一配之義。

translations.literal: This is the Way that spirits admit no second lord; ritual honors the meaning of one consort.
translations.idiomatic: Spirits have one lord; ritual honors single consort.

sentences.zh: 竊尋貞觀、永徽，共尊專配；

translations.literal: Privately searching Zhenguan and Yonghui, both honored a single consort;
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguan and Yonghui honored one consort each;

sentences.zh: 顯慶之後，始創兼尊。

translations.literal: after Xianqing they first created joint honoring.
translations.idiomatic: after Xianqing came joint honoring.

sentences.zh: 必以順古而行，實謂從周為美。

translations.literal: If one must follow antiquity in conduct, truly to follow Zhou is beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Following antiquity means following Zhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖神堯皇帝請配圓丘、方澤，太宗文武聖皇帝請配南郊、北郊。

translations.literal: Spirit Yao Emperor please match Round Mound and Square Mire; Taizong the Civil and Martial Sagely Emperor please match Southern and Northern Suburban Altars.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit Yao: Round Mound and Square Mire; Taizong: southern and northern suburbs.

sentences.zh: 高宗天皇大帝德邁九皇，功開萬宇，制禮作樂，告禪升中，率土共休，普天同賴，竊惟莫大之孝，理當總配五天。

translations.literal: Gaozong the Heavenly Sovereign Great Emperor's virtue surpassed the nine sovereigns, his achievement opened ten thousand realms, regulated rites and made music, reported feng and ascended zhong—all the realm shared repose, the whole sky shared blessing; privately we deem the greatest filial piety should collectively match the Five Heavens.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong surpassed the nine sovereigns—greatest filial piety should match all Five Heavens.

sentences.zh: 鳳閣舍人元萬頃、範履冰等議曰：

translations.literal: Phoenix Pavilion Attendant Yuan Wanqing, Fan Lübing, and others debated:
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Wanqing, Fan Lübing, Phoenix Pavilion attendants, debated:

sentences.zh: 伏惟高祖神堯皇帝鑿乾構象，辟土開基。

translations.literal: We respectfully consider Spirit Yao Emperor carved Heaven and structured the image, opened soil and laid foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit Yao carved Heaven and founded the realm.

sentences.zh: 太宗文武聖皇帝紹統披元，循機闡極。

translations.literal: Taizong the Civil and Martial Sagely Emperor continued the succession and spread the origin, followed the pivot to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong continued the succession to the utmost pivot.

sentences.zh: 高宗天皇大帝弘祖宗之大業，廓文武之宏規。

translations.literal: Gaozong the Heavenly Sovereign Great Emperor enlarged the ancestors' grand enterprise and broadened civil and martial magnificence.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong enlarged ancestral enterprise and civil-martial magnificence.

sentences.zh: 三聖重光，千年接旦。

translations.literal: Three sagely glories, a thousand years joining dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Three sagely glories—millennium joining dawn.

sentences.zh: 神功睿德，罄圖牒而難稱；

translations.literal: Divine achievement and sagely virtue exhaust registers yet are hard to name;
translations.idiomatic: Sagely virtue exhausts registers—unnamable;

sentences.zh: 盛烈鴻猷，超古今而莫擬。

translations.literal: grand triumphs and vast plans surpass past and present and cannot be compared.
translations.idiomatic: triumphs surpass past and present.

sentences.zh: 豈徒錙銖堯、舜，糠粃殷、周而已哉！

translations.literal: How merely to weigh against Yao and Shun by scruple or treat Yin and Zhou as chaff!
translations.idiomatic: More than scruples against Yao and Shun—Yin and Zhou are chaff.

sentences.zh: 謹案見行禮，昊天上帝等祠五所，咸奉高祖神堯皇帝、太宗文武皇帝兼配。

translations.literal: Respectfully examining present rites, for the five shrines including the Sovereign of Heaven, all jointly match Spirit Yao and Taizong the Civil and Martial Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Present rites: five Sovereign of Heaven shrines jointly match Spirit Yao and Taizong.

sentences.zh: 今議者引《祭法》、《周易》、《孝經》之文，雖近稽古之辭，殊失因心之旨。

translations.literal: Now debaters cite the "Sacrifices," Changes, and Classic of Filial Piety—though near antiquarian words, they greatly miss the intent born of the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Citing Sacrifices, Changes, and Filial Piety misses heartfelt intent.

sentences.zh: 但子之事父，臣之事君，孝以成志，忠而順美。

translations.literal: Yet the son's service to the father, the minister's service to the lord—filial piety completes the will, loyalty and compliance beautify.
translations.idiomatic: Son serves father, minister serves lord—filial piety and loyalty align.

sentences.zh: 竊以兼配之禮，特稟先聖之懷，爰取訓於前規，遂申情於大孝。

translations.literal: Privately, joint-matching rite specially inherits the former sages' intent, takes instruction from prior statutes, and declares feeling in great filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Joint matching inherits the sages and declares great filial feeling.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「昊天有成命，二後受之。

translations.literal: The Odes says: "The Sovereign of Heaven has a completed mandate; the two sovereigns received it."
translations.idiomatic: Odes: "Sovereign of Heaven's completed mandate—the two sovereigns received it."

sentences.zh: 」《易》曰：「殷薦之上帝，以配祖考。

translations.literal: The Changes says: "In the Yin season present to the Sovereign, with ancestor and father as consorts."
translations.idiomatic: Changes: "Yin season—present to Sovereign with ancestors as consorts."

sentences.zh: 」敬尋厥旨，本合斯義。

translations.literal: Reverently searching the purport, it originally fits this meaning.
translations.idiomatic: The purport originally fits.

sentences.zh: 今若遠摭遺文，近乖成典，拘常不變，守滯莫通，便是臣黜於君，遽易郊丘之位，下非於上，靡遵弓劍之心。

translations.literal: If now one plucks distant texts and near violates established canon, clinging to the constant without change, guarding stagnation without passage—then the minister is demoted before the lord, hastily shifting suburban and mound positions; the inferior wrongs the superior, not following the heart of bow and sword.
translations.idiomatic: Clinging to old texts demotes ministers over lords and wrongs the superior.

sentences.zh: 豈所以申太后哀感之誠，徇皇帝孝思之德！

translations.literal: How can this declare the empress dowager's grief and feeling, or follow the emperor's filial thought!
translations.idiomatic: How does this serve the empress dowager's grief or the emperor's filial piety?

sentences.zh: 慎終追遠，良謂非宜。

translations.literal: Careful ending and pursuing the remote—truly not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Careful ending and distant pursuit—unfitting.

sentences.zh: 嚴父配天，寧當若是？

translations.literal: Honoring the father to match Heaven—can it be thus?
translations.idiomatic: Honoring the father to match Heaven—can it be so?

sentences.zh: 伏據見行禮，高祖神堯皇帝、太宗文武聖皇帝，今既先配五祠，理當依舊無改。

translations.literal: We submit per present rites: Spirit Yao and Taizong the Civil and Martial Sagely Emperor already first match the five shrines—the principle is they should remain unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit Yao and Taizong already match five shrines—unchanged.

sentences.zh: 高宗天皇大帝齊尊曜魄，等邃含樞，闡三葉之宏基，開萬代之鴻業。

translations.literal: Gaozong the Heavenly Sovereign Great Emperor equals in honor the Bright Soul, equals in depth the Hidden Pivot—he unfolded the third generation's vast foundation and opened ten thousand generations' grand enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong equals Bright Soul and Hidden Pivot—third-generation foundation, ten-thousand-generation enterprise.

sentences.zh: 重規疊矩，在功烈而無差；

translations.literal: Layered statutes and repeated measures—in achievement and merit without difference;
translations.idiomatic: Statutes layered without difference in merit;

sentences.zh: 享帝郊天，豈祀配之有別。

translations.literal: enjoying the Sovereign and suburban Heaven—how could sacrificial matching differ?
translations.idiomatic: Enjoying the Sovereign at suburban Heaven—matching must not differ.

sentences.zh: 請奉高宗天皇大帝曆配五祠。

translations.literal: We ask to have Gaozong the Heavenly Sovereign Great Emperor match across the five shrines in succession.
translations.idiomatic: We ask Gaozong to match all five shrines in succession.

sentences.zh: 制從萬頃議。

translations.literal: The rescript followed Wanqing's debate.
translations.idiomatic: The throne followed Wanqing.

sentences.zh: 自是郊丘諸祠皆以三祖配。

translations.literal: From then suburban and mound shrines all used three ancestors as consorts.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter suburbs and mounds used three ancestors.

sentences.zh: 及則天革命，天冊萬歲元年，加號為天冊金輪大聖皇帝，親享南郊，合祭天地。

translations.literal: When Empress Zetian changed the dynasty, in the first year of Tiance, she added the title Golden Wheel Great Sagely Emperor, personally enjoyed the Southern Suburban Altar, and jointly sacrificed Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Tiance 1: Zetian took title Golden Wheel Great Sagely Emperor and jointly sacrificed Heaven and Earth at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 以武氏始祖周文王追尊為始祖文皇帝，後考應國公追尊為無上孝明高皇帝，亦以二祖同配，如乾封之禮。

translations.literal: The Wu clan's founding ancestor King Wen of Zhou was posthumously honored Founding Ancestor Wen Emperor; her late father the Lord of Ying was posthumously honored Supreme Filial Bright High Emperor—they too used two ancestors jointly as consorts, as in the Qianfeng rite.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen and her father Ying Lord were posthumously honored and jointly matched, as at Qianfeng.

sentences.zh: 其後長安年又親享南郊，合祭天地及諸郊丘，並以配焉。

translations.literal: Later in the Chang'an era she again personally enjoyed the Southern Suburban Altar, jointly sacrificing Heaven and Earth and all suburban mounds, all with consorts.
translations.idiomatic: In Chang'an she again sacrificed at the southern suburb with all suburbs matched.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，神龍元年九月，親享昊天上帝於東都之明堂，以高宗天皇大崇配，其儀亦依乾封故事。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong ascended, in the ninth month of the first year of Shenlong he personally sacrificed to the Sovereign of Heaven at the Bright Hall in the eastern capital, with Gaozong the Heavenly Sovereign Great as honored consort—the rites also followed Qianfeng precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Shenlong 1.9: Zhongzong sacrificed to the Sovereign of Heaven at eastern-capital Bright Hall with Gaozong as consort—Qianfeng precedent.

sentences.zh: 至景龍三年十一月，親祀南郊，初將定儀注，國子祭酒祝欽明希旨上言後亦合助祭，遂奏議曰：「謹按《周禮》：'天神曰祀，地祇曰祭，宗廟曰享。

translations.literal: By the eleventh month of the third year of Jinglong he personally sacrificed at the Southern Suburban Altar; when first fixing the ritual protocol, Director of the Imperial University Zhu Qinming, to please the intent, said the empress should also jointly assist in sacrifice, and memorialized in debate: "Respectfully per the Rites of Zhou: Heavenly spirits are called si; earthly spirits are called ji; ancestral temple is called xiang."
translations.idiomatic: Jinglong 3.11: fixing southern-suburb rites, Zhu Qinming said the empress should assist: "Rites of Zhou: spirits si, earth ji, temple xiang."

sentences.zh: '又《內司服》：'職掌王后之六服，凡祭祀，供後之衣服。

translations.literal: Again the Inner Palace Attire: "In charge of the queen's six garments—for all sacrifices supply the consort's robes."
translations.idiomatic: Inner Palace Attire: "Supply the queen's robes for all sacrifices."

sentences.zh: '又《祭統》曰：'夫祭也者，必夫婦親之。

translations.literal: Again the "Sacrificial Unity" says: "Sacrifice requires husband and wife in person."
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial Unity: "Sacrifice requires husband and wife in person."

sentences.zh: '據此諸文，即知皇后合助皇帝祀天神祭地祇明矣。

translations.literal: Per these texts, the queen's joint assistance in the emperor's sacrifice to heavenly spirits and earthly spirits is clear.
translations.idiomatic: These texts show the queen should assist in heaven and earth sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 望請別修助祭儀注同進。

translations.literal: We ask separately to compile joint-assistance ritual protocol and submit together.
translations.idiomatic: We ask a separate joint-assistance protocol.

sentences.zh: 」上令宰相與禮官議詳其事。

translations.literal: 」The emperor ordered chief ministers and ritual officers to debate the matter in detail.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered ministers and ritual officers to debate.

sentences.zh: 太常博士唐紹、蔣欽緒建議云：「皇后南郊助祭，於禮不合。

translations.literal: Director of Rituals erudites Tang Shao and Jiang Qinxu proposed: "The queen's southern-suburb joint assistance is unfitting in ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Tang Shao and Jiang Qinxu: queen's southern-suburb assistance is uncanonical.

sentences.zh: 但欽明所執，是祭宗廟禮，非祭天地禮。

translations.literal: Yet what Qinming held is ancestral-temple ritual, not heaven-and-earth ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Qinming cited temple rite, not heaven-and-earth rite.

sentences.zh: 按漢、魏、晉、及後魏、齊、梁、隋等歷代史籍，興王令主，郊天祀地，代有其禮，史不闕書，並不見皇后助祭之事。

translations.literal: Examining Han, Wei, Jin, and Later Wei, Qi, Liang, Sui and other dynasties' histories—founding kings and enlightened lords, suburban Heaven and sacrificing earth each generation had its rite, histories do not omit record—yet nowhere is queen joint assistance seen.
translations.idiomatic: Histories from Han through Sui record suburban rites—never queen joint assistance.

sentences.zh: 又高祖神堯皇帝、太宗文武聖皇帝、高宗天皇大帝南郊祀天，並無皇后助祭之禮。

translations.literal: Again Spirit Yao, Taizong, and Gaozong at the Southern Suburban Altar sacrificed to Heaven—none had queen joint assistance.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit Yao, Taizong, and Gaozong at southern suburb—no queen assistance.

sentences.zh: 」尚書右僕射韋巨源又協同欽明之議，上遂以皇后為亞獻，仍補大臣李嶠等女為齋娘，執籩豆焉。

translations.literal: 」Minister of the Right Wei Juyuan also agreed with Qinming's debate; the emperor then made the empress secondary presenter, still supplementing ministers Li Qiao and others' daughters as fast maidens to hold biǎn and dòu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Juyuan agreed; the emperor made the empress secondary presenter and appointed fast maidens for biǎn and dòu.

sentences.zh: 時十一月十三日乙丑，冬至，陰陽人盧雅、侯藝等奏請促冬至就十二日甲子以為吉會。

translations.literal: At the time, the thirteenth day of the eleventh month was yichou—the winter solstice; yin-yang specialists Lu Ya, Hou Yi, and others memorialized asking to advance the winter solstice to the twelfth day jiazi as auspicious assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month 13, yichou—winter solstice; Lu Ya and Hou Yi asked to advance it to jiazi on the 12th.

sentences.zh: 時右台侍御史唐紹奏曰：「禮所以冬至祀圓丘於南郊，夏至祭方澤於北郊者，以其日行躔次，極於南北之際也。

translations.literal: Right Censorate Attending Censor Tang Shao memorialized: "Ritual sacrifices at winter solstice to the Round Mound at the Southern Suburban Altar and at summer solstice to the Square Mire at the Northern Suburban Altar because the sun's course reaches the utmost of south and north."
translations.idiomatic: Tang Shao: winter solstice Round Mound at southern suburb, summer solstice Square Mire at northern suburb—the sun at its south-north limits.

sentences.zh: 日北極當晷度循半，日南極當晷度環周。

translations.literal: When the sun is at the north pole the gnomon shadow follows half; when at the south pole the gnomon shadow circles the full circumference.
translations.idiomatic: At north pole the shadow is half; at south pole it circles full.

sentences.zh: 是日一陽爻生，為天地交際之始。

translations.literal: On that day the first yang line is born—the beginning of Heaven and Earth's interchange.
translations.idiomatic: That day the first yang line is born—Heaven and Earth begin to interchange.

sentences.zh: 故《易》曰：'《復》，其見天地之心乎！

translations.literal: Thus the Changes says: "Fù—does it not show the heart of Heaven and Earth!"
translations.idiomatic: Changes: "Fù—does it not show Heaven and Earth's heart!"

sentences.zh: '即冬至卦象也。

translations.literal: 」That is the winter-solstice hexagram image.
translations.idiomatic: That is winter solstice's hexagram image.

sentences.zh: 一歲之內，吉莫大焉。

translations.literal: Within one year, nothing is more auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Within the year, nothing is more auspicious.

sentences.zh: 甲子但為六旬之首，一年之內，隔月常遇，既非大會，晷運未周，唯總六甲之辰，助四時而成歲。

translations.literal: Jiazi is only the head of the six decad cycles; within one year it is regularly met in alternate months, is not a great assembly, and the gnomon's revolution is not complete—only by totaling the days of the six jia does it aid the four seasons to complete the year.
translations.idiomatic: Jiazi is only the head of the six decad cycles; within a year it appears in alternate months, is no great assembly, and the sundial's cycle is incomplete—only by totaling the six jia days does it help the four seasons make a year.

sentences.zh: 今欲避環周以取甲子，是背大吉而就小吉也。

translations.literal: Now wishing to avoid the full cycle to take jiazi is turning one's back on great auspice to seek small auspice.
translations.idiomatic: To avoid the full cycle and seize jiazi is to forsake great auspice for a lesser one.

sentences.zh: 」太史令傅孝忠奏曰：「准《漏刻經》，南陸北陸並日校一分，若用十二日，即欠一分。

translations.literal: " The Grand Astrologer Fu Xiaozhong memorialized: "Per the Classic of Clepsydra Graduations, south land and north land on the same day are checked one fen; if one uses the twelfth day, one fen is short.
translations.idiomatic: " Grand Astrologer Fu Xiaozhong memorialized: "Per the Classic of Clepsydra Graduations, south and north lands are checked one fen on the same day; using the twelfth day falls one fen short.

sentences.zh: 未南極，即不得為至。

translations.literal: If the south pole is not reached, it cannot count as the solstice.
translations.idiomatic: Without reaching the south pole, it cannot count as the solstice.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「俗諺雲，'冬至長於歲'，亦不可改。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "As the folk proverb says, 'The winter solstice is longer than the year'—this too cannot be changed.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "As the proverb runs, 'The winter solstice is longer than the year'—that too cannot be changed.

sentences.zh: 」竟依紹議以十三日乙丑祀圓丘。

translations.literal: " In the end they followed Shao's proposal and on the thirteenth day, yichou, sacrificed at the round mound.
translations.idiomatic: " They finally followed Shao's proposal and sacrificed at the round mound on the thirteenth day, yichou.

sentences.zh: 睿宗太極元年正月，初將有事南郊，有司立議，惟祭昊天上帝而不設皇地祇位。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Taiji under Ruizong, when they were first to perform the southern suburb rites, the responsible offices established the proposal to sacrifice only to August Heaven High God and not set a seat for August Earth Spirit.
translations.idiomatic: In Ruizong's Taiji year 1, first month, as the southern suburb rites were first planned, the offices proposed sacrificing only to August Heaven High God without a seat for August Earth Spirit.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫賈曾上表曰：

translations.literal: Remonstrance Counselor Jia Zeng submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Counselor Jia Zeng submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 微臣詳據典禮，謂宜天地合祭。

translations.literal: Your humble servant has examined the canonical rites in detail and holds that Heaven and Earth should be sacrificed together.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has examined the canonical rites and holds that Heaven and Earth ought to be sacrificed together.

sentences.zh: 謹按《禮祭法》曰：「有虞氏禘黃帝而郊嚳，夏後氏禘黃帝而郊鯀。

translations.literal: Respectfully per the Record of Rites on Sacrifice: "Youyu di at the di to Huangdi and at the jiao to Ku; Xia hou di at the di to Huangdi and at the jiao to Gun."
translations.idiomatic: Per the Record of Rites on Sacrifice: "Youyu performed di to Huangdi and jiao to Ku; Xia performed di to Huangdi and jiao to Gun."

sentences.zh: 」傳曰：大祭曰禘。

translations.literal: " The tradition says: a great sacrifice is called di.
translations.idiomatic: " Tradition says a great sacrifice is called di.

sentences.zh: 然則郊之與廟，俱有禘祭。

translations.literal: Thus both the suburb and the temple have di sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Thus suburb and temple alike have di sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 禘廟，則祖宗之主俱合于太祖之廟；

translations.literal: At di in the temple, the lords of the ancestors are all united in the Grand Ancestor's temple;
translations.idiomatic: Di at the temple unites the ancestral lords in the Grand Ancestor's temple;

sentences.zh: 禘郊，則地祇群望俱合於圓丘，以始祖配享。

translations.literal: at di at the suburb, Earth Spirits and the host of wang are all united at the round mound, with the founding ancestor as consort.
translations.idiomatic: di at the suburb unites Earth Spirits and the host of wang at the round mound, with the founding ancestor as consort.

sentences.zh: 皆有事而大祭，異于常祀之義。

translations.literal: all are great sacrifices with special intent, differing from ordinary sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: all are solemn great sacrifices, distinct from ordinary rites.

sentences.zh: 《禮大傳》曰：「不王不禘。

translations.literal: The Great Tradition of Rites says: "One who is not king does not perform di."
translations.idiomatic: The Great Tradition says: "One who is not king does not perform di."

sentences.zh: 」故知王者受命，必行禘禮。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that when a king receives the Mandate he must perform the di rite.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when a king receives the Mandate he must perform di.

sentences.zh: 《虞書》曰：「月正元日，舜格于文祖，肆類於上帝，祇于六宗，望於山川，遍於群神。

translations.literal: The Book of Yu says: "On the first day of the first month, Shun arrived at the Literary Ancestor; he then classified sacrifice to High God, presented to the Six Ancestors, wang at mountains and rivers, and pervaded the host of spirits."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Yu says: "On the first day of the first month Shun arrived at the Literary Ancestor; he classified sacrifice to High God, presented to the Six Ancestors, wang at mountains and rivers, and reached the host of spirits."

sentences.zh: 」此則受命而行禘禮者也。

translations.literal: " This is performing the di rite upon receiving the Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: " This is performing di upon receiving the Mandate.

sentences.zh: 言「格于文祖」，則餘廟之享可知矣。

translations.literal: When it says "arrived at the Literary Ancestor," the rest of the temples' offerings can be known.
translations.idiomatic: Saying "arrived at the Literary Ancestor" shows what the other temple offerings were.

sentences.zh: 言「類於上帝」，則地祇之合可知矣。

translations.literal: When it says "classified to High God," the union of Earth Spirits can be known.
translations.idiomatic: Saying "classified to High God" shows Earth Spirits were included.

sentences.zh: 且山川之祀，皆屬於地，群望尚遍，況地祇乎！

translations.literal: Moreover sacrifices to mountains and rivers all belong to Earth; if the host of wang are still pervaded, how much more Earth Spirits!
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices to mountains and rivers belong to Earth; if the host of wang are still fully included, how much more Earth Spirits!

sentences.zh: 《周官》「以六律、六呂、五聲、八音、六舞、大合樂，以致神祇，以和邦國，以諧萬人。

translations.literal: The Offices of Zhou: "With the six lü, six lü, five tones, eight sounds, and six dances, greatly harmonize music to reach the spirits, harmonize the states, and harmonize the myriad people."
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Zhou: "With six lü, six lü, five tones, eight sounds, and six dances, greatly harmonize music to reach the spirits, harmonize the states, and harmonize the people."

sentences.zh: 」又「凡六樂者，六變而致象物及天神」，此則禘郊合天神、地祇、人鬼而祭之樂也。

translations.literal: " Moreover, "Of all six musics, six transformations bring forth images, things, and the Heavenly Spirit"—this is the music of di at the suburb uniting Heavenly Spirit, Earth Spirits, and human ghosts in sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: " Moreover, "Of the six musics, six transformations bring forth images, things, and the Heavenly Spirit"—the music of di at the suburb, uniting Heaven, Earth, and the human dead in one sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 《三輔故事》漢祭圓丘儀：昊天上帝位正南面，後土位兆亦南面而少東。

translations.literal: Han round-mound rites in Old Matters of the Three Metropolises: August Heaven High God's seat faced due south; Queen Earth's seat-plot also faced south but slightly east.
translations.idiomatic: Han round-mound rites per Old Matters of the Three Metropolises: August Heaven High God faced south; Queen Earth's plot also faced south, slightly east.

sentences.zh: 又《東觀漢記》云：「光武即位，為壇于鄗之陽，祭告天地，採用元始故事。

translations.literal: The Eastern Pavilion Han Record also says: "When Guangwu took the throne he built an altar on the sunny slope at Hao, sacrificing to announce to Heaven and Earth, adopting Yuan Shi precedents."
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Pavilion Han Record says: "When Guangwu took the throne he built an altar on Hao's sunny slope to announce sacrifice to Heaven and Earth, following Yuan Shi precedent."

sentences.zh: 二年正月，于洛陽城南依鄗為圓壇，天地位其上，皆南向西上。

translations.literal: In the second year, first month, south of Luoyang he modeled Hao as a round altar; Heaven and Earth seats were upon it, all facing south and west above.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2, first month, south of Luoyang he built a round altar modeled on Hao; Heaven and Earth seats stood upon it, all facing south with west above.

sentences.zh: 」按兩漢時自有後土及北郊祀，而此已於圓丘設地位，明是禘祭之儀。

translations.literal: " Examining the two Han eras, they had their own Queen Earth and northern suburb sacrifices, yet here Earth seats were already set at the round mound—clearly the rite of di sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: " Though the two Han had separate Queen Earth and northern suburb rites, Earth seats were already at the round mound—clearly a di rite.

sentences.zh: 又《春秋說》云：「王者一歲七祭，天地合食于四孟，別於分、至。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Explanations also say: "A king in one year has seven sacrifices; Heaven and Earth eat together at the four meng, separate at equinox and solstice."
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Explanations say: "A king has seven sacrifices a year; Heaven and Earth feast together at the four meng, separately at equinox and solstice."

sentences.zh: 」此復天地自常有同祭之義。

translations.literal: " This again shows Heaven and Earth themselves often share sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: " This again shows Heaven and Earth commonly shared sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 王肅云：「孔子言兆圓丘於南郊，南郊即圓丘，圓丘即南郊也。

translations.literal: Wang Su said: "Confucius said to locate the round mound at the southern suburb—the southern suburb is the round mound, the round mound is the southern suburb."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su said: "Confucius said to locate the round mound at the southern suburb—southern suburb is round mound, round mound is southern suburb."

sentences.zh: 」又云：「祭天地配。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Sacrifice Heaven and Earth with consorts."
translations.idiomatic: " He also said Heaven and Earth are sacrificed with consorts."

sentences.zh: 」此亦郊祀合祭之明說。

translations.literal: " This too is clear proof of combined suburb sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: " This too clearly proves combined suburb sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 惟鄭康成不論禘當合祭，而分昊天上帝為二神，專憑緯文，事匪經見。

translations.literal: Only Zheng Xuan did not discuss di as combined sacrifice but divided August Heaven High God into two spirits, relying solely on weft texts—matters not seen in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zheng Xuan denied di as combined sacrifice, split August Heaven High God into two spirits, and relied on weft texts—not on the classics.

sentences.zh: 又其注《大傳》「不環不禘」義，則云：「正歲之首，祭感帝之精，以其祖配。

translations.literal: Moreover his comment on the Great Tradition's "not cycling, not di" says: "At the head of the correct year, sacrifice the essence of the Felt Emperor, with one's ancestor as consort."
translations.idiomatic: His gloss on "not cycling, not di" says: "At the correct year's head, sacrifice the Felt Emperor's essence with one's ancestor as consort."

sentences.zh: 」注《周官·大司樂》圓丘，則引《大傳》之禘以為冬至之祭。

translations.literal: " Commenting on the Grand Music Master of the Offices of Zhou on the round mound, he cites the Great Tradition's di as the winter-solstice sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Commenting on the round mound in the Grand Music Master chapter, he cites the Great Tradition's di as the winter-solstice rite.

sentences.zh: 遞相矛盾，未足可依。

translations.literal: Mutually contradicting in succession, it is not sufficient to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: These contradict one another and cannot be relied on.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下膺籙居尊，繼文在曆，自臨宸極，未親郊祭。

translations.literal: Bowing low: Your Majesty has received the tally and dwells in honor, continuing culture upon the calendar; since personally attending the imperial pole you have not yourself performed suburb sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has received the Mandate and sits in honor, continuing culture on the calendar; since taking the throne you have not performed suburb sacrifice in person.

sentences.zh: 今之南郊，正當禘禮，固宜合祀天地，鹹秩百神，答受命之符，彰致敬之道。

translations.literal: Today's southern suburb is exactly the di rite; it is right to sacrifice Heaven and Earth together, extend rank to the hundred spirits, answer the tally of receiving the Mandate, and display the way of reverent respect.
translations.idiomatic: Today's southern suburb is properly di; Heaven and Earth should be sacrificed together, the hundred spirits ranked, the Mandate answered, and reverence displayed.

sentences.zh: 豈可不崇盛禮，同彼常郊，使地祇無位，未從禘享！

translations.literal: How can one not exalt the full rite, treat it like an ordinary suburb, leave Earth Spirits without a seat, and not follow di offering!
translations.idiomatic: How can the full rite not be exalted, Earth Spirits left without seats, and di offering withheld like an ordinary suburb!

sentences.zh: 今請備設皇地祇並從祀等座，則禮得稽古，義合緣情。

translations.literal: Now I request fully setting August Earth Spirit and attendant sacrifice seats—then the rite can examine antiquity and the meaning fits human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: I request seats for August Earth Spirit and attendants—then the rite matches antiquity and accords with feeling.

sentences.zh: 然郊丘之祀，國之大事，或失其情，精禋將闕。

translations.literal: Yet suburb and mound sacrifice is a great affair of state; if feeling is lost, the refined offering will be wanting.
translations.idiomatic: Yet suburb and mound sacrifice is a state great affair; if feeling is wrong, the refined offering fails.

sentences.zh: 臣術不通經，識慚博古，徒以昔謬禮職，今忝諫曹，正議是司，敢陳忠讜。

translations.literal: Your servant's art does not penetrate the classics, his learning shames the broadly ancient—only because he once erred in ritual office and now disgraces the remonstrance bureau, whose charge is upright discussion, does he dare state loyal counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant's learning does not penetrate the classics and shames the ancients—having once erred in ritual office and now holding remonstrance, he dares offer loyal counsel.

sentences.zh: 事有可采，惟斷之聖慮。

translations.literal: If anything may be adopted, let it be decided by sagely deliberation alone.
translations.idiomatic: If anything here may be adopted, let sagely deliberation decide.

sentences.zh: 制令宰臣召禮官詳議可否。

translations.literal: An order directed the chief ministers to summon ritual officers to discuss in detail whether it was feasible.
translations.idiomatic: An order directed the chief ministers to summon ritual officers to discuss feasibility.

sentences.zh: 禮官國子祭酒褚無量、國子司業郭山惲等咸請依曾所奏。

translations.literal: Ritual officers—the National University Rector Chu Wuliang, Vice-Rector Guo Shanyun, and others—all requested following Zeng's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers—National University Rector Chu Wuliang, Vice-Rector Guo Shanyun, and others—all asked to follow Zeng's memorial.

sentences.zh: 時又將親享北郊，竟寢曾之表。

translations.literal: At that time they were again about to perform the northern suburb in person, and in the end Zeng's memorial was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: They were again about to perform the northern suburb in person, and Zeng's memorial was shelved.

sentences.zh: 玄宗即位，開元十一年十一月，親享圓丘。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong took the throne, in the eleventh month of Kaiyuan 11 he personally performed the round mound.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong took the throne, in Kaiyuan 11, eleventh month, he personally performed the round mound.

sentences.zh: 時中書令張說為禮儀使，衛尉少卿韋絛為副，說建議請以高祖神堯皇帝配祭，始罷三祖同配之禮。

translations.literal: At that time Chief Councilor Zhang Yue was ritual commissioner and Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wei Tao deputy; Yue proposed using Founding Emperor Shenyao as consort sacrifice and began abolishing the rite of three ancestors as joint consorts.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councilor Zhang Yue was ritual commissioner and Court of Imperial Sacrifices Vice Director Wei Tao deputy; Yue proposed Founding Emperor Shenyao as consort and abolished three-ancestor joint consortship.

sentences.zh: 至二十年，蕭嵩為中書令，改撰新禮。

translations.literal: By the twentieth year Xiao Song was chief councilor and revised and compiled new rites.
translations.idiomatic: By year 20 Xiao Song was chief councilor and compiled new rites.

sentences.zh: 祀天一歲有四，祀地有二。

translations.literal: Sacrifices to Heaven in one year were four; sacrifices to Earth, two.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven was sacrificed four times a year; Earth, twice.

sentences.zh: 冬至，祀昊天上帝於圓丘，高祖神堯皇帝配，中官加為一百五十九座，外官減為一百四座。

translations.literal: At the winter solstice August Heaven High God was sacrificed at the round mound, with Founding Emperor Shenyao as consort; inner officials were increased to 159 seats, outer officials reduced to 104.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter solstice August Heaven High God was sacrificed at the round mound with Founding Emperor Shenyao as consort; inner officials rose to 159 seats, outer to 104.

sentences.zh: 其昊天上帝及配帝二座，每座籩、豆各用十二，簋、簠、、俎各一。

translations.literal: For August Heaven High God and the two consort seats, each seat used twelve bian and dou, one each of gui, fu, jia, and zuo.
translations.idiomatic: For High God and the two consort seats, each used twelve bian and dou and one each of gui, fu, jia, and zuo.

sentences.zh: 上帝則太樽、著樽、犧樽、象樽、壺樽各二，山罍六。

translations.literal: For High God: great zun, zhuo zun, xi zun, elephant zun, and hu zun two each; mountain lei six.
translations.idiomatic: For High God: two each of great, zhuo, xi, elephant, and hu zun; six mountain lei.

sentences.zh: 配帝則不設太樽及壺樽，減山罍之四，餘同上帝。

translations.literal: For the consort seat no great zun or hu zun were set; four mountain lei were reduced; the rest matched High God.
translations.idiomatic: The consort seat omitted great and hu zun, reduced mountain lei by four; the rest matched High God.

sentences.zh: 五方帝座則籩、豆各十，簋、簠、、俎各一，太樽二。

translations.literal: Five Directional Emperor seats had ten bian and dou each, one each of gui, fu, jia, and zuo, and two great zun.
translations.idiomatic: Five Directional Emperor seats had ten bian and dou, one each of gui, fu, jia, and zuo, and two great zun.

sentences.zh: 大明、夜明，籩、豆各八，餘同五方帝。

translations.literal: Great Bright and Night Bright had eight bian and dou each; the rest matched the Five Directional Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Great Bright and Night Bright used eight bian and dou each; all else matched the Five Directional Emperors.

sentences.zh: 內官每座籩、豆二，簋、俎各一。

translations.literal: Each inner official seat had two bian and dou, one gui and one zuo.
translations.idiomatic: Each inner-official seat had two bian and dou, one gui and one zuo.

sentences.zh: 內官已上設樽於十二階之間。

translations.literal: Above inner officials, zun were set between the twelve steps.
translations.idiomatic: Above inner officials, zun were set among the twelve steps.

sentences.zh: 內官每道間著樽二，中官犧樽二，外官著樽二，眾星壺樽二。

translations.literal: Between each inner-official aisle two zhuo zun; middle officials two xi zun; outer officials two zhuo zun; host of stars two hu zun.
translations.idiomatic: Each inner aisle had two zhuo zun; middle officials two xi zun; outer officials two zhuo zun; host of stars two hu zun.

sentences.zh: 正月上辛，祈穀，祀昊天上帝於圓丘，以高祖配，五方帝從祀。

translations.literal: On the upper xin day of the first month, prayer for grain: August Heaven High God was sacrificed at the round mound with the Founder as consort; Five Directional Emperors attended.
translations.idiomatic: On the first month's upper xin, for grain prayer High God was sacrificed at the round mound with the Founder as consort; Five Directional Emperors attended.

sentences.zh: 其上帝、配帝，籩、豆等同冬至之數。

translations.literal: For High God and consort, bian and dou matched the winter-solstice count.
translations.idiomatic: High God and consort used the same bian and dou as at the winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 五方帝，太樽、著樽、犧樽、山罍各一，籩、豆等亦同冬至之數。

translations.literal: Five Directional Emperors: one each of great, zhuo, xi zun and mountain lei; bian, dou, and the rest also matched winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: Five Directional Emperors: one each of great, zhuo, xi zun and mountain lei; bian, dou, and the rest matched winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 孟夏，雩昊天上之帝於圓丘，乙太宗配，五方帝及太昊等五帝、勾芒等五官從祀。

translations.literal: In the first month of summer, rain prayer to High God Above Heaven at the round mound, with Taizong as consort; Five Directional Emperors and Taihao and the five emperors, Gou Mang and the five officials attended.
translations.idiomatic: In early summer, rain prayer to High God Above Heaven at the round mound with Taizong as consort; Five Directional Emperors, Taihao and the five emperors, Gou Mang and the five officials attended.

sentences.zh: 其上帝配帝、五方帝，籩、豆各八，簋、簠、、俎各一。

translations.literal: For High God, consort, and Five Directional Emperors: eight bian and dou each, one each of gui, fu, jia, and zuo.
translations.idiomatic: High God, consort, and Five Directional Emperors: eight bian and dou, one each of gui, fu, jia, and zuo.

sentences.zh: 五官每座籩、豆各二，簋、簠及俎各一。

translations.literal: Each of the five officials' seats had two bian and dou, one gui, one fu, and one zuo.
translations.idiomatic: Each five-official seat had two bian and dou, one gui, one fu, and one zuo.

sentences.zh: 季秋，大享於明堂，祀昊天上帝，以睿宗配，其五方帝、五人帝、五官從祀。

translations.literal: In late autumn, great offering at the Bright Hall: August Heaven High God was sacrificed with Ruizong as consort; Five Directional Emperors, Five Human Emperors, and five officials attended.
translations.idiomatic: In late autumn, great offering at the Bright Hall: High God with Ruizong as consort; Five Directional Emperors, Five Human Emperors, and five officials attended.

sentences.zh: 籩、豆之數，同於雩祀。

translations.literal: The count of bian and dou matched the rain-sacrifice rite.
translations.idiomatic: Bian and dou matched the rain-sacrifice rite.

sentences.zh: 夏至，禮皇地祇于方丘，以高祖配，其從祀神州已下六十八座，同貞觀之禮。

translations.literal: At the summer solstice August Earth Spirit was honored at the square mound with the Founder as consort; attendant sacrifice from Spirit State downward numbered 68 seats, as in the Zhenguan rite.
translations.idiomatic: At the summer solstice Earth Spirit was honored at the square mound with the Founder as consort; 68 attendant seats from Spirit State down, as in Zhenguan.

sentences.zh: 地祇、配帝，籩、豆如圓丘之數。

translations.literal: Earth Spirit and consort: bian and dou as at the round mound.
translations.idiomatic: Earth Spirit and consort used the round-mound bian and dou count.

sentences.zh: 神州，籩、豆各四，簋、簠、、俎各一。

translations.literal: Spirit State: four bian and dou each, one each of gui, fu, jia, and zuo.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit State: four bian and dou, one each of gui, fu, jia, and zuo.

sentences.zh: 五嶽、四鎮、四海、四瀆、五方、山林、川澤等三十七座，每座籩、豆各二，簋、簠各一。

translations.literal: Five Marchmounts, four garrisons, four seas, four streams, five directions, mountains, forests, rivers, and marshes—37 seats—each had two bian and dou, one gui and one fu.
translations.idiomatic: Five marchmounts, four garrisons, four seas, four streams, five directions, mountains, forests, rivers, and marshes—37 seats—each had two bian and dou, one gui and one fu.

sentences.zh: 五方五帝、丘陵、墳衍、原隰等三十座，籩、豆、簋、簠、、俎各一。

translations.literal: Five Directional Emperors, hills, mounds, embankments, plains, and lowlands—30 seats—one each of bian, dou, gui, fu, jia, and zuo.
translations.idiomatic: Five Directional Emperors, hills, mounds, dykes, plains, and lowlands—30 seats—one each of bian, dou, gui, fu, jia, and zuo.

sentences.zh: 立冬，祭神州於北郊，乙太宗配。

translations.literal: At the start of winter Spirit State was sacrificed at the northern suburb, with Taizong as consort.
translations.idiomatic: At winter's start Spirit State was sacrificed at the northern suburb with Taizong as consort.

sentences.zh: 二座籩、豆各十二，簋、簠、、俎各一。

translations.literal: The two seats had twelve bian and dou each, one each of gui, fu, jia, and zuo.
translations.idiomatic: The two seats had twelve bian and dou, one each of gui, fu, jia, and zuo.

sentences.zh: 自冬至圓丘已下，餘同貞觀之禮。

translations.literal: From winter-solstice round mound downward, the rest matched the Zhenguan rite.
translations.idiomatic: From winter-solstice round mound down, the rest matched Zhenguan.

sentences.zh: 時起居舍人王仲丘既掌知修撰，仍建議曰：

translations.literal: At that time Attendant of the Palace Secretariat Wang Zhongqiu, who also directed compilation, further proposed:
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Wang Zhongqiu, who directed compilation, further proposed:

sentences.zh: 按《貞觀禮》，正月上辛，祀感帝於南郊，《顯慶禮》，祀昊天上帝於圓丘以祈穀。

translations.literal: Per the Zhenguan Rites, on the first month's upper xin the Felt Emperor was sacrificed at the southern suburb; per the Xianqing Rites, August Heaven High God was sacrificed at the round mound for grain prayer.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhenguan Rites sacrifice the Felt Emperor at the southern suburb on the first month's upper xin; the Xianqing Rites sacrifice High God at the round mound for grain prayer.

sentences.zh: 《左傳》曰：「郊而後耕。

translations.literal: The Zuo Tradition says: "Suburb sacrifice, then plowing."
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Tradition: suburb sacrifice, then plowing.

sentences.zh: 」《詩》曰：「《噫嘻》，春夏祈谷於上帝。

translations.literal: The Odes say: "Yi Xi—spring and summer grain prayer to High God."
translations.idiomatic: The Odes: "Yi Xi—spring and summer grain prayer to High God."

sentences.zh: 」《禮記》亦曰：「上辛祈谷於上帝。

translations.literal: The Record of Rites also says: "On upper xin, grain prayer to High God."
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites: on upper xin, grain prayer to High God.

sentences.zh: 」則祈谷之文，傳於歷代，上帝之號，允屬昊天。

translations.literal: Thus the text of grain prayer is transmitted through the dynasties, and the title High God properly belongs to August Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Grain-prayer texts run through the dynasties, and the title High God properly belongs to August Heaven.

sentences.zh: 而鄭康成云：「天之五帝遞王，王者之興，必感其一，因其所感，別祭尊之。

translations.literal: Yet Zheng Xuan said: "Heaven's Five Emperors in turn receive kingship; when a king rises he must feel one of them; according to which he felt, sacrifice and honor it separately."
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zheng Xuan said: "Heaven's Five Emperors receive kingship in turn; a rising king feels one of them and sacrifices that one separately."

sentences.zh: 故夏正之月，祭其所生之帝於南郊，以其祖配之。

translations.literal: Therefore in the first month of summer sacrifice is made to the emperor one was born from at the southern suburb, with one's ancestor as consort.
translations.idiomatic: So in summer's first month one sacrifices at the southern suburb to the emperor one was born from, with one's ancestor as consort.

sentences.zh: 故周祭靈威仰，以後稷配之，因以祈穀。

translations.literal: Thus Zhou sacrificed to Lingwei Yang with Hou Ji as consort, thereby grain prayer.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou sacrificed to Lingwei Yang with Hou Ji as consort, calling it grain prayer.

sentences.zh: 」據所說祀感帝之意，本非祈穀。

translations.literal: " According to the intent of sacrificing the Felt Emperor he described, it was originally not grain prayer.
translations.idiomatic: " Sacrificing the Felt Emperor as he described was never grain prayer.

sentences.zh: 先儒所說，事恐難憑。

translations.literal: What former scholars said is probably hard to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Former scholars' views are hard to rely on.

sentences.zh: 今祈穀之禮，請准禮修之。

translations.literal: Now for the grain-prayer rite, I request following the rites in repair.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that grain prayer follow the canonical rites.

sentences.zh: 且感帝之祀，行之自久。

translations.literal: Moreover sacrifice to the Felt Emperor has long been practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice to the Felt Emperor has long been practiced.

sentences.zh: 《記》曰：「有其舉之，莫可廢也。

translations.literal: The Record says: "Where there is an established practice, none may abolish it."
translations.idiomatic: The Record says: "Where a practice exists, it may not be abolished."

sentences.zh: 」請于祈穀之壇，遍祭五方帝。

translations.literal: " I request at the grain-prayer altar to sacrifice pervasively to the Five Directional Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: " I ask that the grain-prayer altar also sacrifice to all Five Directional Emperors.

sentences.zh: 夫五帝者，五行之精。

translations.literal: The Five Emperors are the essences of the Five Phases.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Emperors embody the essences of the Five Phases.

sentences.zh: 五行者，九谷之宗也。

translations.literal: The Five Phases are the patron of the nine grains.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Phases are patron of the nine grains.

sentences.zh: 今請二禮並行，六神鹹祀。

translations.literal: Now I request both rites practiced together, all six spirits fully sacrificed.
translations.idiomatic: I ask both rites run together so all six spirits are sacrificed.

sentences.zh: 又按《貞觀禮》，孟夏雩祀五方上帝、五人帝、五官於南郊，《顯慶禮》，則雩祀昊天上帝於圓丘。

translations.literal: Moreover per the Zhenguan Rites, in early summer rain sacrifice the Five Directional High Gods, Five Human Emperors, and five officials at the southern suburb; per the Xianqing Rites, rain sacrifice to August Heaven High God at the round mound.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhenguan Rites rain-sacrifice Five Directional High Gods, Five Human Emperors, and five officials at the southern suburb in early summer; the Xianqing Rites sacrifice High God at the round mound.

sentences.zh: 且雩祀上帝，蓋為百穀祈甘雨。

translations.literal: Moreover rain sacrifice to High God is broadly to pray sweet rain for the hundred grains.
translations.idiomatic: Rain sacrifice to High God prays sweet rain for the crops.

sentences.zh: 故《月令》云：「命有司大雩帝，用盛樂，以祈穀實。

translations.literal: Thus the Monthly Ordinances say: "Order the officers to great rain prayer to the Emperor, using splendid music, to pray for full grain."
translations.idiomatic: The Monthly Ordinances say: "Order officers to great rain prayer to the Emperor with splendid music, to pray for full grain."

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄云：「雩上帝者，天之別號，允屬昊天，祀於圓丘，尊天位也。

translations.literal: " Zheng Xuan said: "Rain prayer to High God is Heaven's other title, properly August Heaven; sacrifice at the round mound honors Heaven's position."
translations.idiomatic: " Zheng Xuan said: "Rain prayer to High God uses Heaven's other title—August Heaven; the round mound honors Heaven's position."

sentences.zh: 」然雩祀五帝既久，亦請二禮並行，以成大雩帝之義。

translations.literal: " Yet rain sacrifice to the Five Emperors has also been long practiced; I also request both rites together to complete the meaning of great rain prayer to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: " Rain sacrifice to the Five Emperors is also ancient; I ask both rites together to complete great rain prayer to the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 又《貞觀禮》，季秋祀五方帝、五官於明堂，《顯慶禮》，禮昊天上帝於明堂。

translations.literal: Moreover the Zhenguan Rites in late autumn sacrifice the Five Directional Emperors and five officials at the Bright Hall; the Xianqing Rites honor August Heaven High God at the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhenguan Rites sacrifice Five Directional Emperors and five officials at the Bright Hall in late autumn; the Xianqing Rites honor High God there.

sentences.zh: 准《孝經》曰：「郊祀後稷以配天，宗祀文王於明堂，以配上帝。

translations.literal: Per the Classic of Filial Piety: "At the suburb sacrifice to Hou Ji to consort with Heaven; at the ancestral temple sacrifice to King Wen at the Bright Hall to consort with High God."
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Filial Piety says: "Suburb sacrifice to Hou Ji consorts with Heaven; Bright Hall sacrifice to King Wen consorts with High God."

sentences.zh: 」先儒以為天是感精之帝，即太微五帝，此即皆是星辰之例。

translations.literal: Former scholars held that Heaven is the spirit of the Felt Emperor, namely the Five Emperors of the Supreme Palace—all examples of asterisms.
translations.idiomatic: Former scholars held Heaven is the Felt Emperor's spirit—the Supreme Palace Five Emperors—all stellar examples.

sentences.zh: 且上帝之號，皆屬昊天，鄭玄所引，皆云五帝。

translations.literal: Moreover the title High God all belongs to August Heaven; what Zheng Xuan cited all said Five Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: High God's title belongs to August Heaven; Zheng Xuan's citations all speak of Five Emperors.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》曰：「王將旅上帝，張氈案，設皇邸。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou say: "When the king is about to lodge with High God, spread felt mats and set the august lodging."
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou say: "When the king lodges with High God, spread felt mats and set the august lodging."

sentences.zh: 祀五帝，張大次小次。

translations.literal: Sacrifice to the Five Emperors—spread great and small awnings.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificing the Five Emperors—spread great and small awnings.

sentences.zh: 」由此言之，上帝之與五帝，自有差等，豈可混而為一乎！

translations.literal: From this speaking, High God and the Five Emperors have their own gradations—how can they be mixed into one!
translations.idiomatic: Thus High God and the Five Emperors have distinct ranks—how can they be mixed into one!

sentences.zh: 《孝經》云：「嚴父莫大于配天。

translations.literal: The Classic of Filial Piety says: "Honoring the father, nothing is greater than consorting with Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Filial Piety says: "Honoring the father, nothing exceeds consorting with Heaven."

sentences.zh: 」其下文即云：「宗祀文王於明堂，以配上帝。

translations.literal: Its following text immediately says: "Ancestral sacrifice to King Wen at the Bright Hall to consort with High God."
translations.idiomatic: The next line says: "Ancestral sacrifice to King Wen at the Bright Hall to consort with High God."

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄注云：「上帝者，天之別名，神無二主，故異其處。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan commented: "High God is Heaven's other name; spirits have no second lord, therefore the places differ."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan commented: "High God is Heaven's other name; spirits have no second lord, so the places differ."

sentences.zh: 」孔安國之：「帝亦天也。

translations.literal: Kong Anguo said: "Di is also Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Kong Anguo: "Di is also Heaven."

translations.literal: The quotation concluded."
translations.idiomatic: The quoted passage closed.

sentences.zh: 然則禋享上帝，有合經義。

translations.literal: Thus refined offering to High God fits the classic meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Refined offering to High God fits the classics.

sentences.zh: 而五方皆祀，行之已久，有其舉之，難於即廢。

translations.literal: Yet sacrifice to all five directions has long been practiced; where there is an established practice, it is hard to abolish at once.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice to all five directions is also ancient; established practice is hard to abolish at once.

sentences.zh: 亦請二禮並行，以成《月令》大享帝之義。

translations.literal: I also request both rites practiced together to complete the Monthly Ordinances' meaning of great offering to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: I also ask both rites together to complete the Monthly Ordinances' great offering to the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 天寶十載五月已前，郊祭天地，以高祖神堯皇帝配座，故將祭郊廟，告高祖神堯皇帝室。

translations.literal: Before the fifth month of Tianbao 10, suburb sacrifices to Heaven and Earth used Founding Emperor Shenyao as consort seat; therefore before sacrificing at suburb and temple they announced at Founding Emperor Shenyao's chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Before Tianbao 10, fifth month, suburb sacrifices used Founding Emperor Shenyao as consort; before suburb and temple sacrifice they announced at his chamber.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，杜鴻漸為太常卿禮儀使，員外郎薛頎、歸崇敬等議：「以神堯為受命之主，非始封之君不得為太祖以配天地。

translations.literal: In Baoying 1, Du Hongjian as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and ritual commissioner, with Registrar Xue Qi, Gui Chongjing, and others discussed: "Shenyao as recipient of the Mandate is not the first enfeoffed lord and cannot be Grand Ancestor to consort with Heaven and Earth."
translations.idiomatic: In Baoying 1, ritual commissioner Du Hongjian with Registrar Xue Qi and Gui Chongjing argued: "Shenyao received the Mandate but was not the first enfeoffed lord and cannot be Grand Ancestor consort with Heaven and Earth."

sentences.zh: 太祖景皇帝始受封于唐，即殷之契，周之後稷也。

translations.literal: Grand Ancestor Emperor Jing first received enfeoffment in Tang—he is Yin's Qi, Zhou's Hou Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Ancestor Emperor Jing first received Tang—he is Yin's Qi, Zhou's Hou Ji.

sentences.zh: 請以太祖景皇帝郊祀配天地，告請宗廟，亦太祖景皇帝酌獻。

translations.literal: I request using Grand Ancestor Emperor Jing at suburb sacrifice to consort with Heaven and Earth; at temple announcement the libation too should be Grand Ancestor Emperor Jing's.
translations.idiomatic: I ask Grand Ancestor Emperor Jing consort at suburb sacrifice to Heaven and Earth and at temple announcement.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫黎幹議，以太祖景皇帝非受命之君，不合配享天地。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Counselor Li Gan argued that Grand Ancestor Emperor Jing was not the Mandate-receiving lord and did not fit consorting with Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Counselor Li Gan argued Emperor Jing did not receive the Mandate and should not consort with Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 二年五月，幹進議狀為十詰十難，曰：

translations.literal: In the fifth month of year 2, Gan submitted a discussion memorial in ten interrogations and ten refutations, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In year 2, fifth month, Gan submitted ten interrogations and ten refutations:

sentences.zh: 集賢校理潤州別駕歸崇敬議狀及禮儀使判官水部員外郎薛頎等稱：禘謂冬至祭天於圓丘，周人則以遠祖帝嚳配，今欲以景皇帝為始祖，配昊天於圓丘。

translations.literal: Collector of Texts and Runzhou Registrar Gui Chongjing's discussion and ritual commissioner Registrar Xue Qi of the Waterways Bureau said: di means winter-solstice sacrifice to Heaven at the round mound; Zhou people used remote ancestor Emperor Ku as consort—now they wish the Jing Emperor as founding ancestor to consort with August Heaven at the round mound.
translations.idiomatic: Gui Chongjing and ritual commissioner Xue Qi said di is winter-solstice Heaven sacrifice at the round mound; Zhou used remote ancestor Ku as consort—now they want Emperor Jing as founding ancestor to consort with August Heaven.

sentences.zh: 臣幹詰曰：「《國語》曰：「有虞氏、夏後氏俱禘黃帝，商人禘舜，周人禘嚳。

translations.literal: Your servant Gan interrogates: "The Discourses of the States says: "Youyu and Xia both di Huangdi; Shang di Shun; Zhou di Ku.""
translations.idiomatic: Gan interrogates: "The Discourses of the States says Youyu and Xia both di Huangdi, Shang di Shun, Zhou di Ku."

sentences.zh: 」俱不言祭昊天於圓丘，一也。

translations.literal: None speaks of sacrificing August Heaven at the round mound—one.
translations.idiomatic: None mentions sacrificing August Heaven at the round mound—first point.

sentences.zh: 《詩·商頌》曰：「《長髮》，大禘也。

translations.literal: The Odes, Shang Hymns, say: "Chang Fa—a great di."
translations.idiomatic: The Shang Hymns say: "Chang Fa—a great di."

sentences.zh: 」又不言昊天於圓丘，二也。

translations.literal: It also does not speak of August Heaven at the round mound—two.
translations.idiomatic: It too says nothing of August Heaven at the round mound—second.

sentences.zh: 《詩·周頌》曰：「《雍》，禘太祖也。

translations.literal: The Odes, Zhou Hymns, say: "Yong—di to the Grand Ancestor."
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou Hymns say: "Yong—di to the Grand Ancestor."

sentences.zh: 」又不言祭昊天於圓丘，三也。

translations.literal: It also does not speak of sacrificing August Heaven at the round mound—three.
translations.idiomatic: It too says nothing of August Heaven at the round mound—third.

sentences.zh: 《禮記·祭法》曰：「有虞氏、夏後氏俱禘黃帝，殷人、周人俱禘嚳。

translations.literal: Record of Rites, Sacrifice Law: "Youyu and Xia both di Huangdi; Yin and Zhou both di Ku."
translations.idiomatic: The Sacrifice Law says: "Youyu and Xia di Huangdi; Yin and Zhou di Ku."

sentences.zh: 」又不言祭昊天於圓丘，四也。

translations.literal: It also does not speak of sacrificing August Heaven at the round mound—four.
translations.idiomatic: It too says nothing of August Heaven at the round mound—fourth.

sentences.zh: 《禮記·大傳》曰：「不王不禘。

translations.literal: Record of Rites, Great Tradition: "One who is not king does not perform di."
translations.idiomatic: The Great Tradition: "One who is not king does not perform di."

sentences.zh: 王者禘其祖之所自出，以其祖配之。

translations.literal: A king di to the ancestor from whom his line issued, with that ancestor as consort.
translations.idiomatic: A king performs di to the ancestor from whom his line issued, with that ancestor as consort.

sentences.zh: 」又不言祭昊天於圓丘，五也。

translations.literal: It also does not speak of sacrificing August Heaven at the round mound—five.
translations.idiomatic: It too says nothing of August Heaven at the round mound—fifth.

sentences.zh: 《爾雅·釋天》曰：「禘，大祭也。

translations.literal: Erya, Explaining Heaven: "Di—a great sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: Erya, Explaining Heaven: di is a great sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 」又不言祭昊天於圓丘，六也。

translations.literal: It also does not speak of sacrificing August Heaven at the round mound—six.
translations.idiomatic: It too says nothing of August Heaven at the round mound—sixth.

sentences.zh: 《家語》云：「凡四代帝王之所郊，皆以配天也。

translations.literal: Family Sayings: "All four dynasties' kings' suburban sacrifices all used consort with Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Family Sayings: "All four dynasties' suburban sacrifices consorted with Heaven."

sentences.zh: 其所謂禘者，皆五年大祭也。

translations.literal: What they call di are all five-year great sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: What they call di are five-year great sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 」又不言祭昊天於圓丘，七也。

translations.literal: It also does not speak of sacrificing August Heaven at the round mound—seven.
translations.idiomatic: It too says nothing of August Heaven at the round mound—seventh.

sentences.zh: 盧植云：「禘，祭名。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi said: "Di—a name of sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi said: "Di is a sacrifice name."

sentences.zh: 禘者諦也，事尊明諦，故曰禘。

translations.literal: Di means 'to clarify'; serving the honored with clear understanding, therefore called di.
translations.idiomatic: Di means 'to clarify'; serving the honored clearly, hence di.

sentences.zh: 」又不言祭昊天於圓丘，八也。

translations.literal: It also does not speak of sacrificing August Heaven at the round mound—eight.
translations.idiomatic: It too says nothing of August Heaven at the round mound—eighth.

sentences.zh: 王肅云：「禘謂於五年大祭之時。

translations.literal: Wang Su said: "Di refers to the time of the five-year great sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su said: "Di refers to the five-year great sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 」又不言祭昊天於圓丘，九也。

translations.literal: It also does not speak of sacrificing August Heaven at the round mound—nine.
translations.idiomatic: It too says nothing of August Heaven at the round mound—ninth.

sentences.zh: 郭璞云：「禘，五年之大祭。

translations.literal: Guo Pu said: "Di—the five-year great sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu said: "Di is the five-year great sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 」又不言祭昊天於圓丘，十也。

translations.literal: It also does not speak of sacrificing August Heaven at the round mound—ten.
translations.idiomatic: It too says nothing of August Heaven at the round mound—tenth.

sentences.zh: 臣幹謂禘是五年宗廟之大祭，《詩》、《禮》經傳，文義昭然。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that di is the five-year great sacrifice of the ancestral temple; in the Odes, Rites, classics, and traditions the meaning is brilliantly clear.
translations.idiomatic: Gan holds di is the ancestral temple's five-year great sacrifice; Odes, Rites, classics, and traditions make this clear.

sentences.zh: 今略舉十詰以明之。

translations.literal: Now I briefly offer ten interrogations to clarify it.
translations.idiomatic: I briefly offer ten interrogations to clarify it.

sentences.zh: 臣惟見《禮記·祭法》及《禮記·大傳》、《商頌·長髮》等三處鄭玄注，或稱祭昊天，或云祭靈威仰。

translations.literal: Your servant sees only in Record of Rites Sacrifice Law and Great Tradition and Shang Hymns Chang Fa three places Zheng Xuan's comment—sometimes saying sacrifice to August Heaven, sometimes sacrifice to Lingwei Yang.
translations.idiomatic: I find only three Zheng Xuan glosses—in Sacrifice Law, Great Tradition, and Chang Fa—sometimes August Heaven, sometimes Lingwei Yang.

sentences.zh: 臣精詳典籍，更無以禘為祭昊天於圓丘及郊祭天者。

translations.literal: Your servant has examined the canon in detail; nowhere else is di sacrifice to August Heaven at the round mound or suburb Heaven sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: I have examined the canon; nowhere else is di August Heaven at the round mound or suburb Heaven sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 審如禘是祭之最大，則孔子說《孝經》為萬代百王法，稱周公大孝，何不言禘祀帝嚳於圓丘以配天，而反言「郊祀後稷以配天？

translations.literal: If di is truly the greatest sacrifice, then when Confucius taught the Classic of Filial Piety as law for ten thousand generations and hundred kings, praising the Duke of Zhou's great filial piety, why did he not say di sacrifice to Emperor Ku at the round mound to consort with Heaven, but instead said "suburb sacrifice to Hou Ji to consort with Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: If di is the greatest sacrifice, why did Confucius, teaching the Classic of Filial Piety as eternal law and praising the Duke of Zhou's filial piety, not say di to Ku at the round mound to consort with Heaven, but "suburb sacrifice to Hou Ji to consort with Heaven?"

sentences.zh: 」是以《五經》俱無其說，聖人所以不言。

translations.literal: Thus the Five Classics all lack that doctrine—the sage therefore did not speak it.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Classics lack that doctrine—the sage did not speak it.

sentences.zh: 輕議大典，亦何容易。

translations.literal: To lightly discuss the great canon is also how rash!
translations.idiomatic: To lightly dispute the great canon is rash indeed.

sentences.zh: 猶恐不悟，今更作十難。

translations.literal: Fearing they still do not understand, I now further make ten refutations.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing they still misunderstand, I add ten refutations.

sentences.zh: 其一難曰：《周頌》：「《雍》，禘祭太祖也。

translations.literal: The first refutation: Zhou Hymns: "Yong—di sacrifice to the Grand Ancestor."
translations.idiomatic: First refutation: Zhou Hymns: "Yong—di to the Grand Ancestor."

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄箋云：「禘，大祭。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan's commentary says: "Di—great sacrifice. Grand Ancestor—King Wen."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan's commentary: "Di—great sacrifice. Grand Ancestor—King Wen."

sentences.zh: 太祖，文王也。

translations.literal: Grand Ancestor—King Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Ancestor is King Wen.

sentences.zh: 」《商頌》云：「《長髮》，大禘也。

translations.literal: Shang Hymns say: "Chang Fa—a great di."
translations.idiomatic: Shang Hymns: "Chang Fa—a great di."

sentences.zh: 」玄又箋云：「大禘，祭天也。

translations.literal: Xuan again comments: "Great di—sacrifice to Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Xuan again: "Great di—sacrifice to Heaven."

sentences.zh: 」夫商、周之《頌》，其文互說。

translations.literal: The Shang and Zhou hymns' texts explain each other—sometimes saying di to Grand Ancestor, sometimes great di—both are the five-year great sacrifice of the ancestral temple; examining the canon in detail, there is no other difference.
translations.idiomatic: Shang and Zhou hymns explain each other—di to Grand Ancestor or great di—both are the temple's five-year great sacrifice; the canon shows no other sense.

sentences.zh: 或云禘太祖，或云大禘，俱是五年宗廟之大祭，詳覽典籍，更無異同。

translations.literal: Sometimes di to Grand Ancestor, sometimes great di—all are the five-year great sacrifice of the ancestral temple; examining the canon in detail, there is no other difference.
translations.idiomatic: Whether di to Grand Ancestor or great di, both are the temple's five-year great sacrifice—the canon admits no other reading.

sentences.zh: 惟鄭玄箋《長髮》，乃稱是郊祭天。

translations.literal: Only in Zheng Xuan's commentary on Chang Fa does he call it suburb sacrifice to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Only in Zheng Xuan's Chang Fa commentary does he call it suburb Heaven sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 詳玄之意，因此《商頌》禘如《大傳》雲大祭，如《春秋》「大事於太廟」，《爾雅》「禘大祭」，雖雲大祭，亦是宗廟之祭，可得便稱祭天乎？
