translations.literal: Examining Xuan's intent in detail: because this Shang hymn's di, like the Great Tradition's saying great sacrifice, like the Spring and Autumn's "great affair in the Grand Temple," like Erya's "di—great sacrifice"—though it says great sacrifice, it is also ancestral-temple sacrifice; can one readily call it sacrifice to Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's intent: because Chang Fa's di, like "great sacrifice" in the Great Tradition, "great affair in the Grand Temple" in Spring and Autumn, and Erya's "di—great sacrifice," is temple sacrifice despite "great"—can one call it Heaven sacrifice?

sentences.zh: 若如所說，大禘即雲郊祭天，稱禘即是祭宗廟。

translations.literal: If as he says great di means suburb sacrifice to Heaven, then calling di means ancestral-temple sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: If great di means suburb Heaven sacrifice, then di means temple sacrifice—by his own logic.

sentences.zh: 又《祭法》說虞、夏、商、周禘黃帝與嚳，《大傳》「不王不禘」，禘上俱無大字，玄何因復稱祭天乎？

translations.literal: Moreover Sacrifice Law lists You, Xia, Shang, and Zhou di to Huangdi and Ku; Great Tradition "not king, not di"—above di there is no great character; why does Xuan again call it Heaven sacrifice?
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice Law lists You, Xia, Shang, and Zhou di to Huangdi and Ku; "not king, not di" has no "great" above di—why does Xuan again call it Heaven sacrifice?

sentences.zh: 又《長髮》文亦不歌嚳與感生帝，故知《長髮》之禘，而非禘嚳及郊祭天明矣。

translations.literal: Moreover Chang Fa's text does not sing Ku and the birth-feeling emperor; thus one knows Chang Fa's di is not di to Ku and suburb Heaven sacrifice—clear.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Fa does not sing Ku or the birth-feeling emperor—so its di is not di to Ku or suburb Heaven sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 殷、周五帝之大祭，群經眾史及鴻儒碩學，自古立言著論，序之詳矣，俱無以禘為祭天。

translations.literal: Yin and Zhou's great sacrifices to the Five Emperors—in all classics, histories, and great Confucian scholars' writings from antiquity, ordered in detail, all lack taking di as Heaven sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and Zhou great sacrifices to the Five Emperors—in all classics, histories, and great scholars from antiquity—none take di as Heaven sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 何棄周、孔之法言，獨取康成之小注，便欲違經非聖，誣亂祀典，謬哉！

translations.literal: Why abandon Zhou and Confucius' law-words and alone take Zheng Kangcheng's small comment, wishing to violate the classics and slander the sages, confusing and overturning the sacrifice canon—how erroneous!
translations.idiomatic: Why abandon Zhou and Confucius for Zheng Kangcheng's minor gloss, violate the classics, slander the sages, and overturn the sacrifice canon—how wrong!

sentences.zh: 其二難曰：《大傳》稱「禮，不王不禘，王者禘其祖之所自出，以其祖配之，諸侯及其太祖」者，此說王者則當禘。

translations.literal: The second refutation: the Great Tradition says "Rites: not king, not di; a king di to the ancestor from whom his line issued, with that ancestor as consort, and feudal lords to their Grand Ancestor"—this explains when one is king one should di.
translations.idiomatic: Second refutation: the Great Tradition's "not king, not di; a king di to the ancestor from whom his line issued, with that ancestor as consort; feudal lords to their Grand Ancestor" explains when a king should di.

sentences.zh: 其謂《祭法》，虞、夏、殷、周禘黃帝及嚳，「不王則不禘，所當禘其祖之所自出」，謂虞、夏出黃帝，殷、周出帝嚳，以近祖配而祭之。

translations.literal: Regarding Sacrifice Law—You, Xia, Yin, and Zhou di to Huangdi and Ku—"not king, not di; one should di to the ancestor from whom one's line issued" means You and Xia issued from Huangdi, Yin and Zhou from Emperor Ku, sacrificing with the near ancestor as consort.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice Law's You, Xia, Yin, and Zhou di to Huangdi and Ku: "not king, not di" means di to the line's issuing ancestor—You and Xia from Huangdi, Yin and Zhou from Ku, with the near ancestor as consort.

sentences.zh: 自出之祖，既無宗廟，即是自外至者，故同之天地神祇，以祖配而祀之。

translations.literal: The issuing ancestor, having no temple of his own, came from outside; therefore like Heaven-Earth spirits, sacrifice with the ancestor as consort.
translations.idiomatic: The issuing ancestor, without his own temple, came from outside—like Heaven and Earth spirits, sacrifice with the ancestor as consort.

sentences.zh: 自出之說，非但于父，在母亦然。

translations.literal: The doctrine of "issuing" is not only through the father; it applies to the mother as well.
translations.idiomatic: "Issuing" applies through the mother as well as the father.

sentences.zh: 《左傳》子產云：「陳則我周之自出。

translations.literal: The Zuo Tradition: Zichan said: "Chen is our Zhou's issuing."
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Tradition: Zichan said: "Chen is our Zhou's issuing."

sentences.zh: 」此可得稱出於太微五帝乎？

translations.literal: Can this be called issuing from the Supreme Palace Five Emperors?
translations.idiomatic: Can this mean issuing from the Supreme Palace Five Emperors?

sentences.zh: 故曰「不王不禘，王者禘其祖之所自出，以其祖配之」，此之謂也。

translations.literal: Thus "not king, not di; a king di to the ancestor from whom his line issued, with that ancestor as consort"—this is the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Thus "not king, not di; a king di to the ancestor from whom his line issued, with that ancestor as consort" means this.

sentences.zh: 及諸侯之禘，則降于王者，不得祭自出之祖，只及太祖而已。

translations.literal: For feudal lords' di it is reduced below kings—they cannot sacrifice to the issuing ancestor, reaching only the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Feudal lords' di ranks below kings—they cannot sacrifice to the issuing ancestor, only the Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 故曰「諸侯及其太祖」，此之謂也。

translations.literal: Thus "feudal lords to their Grand Ancestor"—this is the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Thus "feudal lords to their Grand Ancestor" means this.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄錯亂，分禘為三：注《祭法》雲「禘謂祭昊天於圓丘」，一也。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan confused and divided di into three: commenting Sacrifice Law "di means sacrifice to August Heaven at the round mound"—one.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan split di into three: Sacrifice Law "di means August Heaven at the round mound"—first.

sentences.zh: 注《大傳》稱「郊祭天，以後稷配靈威仰」，箋《商頌》又稱「郊祭天」，二也。

translations.literal: Commenting Great Tradition "suburb sacrifice to Heaven with Hou Ji consorting with Lingwei Yang"; commenting Shang Hymns again "suburb sacrifice to Heaven"—two.
translations.idiomatic: Great Tradition "suburb Heaven with Hou Ji consorting Lingwei Yang"; Shang Hymns again "suburb Heaven"—second.

sentences.zh: 注《周頌》雲「禘大祭，大於四時之祭，而小於祫，太祖謂文王」，三也。

translations.literal: Commenting Zhou Hymns "di—great sacrifice, greater than the four seasons' sacrifices but lesser than cha; Grand Ancestor means King Wen"—three.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Hymns "di—great sacrifice, greater than seasonal sacrifices but lesser than cha; Grand Ancestor is King Wen"—third.

sentences.zh: 禘是一祭，玄析之為三，顛倒錯亂，皆率胸臆，曾無典據，何足可憑。

translations.literal: Di is one sacrifice; Xuan analyzed it into three, inverted and confused—all from his breast, never from canon; how can it be relied on?
translations.idiomatic: Di is one sacrifice; Xuan made three, inverted and confused—all invention, no canon—unreliable.

sentences.zh: 其三難曰：虞、夏、殷、周已前，禘祖之所自出，其義昭然。

translations.literal: The third refutation: before You, Xia, Yin, and Zhou, di to the ancestor from whom the line issued—the meaning is brilliantly clear.
translations.idiomatic: Third refutation: before You, Xia, Yin, and Zhou, di to the issuing ancestor is clear.

sentences.zh: 自漢、魏、晉已還千餘歲，其禮遂闕。

translations.literal: From Han, Wei, and Jin onward for more than a thousand years the rite was wanting.
translations.idiomatic: From Han, Wei, and Jin onward for a thousand years the rite lapsed.

sentences.zh: 又鄭玄所說，其言不經，先儒棄之，未曾行用。

translations.literal: Moreover what Zheng Xuan said is uncanonical; former scholars discarded it and never practiced it.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan's words are uncanonical; former scholars discarded them and never used them.

sentences.zh: 愚以為錯亂之義，廢棄之注，不足以正大典。

translations.literal: I hold that confused meanings and discarded comments cannot rectify the great canon.
translations.idiomatic: Confused glosses and discarded comments cannot rectify the great canon.

sentences.zh: 其四難曰：所稱今《三禮》行於代者，皆是鄭玄之學，請據鄭學以明之。

translations.literal: The fourth refutation: what is called the Three Rites practiced in the age all is Zheng Xuan's learning—I request relying on Zheng's learning to clarify.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth refutation: the Three Rites in use are all Zheng Xuan's school—I ask to test by Zheng's own teaching.

sentences.zh: 曰雖雲據鄭學，今欲以景皇帝為始祖之廟以配天，復與鄭義相乖。

translations.literal: Though it says relying on Zheng's learning, now wishing the Jing Emperor as founding ancestor's temple to consort with Heaven again departs from Zheng's meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Though citing Zheng, making Emperor Jing founding ancestor to consort with Heaven departs from Zheng's meaning.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 《王制》云：「天子七廟。

translations.literal: Royal Regulations say: "The Son of Heaven has seven temples."
translations.idiomatic: Royal Regulations: "The Son of Heaven has seven temples."

sentences.zh: 」玄云：「此周禮也。

translations.literal: Xuan said: "This is Zhou rite."
translations.idiomatic: Xuan: this is Zhou rite.

sentences.zh: 」七廟者，太祖及文、武之祧與親廟四也。

translations.literal: Seven temples: Grand Ancestor and the shrines of Wen and Wu with four intimate temples.
translations.idiomatic: Seven temples: Grand Ancestor, Wen and Wu shrines, and four intimate temples.

sentences.zh: 殷則六廟，契及湯與二昭二穆也。

translations.literal: Yin had six temples—Qi and Tang with two zhao and two mu.
translations.idiomatic: Yin had six—Qi and Tang with two zhao and two mu.

sentences.zh: 據鄭學，夏不以鯀及顓頊、昌意為始祖，昭然可知也。

translations.literal: Per Zheng's learning, Xia did not take Gun, Zhuanxu, Changyi, and the like as founding ancestors—clearly knowable.
translations.idiomatic: Per Zheng, Xia did not take Gun, Zhuanxu, or Changyi as founding ancestors—this is clear.

sentences.zh: 而欲引稷、契為例，其義又異是。

translations.literal: Yet wishing to cite Hou Ji and Qi as examples—the meaning again differs.
translations.idiomatic: Yet citing Hou Ji and Qi as examples—the meaning differs.

sentences.zh: 爰稽邃古洎今，無以人臣為始祖者，惟殷以契，周以稷。

translations.literal: Tracing from remote antiquity to the present, none take a subject-minister as founding ancestor—only Yin with Qi, Zhou with Ji.
translations.idiomatic: From remote antiquity to the present none take a subject as founding ancestor—only Yin with Qi, Zhou with Ji.

sentences.zh: 夫稷、契者，皆天子元妃之子，感神而生。

translations.literal: Hou Ji and Qi were both sons of the Son of Heaven's primary consort, born from feeling the spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Ji and Qi were sons of the primary consort, born from feeling the spirit.

sentences.zh: 昔帝嚳次妃簡狄，有戎氏之女，吞玄鳥之卵，因生契。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Ku's secondary consort Jiandi, a woman of the Youreng clan, swallowed the dark bird's egg and thereby bore Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ku's secondary consort Jiandi of Youreng swallowed the dark bird's egg and bore Qi.

sentences.zh: 契長而佐禹治水，有大功。

translations.literal: When Qi grew he assisted Yu in controlling water and had great merit.
translations.idiomatic: Qi grew up assisting Yu in flood control with great merit.

sentences.zh: 舜乃命契作司徒，百姓既和，遂封于商。

translations.literal: Shun then ordered Qi as Minister of the Masses; when the hundred clans were harmonious, he was enfeoffed at Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Shun made Qi Minister of the Masses; when the clans were harmonious, Qi was enfeoffed at Shang.

sentences.zh: 故《詩》曰：「天命玄鳥，降而生商，宅殷土芒芒。

translations.literal: Thus the Odes say: "Heaven ordered the dark bird; it descended and bore Shang; it dwelt in the vast Yin soil."
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say: "Heaven ordered the dark bird; it descended and bore Shang; it dwelt in vast Yin soil."

sentences.zh: 」此之謂也。

translations.literal: This is the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: That is the sense.

sentences.zh: 後稷者，其母有邰氏之女曰薑嫄，為帝嚳妃，出野履巨跡，歆然有孕，生稷。

translations.literal: Hou Ji: his mother was a woman of the Youtai clan named Jiang Yuan, consort of Emperor Ku; going into the wild she trod a great footprint, was moved and became pregnant, and bore Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Ji's mother was Youtai clanswoman Jiang Yuan, consort of Emperor Ku; in the wild she trod a great footprint, conceived, and bore Ji.

sentences.zh: 稷長而勤於稼穡，堯聞，舉為農師，天下得其利，有大功，舜封于邰，號曰後稷。

translations.literal: When Ji grew up he was diligent in farming and planting; Yao heard of it and appointed him Agricultural Master; all under Heaven gained benefit—he had great merit; Shun enfeoffed him at Tai and styled him Hou Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Ji grew diligent in field and furrow; Yao heard and made him Agricultural Master. The realm profited—great was his merit. Shun enfeoffed him at Tai and named him Hou Ji.

sentences.zh: 唐、虞、夏之際，皆有令德。

translations.literal: In the age of Tang, Yu, and Xia, each possessed eminent virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In the age of Tang, Yu, and Xia, each bore eminent virtue.

sentences.zh: 故《詩》曰：「履帝武敏歆，居然生子，即有邰家室。

translations.literal: Thus the Odes says: "She trod the great god's footprint and was moved; she bore a child, and there was the house of Tai."
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Odes: "She trod the great god's footprint and was moved; she bore a child—and there was the house of Tai."

sentences.zh: 」此之謂也。

translations.literal: " This is what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: " So it is meant.

sentences.zh: 舜、禹有天下，稷、契在其間，量功比德，抑其次也。

translations.literal: When Shun and Yu held all under Heaven, Ji and Qi were among them; weighing merit and comparing virtue, they were rather second rank.
translations.idiomatic: Shun and Yu held the realm; Ji and Qi stood among them—by merit and virtue, rather second rank.

sentences.zh: 舜授職，則播百穀，敷五教。

translations.literal: When Shun invested them with office, Qi sowed the hundred grains and spread the Five Teachings.
translations.idiomatic: Shun gave them office: Qi sowed the hundred grains and spread the Five Teachings.

sentences.zh: 禹讓功，則平水土，宅百揆。

translations.literal: When Yu yielded merit, he leveled water and earth and settled the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu yielded the merit, he leveled water and earth and took charge of the hundred offices.

sentences.zh: 故《國語》曰：「聖人之制祀也，功施於人則祀之，以死勤事則祀之。

translations.literal: Thus the Discourses of the States says: "When the sage instituted sacrifice, if merit was bestowed upon the people then he sacrificed to them; if one died in diligent service then he sacrificed to them."
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Discourses: "The sage made sacrifice—whoever bestowed merit on the people was sacrificed to; whoever died in diligent service was sacrificed to."

sentences.zh: 」契為司徒而人輯睦，稷勤百穀而死，皆居前代祀典，子孫有天下，得不尊而祖之乎？

translations.literal: " Qi was Minister of Education and the people were harmonious; Ji labored over the hundred grains and died—both stood in the sacrificial canon of former ages; when their descendants held all under Heaven, could they fail to honor and take them as ancestors?
translations.idiomatic: " Qi as Minister of Education made the people harmonious; Ji labored over the hundred grains unto death—both stood in the sacrificial canon of former ages. When their line held the realm, could they fail to honor them as ancestors?

sentences.zh: 其五難曰：既遵鄭說，小德配寡，遂以後稷只配一帝，尚不得全配五帝。

translations.literal: The fifth objection says: Having followed Zheng's doctrine, minor virtue pairs with few—thus Hou Ji pairs with only one Thearch and still cannot fully pair with the Five Thearchs.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth objection: Following Zheng's doctrine, minor virtue pairs with few—Hou Ji pairs with only one Thearch and cannot fully pair with the Five.

sentences.zh: 今以景皇帝特配昊天，于鄭義可乎？

translations.literal: Now to have the Jing Emperor pair solely with August Heaven—is that permissible in Zheng's meaning?
translations.idiomatic: To pair the Jing Emperor solely with August Heaven—is that allowed in Zheng's doctrine?

sentences.zh: 其六難曰：眾難臣云：「上帝與五帝，一也。

translations.literal: The sixth objection says: Those who object to me say: "The High God and the Five Thearchs are one."
translations.idiomatic: The sixth objection: My opponents say, "The High God and the Five Thearchs are one."

sentences.zh: 所引《春官》：祀天旅上帝，祀地旅四望。

translations.literal: They cite the Offices of Spring: "In sacrificing to Heaven, marshal the High God; in sacrificing to Earth, marshal the Four Quarters."
translations.idiomatic: They cite the Offices of Spring: "Sacrificing to Heaven, marshal the High God; sacrificing to Earth, marshal the Four Quarters."

sentences.zh: 旅訓眾，則上帝是五帝。

translations.literal: "Marshal" means "the multitude"—thus the High God is the Five Thearchs.
translations.idiomatic: "Marshal" means multitude—therefore the High God is the Five Thearchs.

sentences.zh: 臣曰，不然。

translations.literal: I say: Not so.
translations.idiomatic: I say: That is not so.

sentences.zh: 旅雖訓眾，出於《爾雅》，及為祭名，《春官》訓陳，注有明文。

translations.literal: Though "marshal" does mean multitude, that comes from the Erya; as a name for sacrifice, the Offices of Spring gloss it as "array," and the commentary has explicit text.
translations.idiomatic: Though "marshal" means multitude in the Erya, as a sacrificial term the Offices of Spring glosses it "array"—the commentary is explicit.

sentences.zh: 若如所言，旅上帝便成五帝，則季氏旅于泰山，可得便是四鎮耶？

translations.literal: If as they say marshaling the High God becomes the Five Thearchs, then when the Ji clan marshaled at Mount Tai, could that mean the Four Guardians?
translations.idiomatic: If marshaling the High God means the Five Thearchs, then when the Ji clan "marshaled" at Mount Tai—was that the Four Guardians?

sentences.zh: 其七難曰：所雲據鄭學，則景皇帝親盡，廟主合祧，卻欲配祭天地，錯亂祖宗。

translations.literal: The seventh objection says: They claim to rely on Zheng's learning—yet the Jing Emperor's kinship is exhausted, temple tablets are merged in the collective shrine, and they still wish him to pair in sacrifice to Heaven and Earth, disordering ancestors and forbears.
translations.idiomatic: The seventh objection: By Zheng's learning the Jing Emperor's kinship is exhausted and tablets merged—yet they would have him pair with Heaven and Earth, disordering the ancestral line.

sentences.zh: 夫始祖者，經綸草昧，體大則天，所以正元氣廣大，萬物之宗尊，以長至陽氣萌動之始日，俱祀於南郊也。

translations.literal: The founding ancestor is he who brought order in the primal chaos, whose substance is great and matches Heaven; therefore to rectify the primordial qi's vastness and the veneration of all things' origin, on the day when yang qi first stirs at the summer solstice, both are sacrificed at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: The founding ancestor brought order from primal chaos—his substance vast as Heaven. To rectify primordial qi and honor the origin of all things, on the day yang first stirs at summer solstice, both are sacrificed at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 夫萬物之始，天也。

translations.literal: The beginning of all things is Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: All things begin with Heaven.

sentences.zh: 人之始，祖也。

translations.literal: The beginning of man is the ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Man begins with the ancestor.

sentences.zh: 日之始，至也。

translations.literal: The beginning of the day is the solstice.
translations.idiomatic: The day begins at the solstice.

sentences.zh: 掃地而祭，質也。

translations.literal: Sweeping the ground to sacrifice is simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: To sweep the ground and sacrifice is simplicity.

sentences.zh: 器用陶匏，性也。

translations.literal: Using pottery and gourds for vessels is nature.
translations.idiomatic: Pottery and gourds for vessels is nature.

sentences.zh: 牲用犢，誠也。

translations.literal: Using calves for victims is sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Calves for victims is sincerity.

sentences.zh: 兆于南郊，就陽位也。

translations.literal: Establishing the altar at the southern suburb is taking the yang position.
translations.idiomatic: The altar at the southern suburb takes the yang position.

sentences.zh: 至尊至質，不敢同于先祖，禮也。

translations.literal: Most exalted, most simple—daring not to be the same as former ancestors: that is ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Most exalted, most simple—daring not share rites with former ancestors: that is ritual.

sentences.zh: 故《白虎通》曰：「祭天歲一，何？

translations.literal: Thus the Comprehensive Discussions on the White Tiger says: "Sacrifice to Heaven once a year—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Comprehensive Discussions: "Sacrifice to Heaven once a year—why?"

sentences.zh: 天至尊至質，事之不敢褻黷，故因歲之陽氣始達而祭之。

translations.literal: "Heaven is most exalted and most simple; in serving it one dares not be irreverent or excessive—therefore one sacrifices when the year's yang qi first reaches forth."
translations.idiomatic: "Heaven is most exalted and most simple; one dares not treat it lightly—therefore sacrifice when the year's yang qi first reaches forth."

sentences.zh: 」今國家一歲四祭之，黷莫大焉。

translations.literal: " Now the state sacrifices four times a year—no excess could be greater.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet the state now sacrifices four times a year—no excess could be greater.

sentences.zh: 上帝、五帝，其祀遂闕，怠亦甚矣。

translations.literal: Sacrifice to the High God and the Five Thearchs is thereby neglected—negligence is also extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice to the High God and the Five Thearchs is neglected—negligence is also extreme.

sentences.zh: 黷與怠，皆禮之失，不可不知。

translations.literal: Excess and negligence are both failures of ritual—not to be unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Excess and negligence are both ritual failures—not to be ignored.

sentences.zh: 夫親有限，祖有常，聖人制禮，君子不以情變易。

translations.literal: Kinship has limits; ancestors have constants—the sage made ritual, and the gentleman does not alter it for emotion.
translations.idiomatic: Kinship has limits; ancestors have constants—the sage made ritual; the gentleman does not alter it for feeling.

sentences.zh: 國家重光累聖，曆祀百數，豈不知景皇帝始封于唐。

translations.literal: The state has renewed glory through successive sages, with sacrifices numbering in the hundreds—how could it not know that the Jing Emperor was first enfeoffed in Tang?
translations.idiomatic: The state has renewed glory through successive sages, sacrifices numbering in the hundreds—how could it not know the Jing Emperor was first enfeoffed in Tang?

sentences.zh: 當時通儒議功度德，尊神堯克配彼天，宗太宗以配上帝。

translations.literal: At that time thorough scholars weighed merit and measured virtue, honored Shenyao as fit to pair with that Heaven, and took Taizong as cult-ancestor to pair with the High God.
translations.idiomatic: Then thorough scholars weighed merit and virtue: Shenyao was honored fit to pair with Heaven; Taizong was cult-ancestor to pair with the High God.

sentences.zh: 神有定主，為日已久。

translations.literal: The spirits have fixed lords—it has been so long.
translations.idiomatic: The spirits have had fixed lords for a very long time.

sentences.zh: 今欲黜神堯配含樞紐，乙太宗配上帝，則紫微五精，上帝佐也，以子先父，豈禮意乎！

translations.literal: Now wishing to demote Shenyao to pair with the Pivot of Heaven, and elevate Taizong to pair with the High God—the Purple Palace's five essences are assistants to the High God; to put the son before the father—how is that ritual's intent!
translations.idiomatic: Now to demote Shenyao to pair with the Pivot of Heaven and elevate Taizong to the High God—the five essences of the Purple Palace assist the High God; the son before the father—how is that ritual's intent!

sentences.zh: 非止神祇錯位，亦以祖宗乖序，何以上稱皇天祖宗之意哉！

translations.literal: It is not only that the spirits are misplaced—ancestors too are out of order; how could one answer to the intent of August Heaven and the ancestors!
translations.idiomatic: Not only are the spirits misplaced—ancestors are out of order. How answer to August Heaven and the ancestors!

sentences.zh: 若夫神堯之功，太宗之德，格於皇天上帝，臣以為郊祀宗祀，無以加焉。

translations.literal: As for Shenyao's merit and Taizong's virtue, reaching August Heaven and the High God—in my view suburban and ancestral sacrifice cannot add to them.
translations.idiomatic: Shenyao's merit and Taizong's virtue reach August Heaven and the High God—in my view suburban and ancestral rites cannot add to them.

sentences.zh: 其八難曰：欲以景皇帝為始祖，既非造我區宇，經綸草昧之主，故非夏始祖禹、殷始祖契、周始祖稷、漢始祖高帝、魏始祖武皇帝、晉始祖宣帝、國家始祖神堯皇帝同功比德，而忽升于宗祀圓丘之上，為昊天匹，曾謂圓丘不如林放乎？

translations.literal: The eighth objection says: Wishing to make the Jing Emperor the founding ancestor—yet he is not the lord who made our realm and brought order in primal chaos—therefore he is not of the same merit and virtue as Xia's founding ancestor Yu, Shang's founding ancestor Qi, Zhou's founding ancestor Ji, Han's founding ancestor the High Emperor, Wei's founding ancestor the Martial Emperor, Jin's founding ancestor the August Emperor, or our state's founding ancestor the Shenyao Emperor; yet suddenly to raise him upon the round hill of ancestral cult as August Heaven's peer—did the round hill mean less than Lin Fang?
translations.idiomatic: The eighth objection: To make the Jing Emperor founding ancestor—yet he did not forge our realm from primal chaos—he is not Yu, Qi, Ji, the High Emperor, Cao Cao, Sima Yi, or Shenyao in merit. Yet suddenly to raise him on the round hill as August Heaven's peer—was the round hill less than Lin Fang?

sentences.zh: 其九難曰：昨所言魏文帝丕以武帝操為始祖，晉武帝炎以宣帝懿為始祖者。

translations.literal: The ninth objection says: What was said yesterday—that Wei Emperor Wen Pi took Emperor Wu Cao as founding ancestor, and Jin Emperor Wu Yan took Emperor Xuan Yi as founding ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: The ninth objection: Yesterday's point—that Wei Wen took Wu Cao as founding ancestor, Jin Wu took Xuan Yi as founding ancestor.

sentences.zh: 夫孟德、仲達者，皆人傑也。

translations.literal: Mengde and Zhongda were both towering men.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao and Sima Yi were both men of towering stature.

sentences.zh: 擁天下之強兵，挾漢、魏之微主，專制海內，令行草偃，服袞冕，陳軒懸，天子決事于私第，公卿列拜于道左，名雖為臣，勢實淩君。

translations.literal: They held the realm's strong armies, held Han and Wei's feeble lords in their grasp, monopolized power within the seas, commands ran like wind over grass, they wore imperial robes and displayed suspended bells—the Son of Heaven decided affairs in their private quarters, dukes and ministers lined up to bow at the roadside; in name they were subjects, in power they truly overawed their lord.
translations.idiomatic: They held the realm's armies, clutched Han and Wei's feeble lords, monopolized the seas—commands ran like wind over grass; they wore imperial robes, displayed suspended bells; the Son of Heaven decided affairs in their private halls, ministers bowed in the road. In name subjects—in power they overawed their lord.

sentences.zh: 後主因之而業帝，前王由之而禪代，子孫尊而祖之，不亦可乎？

translations.literal: Later rulers thereby achieved the imperial enterprise; former kings thereby received abdication—their descendants honor and take them as ancestors—is that not permissible?
translations.idiomatic: Later rulers thereby became emperors; former kings abdicated to them—their descendants honor them as ancestors—is that not permissible?

sentences.zh: 其十難曰：所引商、周、魏、晉，既不當矣，則景皇帝不為始祖明矣。

translations.literal: The tenth objection says: The Shang, Zhou, Wei, and Jin cited are already inapt—then it is clear the Jing Emperor is not a founding ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: The tenth objection: Shang, Zhou, Wei, and Jin are already inapt—the Jing Emperor is clearly not a founding ancestor.

sentences.zh: 我神堯拔出群雄之中，廓清隋室，拯生人於塗炭，則夏禹之勳不足多；

translations.literal: Our Shenyao drew forth from among contending heroes, cleared away the Sui house, and rescued the living from flood and fire—then Xia Yu's merit is not worth multiplying;
translations.idiomatic: Our Shenyao rose from contending heroes, cleared the Sui, rescued the living from flood and fire—Xia Yu's merit is not worth multiplying;

sentences.zh: 成帝業於數年之間，則漢祖之功不足比。

translations.literal: he completed the imperial enterprise within a few years—then the Han founder's merit is not worth comparing.
translations.idiomatic: he completed the imperial enterprise within a few years—the Han founder's merit is not worth comparing.

sentences.zh: 夏以大禹為始祖，漢以高帝為始祖，則我唐以神堯為始祖，法夏則漢，于義何嫌？

translations.literal: Xia took Great Yu as founding ancestor, Han took the High Emperor as founding ancestor—then our Tang takes Shenyao as founding ancestor; following Xia and Han, what objection in ritual?
translations.idiomatic: Xia took Yu, Han took the High Emperor—our Tang takes Shenyao; following Xia and Han, what ritual objection?

sentences.zh: 今欲革皇天之禮，易太祖之廟，事之大者，莫大于斯，曾無按據，一何寡陋，不愧於心，不畏於天乎！

translations.literal: Now wishing to alter August Heaven's ritual and change the Grand Ancestor's temple—of great affairs none is greater; yet there is no basis whatsoever—how shallow! No shame in the heart, no fear of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Now to alter August Heaven's ritual and change the Grand Ancestor's temple—of great affairs none is greater; yet no basis whatsoever—how shallow! No shame in the heart, no fear of Heaven?

sentences.zh: 以前奉詔，令諸司各據禮經定議者。

translations.literal: Previously I received an edict ordering each office to fix its deliberation according to the ritual classics.
translations.idiomatic: Previously I received an edict ordering each office to deliberate according to the ritual classics.

sentences.zh: 臣幹忝竊朝列，官以諫為名，以直見知，以學見達，不敢不罄竭以裨萬一。

translations.literal: I, Gan, unworthily hold a place in the court ranks; my office is named for remonstrance, known for forthrightness, accomplished in learning—I dare not fail to exhaust myself to aid the slightest measure.
translations.idiomatic: I, Gan, unworthily hold court rank; my office is named for remonstrance, known for forthrightness and learning—I dare not fail to exhaust myself for the slightest measure.

sentences.zh: 昨十四日，具以議狀呈宰相，宰相令朝臣與臣論難。

translations.literal: Yesterday, the fourteenth, I fully presented my deliberation to the chief ministers; the chief ministers ordered court officials to debate with me.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday, the fourteenth, I presented my deliberation to the chief ministers; they ordered court officials to debate with me.

sentences.zh: 所難臣者，以臣所見獨異，莫不勝辭飛辯，競欲碎臣理，鉗臣口。

translations.literal: Those who objected to me—because my view stood alone—none failed to triumph in words and fly in debate, each competing to shatter my reasoning and clamp my mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Those who objected—because my view stood alone—none failed to fly at debate, each competing to shatter my reasoning and clamp my mouth.

sentences.zh: 剖析毫釐，分別異同，序墳典之凝滯，指子傳之乖謬，事皆歸根，觸物不礙。

translations.literal: They parsed hair's breadths and distinguished sameness and difference, ordered the congealed passages of the classics, pointed to the errors of the masters' transmissions—every matter returned to its root; nothing encountered was blocked.
translations.idiomatic: They parsed hair's breadths, distinguished sameness and difference, ordered congealed passages of the classics, pointed to errors in the masters' transmissions—every matter returned to its root; nothing blocked them.

sentences.zh: 但臣言有宗爾，豈辯者之流也。

translations.literal: Yet my words have a lineage—how could I be of the debaters' sort!
translations.idiomatic: Yet my words have a lineage—I am not of the debaters' sort!

sentences.zh: 又歸崇敬、薛頎等援引鄭學，欲蕪祀典，臣為明辯，迷而不復。

translations.literal: Again Gui Chongjing, Xue Yi, and others cited Zheng's learning, wishing to overgrow the sacrificial canon; I made clear the debate, but they were lost and did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Again Gui Chongjing, Xue Yi, and others cited Zheng's learning to overgrow the sacrificial canon; I made clear the debate, but they were lost and did not return.

sentences.zh: 臣輒作十詰十難，援據墳籍，昭然可知。

translations.literal: I thereupon composed ten interrogations and ten objections, citing the classics and histories—it is plainly knowable.
translations.idiomatic: I composed ten interrogations and ten objections, citing classics and histories—it is plainly knowable.

sentences.zh: 庶郊禘事得其真，嚴配不失其序，皇靈降祉，天下蒙賴。

translations.literal: May suburban and di rites obtain their truth, solemn pairing not lose its order, the imperial numen send blessing, and all under Heaven receive the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: May suburban and di rites find their truth, solemn pairing keep its order, the imperial numen send blessing, and the realm receive the benefit.

sentences.zh: 臣亦何顧不蹈鼎鑊？

translations.literal: What would I not face—would I not tread the cauldron and seething pot?
translations.idiomatic: What would I not face—would I shrink from the cauldron and seething pot?

sentences.zh: 謹敢聞達，伏增悚越。

translations.literal: I respectfully dare report this; prostrate, I am ever more fearful and overwhelmed.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully report this; prostrate, I am ever more fearful and overwhelmed.

sentences.zh: 議奏，不報。

translations.literal: The deliberation was submitted; no response was given.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted; the throne did not reply.

sentences.zh: 至二年春夏旱。

translations.literal: By the second year, spring and summer brought drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year drought came in spring and summer.

sentences.zh: 言事者云：太祖景皇帝追封于唐，高祖實受命之祖，百神受職，合依高祖。

translations.literal: Memorialists said: The Grand Ancestor Jing Emperor was posthumously enfeoffed in Tang; the High Ancestor was truly the ancestor who received the Mandate—the hundred spirits received their offices; it should follow the High Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists said: The Grand Ancestor Jing Emperor was posthumously enfeoffed in Tang; the High Ancestor truly received the Mandate—the hundred spirits took office; rites should follow the High Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 今不得配享天地，所以神不降福，以致愆陽。

translations.literal: Now he cannot be paired in sacrifice to Heaven and Earth—therefore the spirits do not send blessing, and excess yang results.
translations.idiomatic: Now he cannot pair with Heaven and Earth—therefore the spirits send no blessing, and excess yang results.

sentences.zh: 代宗疑之，詔百僚會議。

translations.literal: Daizong was doubtful and ordered the hundred officials to convene in deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong was doubtful and ordered the hundred officials to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 太常博士獨孤及獻議曰：

translations.literal: Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Du Ji presented a deliberation, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Court of Imperial Sacrifices Erudite Du Ji presented a deliberation, saying:

sentences.zh: 禮，王者禘其祖之所自出，以其祖配之。

translations.literal: "Ritual: the king di-sacrifices to the ancestor from whom his line issued forth, and pairs his ancestor with him."
translations.idiomatic: "Ritual says: the king di-sacrifices to the ancestor from whom his line issued forth and pairs that ancestor with him."

sentences.zh: 凡受命始封之君，皆為太祖。

translations.literal: Every lord who received the Mandate at first enfeoffment is the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever received the Mandate at first enfeoffment is the Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 繼太祖已下六廟，則以親盡迭毀。

translations.literal: For the six temples below the Grand Ancestor, when kinship is exhausted they are destroyed in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Below the Grand Ancestor, six temples—when kinship is exhausted, they are destroyed in turn.

sentences.zh: 而太祖之廟，雖百代不遷。

translations.literal: But the Grand Ancestor's temple, though a hundred generations pass, is not moved.
translations.idiomatic: But the Grand Ancestor's temple is not moved though a hundred generations pass.

sentences.zh: 此五帝、三王所以尊祖敬宗也。

translations.literal: This is why the Five Thearchs and Three Kings honored ancestors and revered the cult-line.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Five Thearchs and Three Kings honored ancestors and revered the cult-line.

sentences.zh: 故受命于神宗，禹也，而夏後氏祖顓頊而郊鯀。

translations.literal: Thus receiving the Mandate from the Spirit Ancestor was Yu, yet the Xia honored Zhuanxu and suburban-sacrificed to Gun.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving the Mandate from the Spirit Ancestor was Yu—yet Xia honored Zhuanxu and suburban-sacrificed to Gun.

sentences.zh: 纘禹黜夏，湯也，而殷人郊冥而祖契。

translations.literal: Continuing Yu and deposing Xia was Tang, yet the Yin suburban-sacrificed to Ming and took Qi as cult-ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Continuing Yu and deposing Xia was Tang—yet Yin suburban-sacrificed to Ming and took Qi as cult-ancestor.

sentences.zh: 革命作周，武王也，而周人郊稷而祖文王。

translations.literal: Revolution made Zhou—King Wu—yet Zhou suburban-sacrificed to Ji and took King Wen as cult-ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: The revolution that made Zhou was King Wu—yet Zhou suburban-sacrificed to Ji and took King Wen as cult-ancestor.

sentences.zh: 則明自古必以首封之君，配昊天上帝。

translations.literal: Then it is clear that from antiquity the lord of first enfeoffment must pair with August Heaven the High God.
translations.idiomatic: Then it is clear: from antiquity the lord of first enfeoffment pairs with August Heaven the High God.

sentences.zh: 唯漢氏崛起豐沛，豐公太公，皆無位無功，不可以為祖宗，故漢以高皇帝為太祖，其先細微也。

translations.literal: Only the Han house rose from Feng and Pei—Duke Feng and Grand Duke Tai had neither rank nor merit and could not serve as ancestors; therefore Han took the High Emperor as Grand Ancestor; his forebears were slight.
translations.idiomatic: Only Han rose from Feng and Pei—Duke Feng and Grand Duke Tai had neither rank nor merit and could not be ancestors; Han took the High Emperor as Grand Ancestor; his forebears were slight.

sentences.zh: 非足為後代法。

translations.literal: It is not sufficient to be a model for later ages.
translations.idiomatic: That is not enough to serve as a model for later ages.

sentences.zh: 伏惟太祖景皇帝以柱國之任，翼周弼魏，肇啟王業，建封于唐。

translations.literal: I consider: the Grand Ancestor Jing Emperor, in the office of Pillar of State, aided Zhou and assisted Wei, first opened the royal enterprise, and was enfeoffed in Tang.
translations.idiomatic: I consider: Grand Ancestor Jing Emperor, as Pillar of State, aided Zhou and assisted Wei, first opened the royal enterprise, and was enfeoffed in Tang.

sentences.zh: 高祖因之，以為有天下之號，天所命也。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor followed upon this and took the title of holding all under Heaven—Heaven's command.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor followed and took the title of holding all under Heaven—Heaven's command.

sentences.zh: 亦如契之封商，後稷之封邰。

translations.literal: It is also like Qi's enfeoffment in Shang and Hou Ji's enfeoffment in Tai.
translations.idiomatic: It is like Qi's enfeoffment in Shang and Hou Ji's in Tai.

sentences.zh: 禘郊祖宗之位，宜在百代不遷之典。

translations.literal: The positions of di, suburb, cult, and ancestor should be in the canon that does not move for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: The positions of di, suburb, cult, and ancestor belong in the canon that does not move for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 郊祀太祖，宗祀高祖，猶周之祖文王而宗武王也。

translations.literal: Suburban sacrifice to the Grand Ancestor, cult-sacrifice to the High Ancestor—it is like Zhou taking King Wen as cult-ancestor and King Wu as cult-lord.
translations.idiomatic: Suburban sacrifice to the Grand Ancestor, cult-sacrifice to the High Ancestor—as Zhou took King Wen as cult-ancestor and King Wu as cult-lord.

sentences.zh: 今若以高祖創業，當躋其祀，是棄三代之令典，尊漢氏之末制，黜景皇帝之大業，同豐公太公之不祀，反古違道，失孰大焉？

translations.literal: Now if because the High Ancestor founded the enterprise one should elevate his cult, that is abandoning the fine canon of the Three Dynasties, honoring Han's late institution, demoting the Jing Emperor's great enterprise, and equaling Duke Feng and Grand Duke Tai's lack of sacrifice—reversing antiquity and violating the Way; what failure could be greater?
translations.idiomatic: Now to elevate the High Ancestor's cult because he founded the enterprise is to abandon the Three Dynasties' fine canon, honor Han's late institution, demote the Jing Emperor's great enterprise, and equal Duke Feng and Grand Duke Tai's lack of sacrifice—reversing antiquity; what failure could be greater?

sentences.zh: 夫追尊景皇，廟號太祖，高祖、太宗所以崇尊之禮也。

translations.literal: Posthumously honoring the Jing Emperor and temple-name Grand Ancestor—that is the rite by which the High Ancestor and Taizong showed lofty honor.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously honoring the Jing Emperor as Grand Ancestor—that is how the High Ancestor and Taizong showed lofty honor.

sentences.zh: 若配天之位既異，則太祖之號宜廢，祀之不修，廟亦當毀。

translations.literal: If the position of pairing with Heaven is already different, then the title Grand Ancestor should be abolished, sacrifice not maintained, and the temple also destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: If the position pairing with Heaven differs, the title Grand Ancestor should be abolished, sacrifice abandoned, the temple destroyed.

sentences.zh: 尊祖報本之道，其墜於地乎！

translations.literal: The Way of honoring ancestors and repaying origin—has it fallen to earth!
translations.idiomatic: The Way of honoring ancestors and repaying origin—will it fall to earth!

sentences.zh: 漢制，擅議宗廟，以大不敬論。

translations.literal: Han statute: presuming to deliberate the ancestral temples was judged great irreverence.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han law, presuming to debate the ancestral temples was great irreverence.

sentences.zh: 今武德、貞觀憲章未改，國家方將敬祀事，和神人，禘郊之間，恐非所宜。

translations.literal: Now the Wude and Zhenguan statutes are unaltered; the state is about to respectfully perform sacrifice and harmonize spirits and men—between di and suburb, perhaps it is not suitable.
translations.idiomatic: Wude and Zhenguan statutes stand unaltered; the state is about to sacrifice and harmonize spirits and men—between di and suburb, perhaps it is not suitable.

sentences.zh: 臣謹稽禮文，參諸往制，請仍舊典。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully examines ritual texts and compares former institutions, and asks that the old canon remain.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant examines ritual texts and former institutions and asks that the old canon remain.

sentences.zh: 竟依歸崇敬等議，以太祖配享天地。

translations.literal: In the end they followed Gui Chongjing and others' deliberation, taking the Grand Ancestor as paired in sacrifice to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: In the end they followed Gui Chongjing and others— the Grand Ancestor paired with Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 廣德二年正月十六日，禮儀使杜鴻漸奏：「郊、太廟，大禮，其祝文自今已後，請依唐禮，板上墨書。

translations.literal: On the sixteenth day of the first month of the second year of Guangde, Rites Commissioner Du Hongjian memorialized: "Suburban and Grand Temple rites are great ceremonies; from now on for prayer texts, please follow Tang ritual and write in ink on boards."
translations.idiomatic: Sixteenth day, first month, Guangde year 2: Rites Commissioner Du Hongjian memorialized: "Suburban and Grand Temple are great ceremonies; prayer texts hereafter should follow Tang ritual—ink on boards."

sentences.zh: 其玉簡金字者，一切停廢。

translations.literal: Jade slips with golden characters—all are to be discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: Jade slips with golden characters—all discontinued.

sentences.zh: 如允臣所奏，望編為常式。

translations.literal: "If Your Majesty approves my memorial, I hope it may be compiled as a standing regulation."
translations.idiomatic: "If approved, I hope it may be compiled as standing regulation."

sentences.zh: 」敕曰：「宜行用竹簡。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Bamboo slips should be used."
translations.idiomatic: The edict said: "Use bamboo slips."

translations.literal: The edict concluded."
translations.idiomatic: The edict closed.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年十一月十一日，德宗親祀南郊。

translations.literal: On the eleventh day of the eleventh month of the first year of Zhenyuan, Dezong personally sacrificed at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, eleventh day, Zhenyuan year 1: Dezong personally sacrificed at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 有司進圖，敕付禮官詳酌。

translations.literal: The relevant offices presented diagrams; an edict ordered them delivered to ritual officials for detailed deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices presented diagrams; an edict ordered ritual officials to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 博士柳冕奏曰：「開元定禮，垂之不刊。

translations.literal: Erudite Liu Mian memorialized, saying: "The Kaiyuan fixed ritual is engraved and shall not be altered."
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Liu Mian memorialized: "The Kaiyuan fixed ritual is engraved and shall not be altered."

sentences.zh: 天寶改作，起自權制，此皆方士謬妄之說，非禮典之文，請一準《開元禮》。

translations.literal: "The Tianbao revisions arose from expedient regulation—these are all the wild sayings of masters of the methods, not texts of the ritual canon; I ask that everything follow the Kaiyuan Rites."
translations.idiomatic: "Tianbao revisions arose from expedient regulation—wild sayings of masters of the methods, not ritual canon; let all follow the Kaiyuan Rites."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " Approved.

sentences.zh: 其年十月二十七日，詔：「郊禮之議，本于至誠。

translations.literal: That year, the twenty-seventh day of the tenth month, an edict: "Deliberation on suburban rites rests upon utmost sincerity."
translations.idiomatic: That year, tenth month, twenty-seventh day, an edict: "Deliberation on suburban rites rests upon utmost sincerity."

sentences.zh: 制禮定名，合從事實，使名實相副，則尊卑有倫。

translations.literal: "Fixing ritual and fixing names should accord with the facts of the affair, so that name and fact match—then honor and baseness have order."
translations.idiomatic: "Fixing ritual and names should accord with facts, so name and fact match—then honor and baseness have order."

sentences.zh: 五方配帝，上古哲王，道濟烝人，禮著明祀。

translations.literal: "The Five Directions' paired Thearchs are sage kings of high antiquity; their Way succored the teeming people, their ritual is set forth in bright sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: "The Five Directions' paired Thearchs are sage kings of high antiquity whose Way succored the people—bright sacrifice records their ritual."

sentences.zh: 論善計功，則朕德不類，統天禦極，朕位攸同。

translations.literal: "Weighing goodness and reckoning merit, then my virtue is not of that sort; holding Heaven and standing at the pole, my position is the same."
translations.idiomatic: "Weighing goodness and merit, my virtue is not of that sort; holding Heaven and standing at the pole, my position is the same."

sentences.zh: 而于祝文稱臣以祭，既無益於誠敬，徒有瀆於等威。

translations.literal: "Yet in the prayer text to call myself subject in sacrifice benefits sincerity not at all—it only profanes rank and majesty."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet calling myself subject in the prayer text benefits sincerity not at all—it only profanes rank and majesty."

sentences.zh: 前京兆府司錄參軍高佩上疏陳請，其理精詳。

translations.literal: "Formerly Senior Recorder of the Capital Gao Pei memorialized with a request; his reasoning was refined and detailed."
translations.idiomatic: "Formerly Capital Senior Recorder Gao Pei memorialized; his reasoning was refined and detailed."

sentences.zh: 朕重變舊儀，訪於卿士，申明大義，是用釋然。

translations.literal: "I weighed altering the old rites and consulted you ministers; the great meaning was clarified—therefore I am released."
translations.idiomatic: "I weighed altering the old rites and consulted you ministers; the great meaning clarified—I am released."

sentences.zh: 宜從改正，以敦至禮。

translations.literal: "It is fitting to follow the correction and thereby thicken the utmost rite."
translations.idiomatic: "Follow the correction and thereby thicken the utmost rite."

sentences.zh: 自今已後，祀五方配帝祝文，並不須稱臣。

translations.literal: "From now on, in prayer texts for sacrifice to the Five Directions' paired Thearchs, none need call themselves subject."
translations.idiomatic: "Hereafter, prayer texts for the Five Directions' paired Thearchs need not call oneself subject."

sentences.zh: 其餘禮數如舊。

translations.literal: "The remaining ritual details are as before."
translations.idiomatic: "Remaining ritual details are as before."

translations.literal: The edict concluded."
translations.idiomatic: The edict closed.

sentences.zh: 六年十一月八日，有事於南郊。

translations.literal: On the eighth day of the eleventh month of the sixth year, there was an affair at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth year, eleventh month, eighth day: an affair at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 詔以皇太子為亞獻，親王為終獻。

translations.literal: An edict made the crown prince the secondary offerer and imperial princes the final offerers.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made the crown prince secondary offerer and imperial princes final offerers.

sentences.zh: 上問禮官：「亞獻、終獻合受誓誡否？

translations.literal: The emperor asked the ritual officials: "Should secondary and final offerers receive the oath and admonition?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked ritual officials: "Should secondary and final offerers receive the oath and admonition?"

sentences.zh: 」吏部郎中柳冕曰：「准《開元禮》，獻官前七日於內受誓誡。

translations.literal: " The Director of the Ministry of Civil Office Liu Mian said: "According to the Kaiyuan Rites, offering officials seven days before receive the oath and admonition within the palace."
translations.idiomatic: " Ministry of Civil Office Director Liu Mian said: "Per the Kaiyuan Rites, offering officials receive oath and admonition in the palace seven days before."

sentences.zh: 辭云：'各揚其職，不供其事，國有常刑。

translations.literal: The text says: "Each display his office; whoever does not supply his task—the state has constant punishment."
translations.idiomatic: The oath reads: "Each display his office; whoever fails his task—the state has fixed punishment."

sentences.zh: '今以皇太子為亞獻，請改舊辭，雲'各揚其職，肅奉常儀'。

translations.literal: "Now with the crown prince as secondary offerer, I ask to alter the old text to say: 'Each display his office; reverently uphold the constant rites.'"
translations.idiomatic: "With the crown prince as secondary offerer, I ask to alter the old text: 'Each display his office; reverently uphold the constant rites.'"

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " Approved.

sentences.zh: 十五年四月，術士匡彭祖上言：「大唐土德，千年合符，請每於四季月郊祀天地。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifteenth year, the adept Kuang Pengzu memorialized: "Great Tang's earth virtue—after a thousand years the tallies match; I ask that each season's month suburban-sacrifice Heaven and Earth."
translations.idiomatic: Fifteenth year, fourth month: adept Kuang Pengzu memorialized: "Great Tang's earth virtue—a thousand-year tally matches; suburban-sacrifice Heaven and Earth each season's month."

sentences.zh: 」詔禮官儒者議。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered ritual officials and Confucian scholars to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict ordered ritual officials and scholars to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 歸崇敬曰：「准禮，立春迎春於東郊，祭青帝。

translations.literal: Gui Chongjing said: "According to ritual, at the establishment of spring welcome spring at the eastern suburb and sacrifice to the Green Thearch."
translations.idiomatic: Gui Chongjing said: "Per ritual, at spring's establishment welcome spring at the eastern suburb and sacrifice to the Green Thearch."

sentences.zh: 立夏日迎夏於南郊，祭赤帝。

translations.literal: "At the establishment of summer welcome summer at the southern suburb and sacrifice to the Red Thearch."
translations.idiomatic: "At summer's establishment welcome summer at the southern suburb and sacrifice to the Red Thearch."

sentences.zh: 立秋後十八日，迎黃靈於中地，祭黃帝。

translations.literal: "Eighteen days after the establishment of autumn welcome the Yellow Spirit at the central ground and sacrifice to the Yellow Thearch."
translations.idiomatic: "Eighteen days after autumn's establishment welcome the Yellow Spirit at the central ground and sacrifice to the Yellow Thearch."

sentences.zh: 秋、冬各于其方。

translations.literal: "Autumn and winter each at its direction."
translations.idiomatic: "Autumn and winter, each at its proper quarter."

sentences.zh: 黃帝於五行為土，王在四季，土生於火，用事於木，而祭於秋，三季則否。

translations.literal: "The Yellow Thearch in the Five Phases is earth; earth's king is in the four seasons; earth is born from fire and acts through wood—yet sacrifice is in autumn; three seasons are not so."
translations.idiomatic: "The Yellow Thearch is earth among the Five Phases; earth's king is the four seasons; earth is born from fire and acts through wood—yet sacrifice falls in autumn; three seasons are not so."

sentences.zh: 漢、魏、周、隋，共行此禮。

translations.literal: "Han, Wei, Zhou, and Sui all practiced this rite."
translations.idiomatic: "Han, Wei, Zhou, and Sui all kept this rite."

sentences.zh: 國家土德乘時，亦以每歲六月土王之日，祀黃帝於南郊，以後土配，合於典禮。

translations.literal: "Our state, riding earth virtue's season, also each year on the earth-king day of the sixth month sacrifices to the Yellow Thearch at the southern suburb with Queen Earth paired—accordant with the canon."
translations.idiomatic: "Our state, riding earth virtue, also each sixth month on the earth-king day sacrifices to the Yellow Thearch at the southern suburb with Queen Earth paired—accordant with canon."

sentences.zh: 彭祖憑候緯之說，據陰陽之書，事涉不經，恐難行用。

translations.literal: "Pengzu relies on apocryphal prognostication and yin-yang books—the affair is uncanonical; I fear it will be hard to put into practice."
translations.idiomatic: "Pengzu relies on apocrypha and yin-yang books—uncanonical; I fear it will be hard to practice."

sentences.zh: 」乃寢。

translations.literal: " Thereupon it was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: " Shelved.

sentences.zh: 元和十五年十二月，將有事於南郊。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fifteenth year of Yuanhe, they were about to have an affair at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhe year 15, twelfth month: they were about to sacrifice at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 穆宗問禮官：「南郊卜日否？

translations.literal: Muzong asked the ritual officials: "Has the southern suburb day been divined?"
translations.idiomatic: Muzong asked ritual officials: "Has the southern suburb day been divined?"

sentences.zh: 」禮院奏：「伏准禮令，祠祭皆卜。

translations.literal: " The Rites Office memorialized: "I consider that per ritual statutes, all temple sacrifices are divined."
translations.idiomatic: " The Rites Office memorialized: "Per ritual statutes, all temple sacrifices are divined."

sentences.zh: 自天寶已後，凡欲郊祀，必先朝太清宮，次日饗太廟，又次日祀南郊。

translations.literal: "From after Tianbao, whenever they wished suburban sacrifice, they first attended the Grand Pure Palace, the next day feasted at the Grand Temple, and the day after sacrificed at the southern suburb."
translations.idiomatic: "From after Tianbao, before suburban sacrifice they first attended the Grand Pure Palace, next day feasted at the Grand Temple, day after sacrificed at the southern suburb."

sentences.zh: 相循至今，並不卜日。

translations.literal: "This has continued to the present—days are not divined."
translations.idiomatic: "This continues to the present—days are not divined."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " Approved.

sentences.zh: 及明年正月，南郊禮畢，有司不設禦榻，上立受群臣慶賀。

translations.literal: By the first month of the following year, when the southern suburb rite was complete, the relevant offices did not set the imperial couch; the emperor stood to receive the hundred officials' congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: First month of the following year, southern suburb complete: relevant offices set no imperial couch; the emperor stood to receive officials' congratulations.

sentences.zh: 及禦樓仗退，百僚復不于樓前賀，乃受賀于興慶宮。

translations.literal: When the imperial tower guard withdrew, the hundred officials again did not congratulate before the tower but received congratulations at Xingqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the tower guard withdrew, officials again did not congratulate before the tower but at Xingqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 二者闕禮，有司之過也。

translations.literal: Both were lapses of ritual—the fault of the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: Both were breaches of ritual—and the fault lay with the officers charged.
